verses.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth as formless and empty. Darkness as on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit as hovering over the surface of the aters.
God said, “ Let there be light,” and there as light.
God sa the light, and sa that it as good. God divided the light from the darkness.
God called the light “ day”, and the darkness he called “ night”. There as evening and there as morning, the first day.
God said, “ Let there be an expanse in the middle of the aters, and let it divide the aters from the aters.”
God made the expanse, and divided the aters hich ere under the expanse from the aters hich ere above the expanse; and it as so.
God called the expanse “ sky”. There as evening and there as morning, a second day.
God said, “ Let the aters under the sky be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear;” and it as so.
God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the aters he called “ seas”. God sa that it as good.
God said, “ Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, ith their seeds in it, on the earth;” and it as so.
The earth yielded grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, ith their seeds in it, after their kind; and God sa that it as good.
There as evening and there as morning, a third day.
God said, “ Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;
and let them be for lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth;” and it as so.
God made the to great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
God set them in the expanse of the sky to give light to the earth,
and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. God sa that it as good.
There as evening and there as morning, a fourth day.
God said, “ Let the aters abound ith living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”
God created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves, ith hich the aters sarmed, after their kind, and every inged bird after its kind. God sa that it as good.
God blessed them, saying, “ Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the aters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
There as evening and there as morning, a fifth day.
God said, “ Let the earth produce living creatures after their kind, livestock, creeping things, and animals of the earth after their kind;” and it as so.
God made the animals of the earth after their kind, and the livestock after their kind, and everything that creeps on the ground after its kind. God sa that it as good.

God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
God created man in his on image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

God blessed them. God said to them, “ Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
God said, “ Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, hich is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, hich bears fruit yielding seed. It ill be your food.
To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in hich there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it as so.
God sa everything that he had made, and, behold, it as very good. There as evening and there as morning, a sixth day.
The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array ere finished.
On the seventh day God finished his ork hich he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his ork hich he had done.
God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his ork of creation hich he had done.
This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth hen they ere created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
No plant of the field as yet on the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There as not a man to till the ground,
but a mist ent up from the earth, and atered the hole surface of the ground.
The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
The LORD God planted a garden eastard, in Eden, and there he put the man hom he had formed.

Out of the ground the LORD God made every tree to gro that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knoledge of good and evil.
A river ent out of Eden to ater the garden; and from there it as parted, and became the source of four rivers.
The name of the first is Pishon: it flos through the hole land of Havilah, here there is gold;
and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are also there.
The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the same river that flos through the hole land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Hiddekel. This is the one hich flos in front of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
The LORD God commanded the man, saying, “ You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;
but you shall not eat of the tree of the knoledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you ill surely die.”
The LORD God said, “ It is not good for the man to be alone. I ill make him a helper comparable to him.”

Out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see hat he ould call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.
The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there as not found a helper comparable to him.
The LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
The LORD God made a oman from the rib hich he had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.
The man said, “ This is no bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She ill be called ’oman,’ because she as taken out of Man.”
Therefore a man ill leave his father and his mother, and ill join ith his ife, and they ill be one flesh.
The man and his ife ere both naked, and they ere not ashamed.
No the serpent as more subtle than any animal of the field hich the LORD God had made. He said to the oman, “ Has God really said, ’ You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
The oman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
but not the fruit of the tree hich is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ’ You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’”
The serpent said to the oman, “ You on’t really die,
for God knos that in the day you eat it, your eyes ill be opened, and you ill be like God, knoing good and evil.”

When the oman sa that the tree as good for food, and that it as a delight to the eyes, and that the tree as to be desired to make one ise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband ith her, and he ate it, too.
Their eyes ere opened, and they both kne that they ere naked. They seed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.
They heard the LORD God’s voice alking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his ife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
The man said, “ I heard your voice in the garden, and I as afraid, because I as naked; so I hid myself.”
God said, “ Who told you that you ere naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”
The man said, “ The oman hom you gave to be ith me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
The LORD God said to the oman, “ What have you done?” The oman said, “ The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

The LORD God said to the serpent, “ Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.
I ill put hostility beteen you and the oman, and beteen your offspring and her offspring. He ill bruise your head, and you ill bruise his heel.”
To the oman he said, “ I ill greatly multiply your pain in childbirth. You ill bear children in pain. Your desire ill be for your husband, and he ill rule over you.”

To Adam he said, “ Because you have listened to your ife’s voice, and have eaten from the tree, about hich I commanded you, saying, ’ You shall not eat of it,’ the ground is cursed for your sake. You ill eat from it ith much labor all the days of your life.
It ill yield thorns and thistles to you; and you ill eat the herb of the field.
You ill eat bread by the seat of your face until you return to the ground, for you ere taken out of it. For you are dust, and you shall return to dust.”
The man called his ife Eve because she ould be the mother of all the living.
The LORD God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his ife, and clothed them.
The LORD God said, “ Behold, the man has become like one of us, knoing good and evil. No, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—”
Therefore the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from hich he as taken.
So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sord hich turned every ay, to guard the ay to the tree of life.
The man kne Eve his ife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said, “ I have gotten a man ith the LORD’s help.”
Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel as a keeper of sheep, but Cain as a tiller of the ground.
As time passed, Cain brought an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.
Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. The LORD respected Abel and his offering,
but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain as very angry, and the expression on his face fell.
The LORD said to Cain, “ Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?
If you do ell, on’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do ell, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”
Cain said to Abel, his brother, “ Let’s go into the field.” While they ere in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.
The LORD said to Cain, “ Where is Abel, your brother?” He said, “ I don’t kno. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
The LORD said, “ What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.
No you are cursed because of the ground, hich has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
From no on, hen you till the ground, it on’t yield its strength to you. You ill be a fugitive and a anderer on the earth.”
Cain said to the LORD, “ My punishment is greater than I can bear.
Behold, you have driven me out today from the surface of the ground. I ill be hidden from your face, and I ill be a fugitive and a anderer on the earth. Whoever finds me ill kill me.”
The LORD said to him, “ Therefore hoever slays Cain, vengeance ill be taken on him sevenfold.” The LORD appointed a sign for Cain, so that anyone finding him ould not strike him.
Cain left the LORD’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Cain kne his ife. She conceived, and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city, and named the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
Irad as born to Enoch. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.
Lamech took to ives: the name of the first one as Adah, and the name of the second one as Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal, ho as the father of those ho dell in tents and have livestock.
His brother’s name as Jubal, ho as the father of all ho handle the harp and pipe.
Zillah also gave birth to Tubal Cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron. Tubal Cain’s sister as Naamah.
Lamech said to his ives, “ Adah and Zillah, hear my voice. You ives of Lamech, listen to my speech, for I have slain a man for ounding me, a young man for bruising me.
If Cain ill be avenged seven times, truly Lamech seventy-seven times.”
Adam kne his ife again. She gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, saying, “ for God has given me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.”
A son as also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on the LORD’s name.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him in God’s likeness.
He created them male and female, and blessed them. On the day they ere created, he named them Adam.
Adam lived one hundred thirty years, and became the father of a son in his on likeness, after his image, and named him Seth.
The days of Adam after he became the father of Seth ere eight hundred years, and he became the father of other sons and daughters.
All the days that Adam lived ere nine hundred thirty years, then he died.
Seth lived one hundred five years, then became the father of Enosh.
Seth lived after he became the father of Enosh eight hundred seven years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Seth ere nine hundred telve years, then he died.
Enosh lived ninety years, and became the father of Kenan.
Enosh lived after he became the father of Kenan eight hundred fifteen years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Enosh ere nine hundred five years, then he died.
Kenan lived seventy years, then became the father of Mahalalel.
Kenan lived after he became the father of Mahalalel eight hundred forty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters
and all of the days of Kenan ere nine hundred ten years, then he died.
Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Jared.
Mahalalel lived after he became the father of Jared eight hundred thirty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Mahalalel ere eight hundred ninety-five years, then he died.
Jared lived one hundred sixty-to years, then became the father of Enoch.
Jared lived after he became the father of Enoch eight hundred years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Jared ere nine hundred sixty-to years, then he died.
Enoch lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Methuselah.
After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch alked ith God for three hundred years, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
All the days of Enoch ere three hundred sixty-five years.
Enoch alked ith God, and he as not found, for God took him.
Methuselah lived one hundred eighty-seven years, then became the father of Lamech.
Methuselah lived after he became the father of Lamech seven hundred eighty-to years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All the days of Methuselah ere nine hundred sixty-nine years, then he died.
Lamech lived one hundred eighty-to years, then became the father of a son.
He named him Noah, saying, “ This one ill comfort us in our ork and in the toil of our hands, caused by the ground hich the LORD has cursed.”
Lamech lived after he became the father of Noah five hundred ninety-five years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All the days of Lamech ere seven hundred seventy-seven years, then he died.
Noah as five hundred years old, then Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters ere born to them,
God’s sons sa that men’s daughters ere beautiful, and they took any that they anted for themselves as ives.
The LORD said, “ My Spirit ill not strive ith man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days ill be one hundred tenty years.”
The Nephilim ere on the earth in those days, and also after that, hen God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children ith them. Those ere the mighty men ho ere of old, men of renon.
The LORD sa that the ickedness of man as great on the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart as continually only evil.
The LORD as sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
The LORD said, “ I ill destroy man hom I have created from the surface of the ground— man, along ith animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky— for I am sorry that I have made them.”
But Noah found favor in the LORD’s eyes.
This is the history of the generations of Noah: Noah as a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah alked ith God.
Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth as corrupt before God, and the earth as filled ith violence.
God sa the earth, and sa that it as corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their ay on the earth.
God said to Noah, “ I ill bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled ith violence through them. Behold, I ill destroy them and the earth.
Make a ship of gopher ood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside ith pitch.
This is ho you shall make it. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits, its idth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
You shall make a roof in the ship, and you shall finish it to a cubit upard. You shall set the door of the ship in its side. You shall make it ith loer, second, and third levels.
I, even I, ill bring the flood of aters on this earth, to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky. Everything that is on the earth ill die.
But I ill establish my covenant ith you. You shall come into the ship, you, your sons, your ife, and your sons’ ives ith you.
Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring to of every sort into the ship, to keep them alive ith you. They shall be male and female.
Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, to of every sort ill come to you, to keep them alive.
Take ith you some of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it ill be for food for you, and for them.”
Thus Noah did. He did all that God commanded him.
The LORD said to Noah, “Come ith all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.
You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal ith you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take to, the male and his female.
Also of the birds of the sky, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive on the surface of all the earth.
In seven days, I ill cause it to rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I ill destroy every living thing that I have made from the surface of the ground.”
Noah did everything that the LORD commanded him.
Noah as six hundred years old hen the flood of aters came on the earth.
Noah ent into the ship ith his sons, his ife, and his sons’ ives, because of the floodaters.
Clean animals, unclean animals, birds, and everything that creeps on the ground
ent by pairs to Noah into the ship, male and female, as God commanded Noah.
After the seven days, the floodaters came on the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the sky’s indos opened.
It rained on the earth forty days and forty nights.
In the same day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth— the sons of Noah— and Noah’s ife and the three ives of his sons ith them, entered into the ship—
they, and every animal after its kind, all the livestock after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
Pairs from all flesh ith the breath of life in them ent into the ship to Noah.
Those ho ent in, ent in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him; then the LORD shut him in.
The flood as forty days on the earth. The aters increased, and lifted up the ship, and it as lifted up above the earth.
The aters rose, and increased greatly on the earth; and the ship floated on the surface of the aters.
The aters rose very high on the earth. All the high mountains that ere under the hole sky ere covered.
The aters rose fifteen cubits higher, and the mountains ere covered.
All flesh died that moved on the earth, including birds, livestock, animals, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and every man.
All on the dry land, in hose nostrils as the breath of the spirit of life, died.

Every living thing as destroyed that as on the surface of the ground, including man, livestock, creeping things, and birds of the sky. They ere destroyed from the earth. Only Noah as left, and those ho ere ith him in the ship.
The aters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days.
God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that ere ith him in the ship; and God made a ind to pass over the earth. The aters subsided.
The deep’s fountains and the sky’s indos ere also stopped, and the rain from the sky as restrained.
The aters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred fifty days the aters receded.
The ship rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on Ararat’s mountains.
The aters receded continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains ere visible.
At the end of forty days, Noah opened the indo of the ship hich he had made,
and he sent out a raven. It ent back and forth, until the aters ere dried up from the earth.
He himself sent out a dove to see if the aters ere abated from the surface of the ground,

but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned into the ship to him, for the aters ere on the surface of the hole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.
He aited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship.
The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth as a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah kne that the aters ere abated from the earth.
He aited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she didn’t return to him any more.

In the six hundred first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the aters ere dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He sa that the surface of the ground as dry.
In the second month, on the tenty-seventh day of the month, the earth as dry.
God spoke to Noah, saying,
“ Go out of the ship, you, your ife, your sons, and your sons’ ives ith you.

Bring out ith you every living thing that is ith you of all flesh, including birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, that they may breed abundantly on the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.”
Noah ent out, ith his sons, his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him.
Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird, hatever moves on the earth, after their families, ent out of the ship.
Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean animal, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

The LORD smelled the pleasant aroma. The LORD said in his heart, “ I ill not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I ill never again strike every living thing, as I have done.
While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and inter, and day and night ill not cease.”
God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “ Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.

The fear of you and the dread of you ill be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that moves along the ground, and all the fish of the sea, are delivered into your hand.
Every moving thing that lives ill be food for you. As I gave you the green herb, I have given everything to you.
But flesh ith its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.
I ill surely require accounting for your life’s blood. At the hand of every animal I ill require it. At the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, I ill require the life of man.
Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood ill be shed by man, for God made man in his on image.
Be fruitful and multiply. Increase abundantly on the earth, and multiply in it.”
God spoke to Noah and to his sons ith him, saying,
“ As for me, behold, I establish my covenant ith you, and ith your offspring after you,
and ith every living creature that is ith you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth ith you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth.
I ill establish my covenant ith you: All flesh ill not be cut off any more by the aters of the flood. There ill never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
God said, “ This is the token of the covenant hich I make beteen me and you and every living creature that is ith you, for perpetual generations:
I set my rainbo in the cloud, and it ill be a sign of a covenant beteen me and the earth.
When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbo ill be seen in the cloud,
I ill remember my covenant, hich is beteen me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the aters ill no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
The rainbo ill be in the cloud. I ill look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant beteen God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
God said to Noah, “ This is the token of the covenant hich I have established beteen me and all flesh that is on the earth.”
The sons of Noah ho ent out from the ship ere Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.
These three ere the sons of Noah, and from these the hole earth as populated.
Noah began to be a farmer, and planted a vineyard.
He drank of the ine and got drunk. He as uncovered ithin his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, sa the nakedness of his father, and told his to brothers outside.

Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it on both their shoulders, ent in backards, and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces ere backards, and they didn’t see their father’s nakedness.
Noah aoke from his ine, and kne hat his youngest son had done to him.
He said, “ Canaan is cursed. He ill be a servant of servants to his brothers.”
He said, “ Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.
May God enlarge Japheth. Let him dell in the tents of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.”
Noah lived three hundred fifty years after the flood.
All the days of Noah ere nine hundred fifty years, and then he died.
No this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons ere born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth ere: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer ere: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan ere: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Of these ere the islands of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in their nations.
The sons of Ham ere: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush ere: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah ere: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one on the earth.
He as a mighty hunter before the LORD. Therefore it is said, “ like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD”.
The beginning of his kingdom as Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
Out of that land he ent into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah,
and Resen beteen Nineveh and the great city Calah.
Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim ( hich the Philistines descended from), and Caphtorim.
Canaan became the father of Sidon ( his firstborn), Heth,
the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterard the families of the Canaanites ere spread abroad.
The border of the Canaanites as from Sidon— as you go toard Gerar— to Gaza— as you go toard Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim— to Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, after their families, according to their languages, in their lands and their nations.
Children ere also born to Shem ( the elder brother of Japheth), the father of all the children of Eber.
The sons of Shem ere: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram ere: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.
To Eber ere born to sons. The name of the one as Peleg, for in his days the earth as divided. His brother’s name as Joktan.
Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these ere the sons of Joktan.
Their delling extended from Mesha, as you go toard Sephar, the mountain of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, by their families, according to their languages, lands, and nations.
