Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “ What have you done to us? Ho have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done!”
Abimelech said to Abraham, “ What did you see, that you have done this thing?”
Abraham said, “ Because I thought, ’ Surely the fear of God is not in this place. They ill kill me for my ife’s sake.’
Besides, she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my ife.
When God caused me to ander from my father’s house, I said to her, ’ This is your kindness hich you shall sho to me. Everyhere that e go, say of me, “ He is my brother.”’”
Abimelech took sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored Sarah, his ife, to him.
Abimelech said, “ Behold, my land is before you. Dell here it pleases you.”
To Sarah he said, “ Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. Behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes to all that are ith you. In front of all you are vindicated.”
Abraham prayed to God. So God healed Abimelech, his ife, and his female servants, and they bore children.
For the LORD had closed up tight all the ombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s ife.
The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as he had spoken.
Sarah conceived, and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of hich God had spoken to him.
Abraham called his son ho as born to him, hom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
Abraham circumcised his son, Isaac, hen he as eight days old, as God had commanded him.
Abraham as one hundred years old hen his son, Isaac, as born to him.
Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. Everyone ho hears ill laugh ith me.”
She said, “ Who ould have said to Abraham that Sarah ould nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
The child gre and as eaned. Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac as eaned.
Sarah sa the son of Hagar the Egyptian, hom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
Therefore she said to Abraham, “ Cast out this servant and her son! For the son of this servant ill not be heir ith my son, Isaac.”
The thing as very grievous in Abraham’s sight on account of his son.

God said to Abraham, “Don’t let it be grievous in your sight because of the boy, and because of your servant. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice. For your offspring ill be named through Isaac.
I ill also make a nation of the son of the servant, because he is your child.”

Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a container of ater, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder; and gave her the child, and sent her aay. She departed, and andered in the ilderness of Beersheba.
The ater in the container as spent, and she put the child under one of the shrubs.
She ent and sat don opposite him, a good ay off, about a bo shot aay. For she said, “Don’t let me see the death of the child.” She sat opposite him, and lifted up her voice, and ept.
God heard the voice of the boy. The angel of God called to Hagar out of the sky, and said to her, “ What troubles you, Hagar? Don’t be afraid. For God has heard the voice of the boy here he is.
Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him ith your hand. For I ill make him a great nation.”
God opened her eyes, and she sa a ell of ater. She ent, filled the container ith ater, and gave the boy a drink.
God as ith the boy, and he gre. He lived in the ilderness, and as he gre up, he became an archer.
He lived in the ilderness of Paran. His mother got a ife for him out of the land of Egypt.
At that time, Abimelech and Phicol the captain of his army spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is ith you in all that you do.

No, therefore, sear to me here by God that you ill not deal falsely ith me, nor ith my son, nor ith my son’s son. But according to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the land in hich you have lived as a foreigner.”
Abraham said, “ I ill sear.”
Abraham complained to Abimelech because of a ater ell, hich Abimelech’s servants had violently taken aay.
Abimelech said, “ I don’t kno ho has done this thing. You didn’t tell me, and I didn’t hear of it until today.”
Abraham took sheep and cattle, and gave them to Abimelech. Those to made a covenant.
Abraham set seven ee lambs of the flock by themselves.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “ What do these seven ee lambs, hich you have set by themselves, mean?”
He said, “ You shall take these seven ee lambs from my hand, that it may be a itness to me, that I have dug this ell.”
Therefore he called that place Beersheba, because they both sore an oath there.
So they made a covenant at Beersheba. Abimelech rose up ith Phicol, the captain of his army, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines many days.
After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “ Here I am.”
He said, “ No take your son, your only son, Isaac, hom you love, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains hich I ill tell you of.”

Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey; and took to of his young men ith him, and Isaac his son. He split the ood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and ent to the place of hich God had told him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and sa the place far off.
Abraham said to his young men, “ Stay here ith the donkey. The boy and I ill go over there. We ill orship, and come back to you.”
Abraham took the ood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both ent together.
Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “ Here I am, my son.” He said, “ Here is the fire and the ood, but here is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
Abraham said, “God ill provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both ent together.
They came to the place hich God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the ood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the ood.
Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.
The LORD’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “ Here I am.”
He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For no I kno that you fear God, since you have not ithheld your son, your only son, from me.”
Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and sa that behind him as a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham ent and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
Abraham called the name of that place “ The LORD Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “ On the LORD’s mountain, it ill be provided.”
The LORD’s angel called to Abraham a second time out of the sky,
and said, “’ I have sorn by myself,’ says the LORD, ’ because you have done this thing, and have not ithheld your son, your only son,
that I ill bless you greatly, and I ill multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand hich is on the seashore. Your offspring ill possess the gate of his enemies.
All the nations of the earth ill be blessed by your offspring, because you have obeyed my voice.’”
So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and ent together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
After these things, Abraham as told, “ Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
His concubine, hose name as Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived one hundred tenty-seven years. This as the length of Sarah’s life.
Sarah died in Kiriath Arba ( also called Hebron), in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to eep for her.
Abraham rose up from before his dead and spoke to the children of Heth, saying,
“ I am a stranger and a foreigner living ith you. Give me a possession of a burying-place ith you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
The children of Heth ansered Abraham, saying to him,
“ Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us ill ithhold from you his tomb. Bury your dead.”
Abraham rose up, and boed himself to the people of the land, to the children of Heth.
He talked ith them, saying, “ If you agree that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
that he may sell me the cave of Machpelah, hich he has, hich is in the end of his field. For the full price let him sell it to me among you as a possession for a burial place.”
No Ephron as sitting in the middle of the children of Heth. Ephron the Hittite ansered Abraham in the hearing of the children of Heth, even of all ho ent in at the gate of his city, saying,
“ No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of the children of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
Abraham boed himself don before the people of the land.
He spoke to Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, “ But if you ill, please hear me. I ill give the price of the field. Take it from me, and I ill bury my dead there.”
Ephron ansered Abraham, saying to him,
“ My lord, listen to me. What is a piece of land orth four hundred shekels of silver beteen me and you? Therefore bury your dead.”
Abraham listened to Ephron. Abraham eighed to Ephron the silver hich he had named in the hearing of the children of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, according to the current merchants’ standard.
So the field of Ephron, hich as in Machpelah, hich as before Mamre, the field, the cave hich as in it, and all the trees that ere in the field, that ere in all of its borders, ere deeded
to Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all ho ent in at the gate of his city.
After this, Abraham buried Sarah his ife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre ( that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
The field, and the cave that is in it, ere deeded to Abraham by the children of Heth as a possession for a burial place.
Abraham as old, and ell advanced in age. The LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, ho ruled over all that he had, “ Please put your hand under my thigh.
I ill make you sear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a ife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among hom I live.
But you shall go to my country, and to my relatives, and take a ife for my son Isaac.”
The servant said to him, “ What if the oman isn’t illing to follo me to this land? Must I bring your son again to the land you came from?”
Abraham said to him, “ Beare that you don’t bring my son there again.

The LORD, the God of heaven— ho took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, ho spoke to me, and ho sore to me, saying, ’ I ill give this land to your offspring— he ill send his angel before you, and you shall take a ife for my son from there.
If the oman isn’t illing to follo you, then you shall be clear from this oath to me. Only you shall not bring my son there again.”
The servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sore to him concerning this matter.
The servant took ten of his master’s camels, and departed, having a variety of good things of his master’s ith him. He arose, and ent to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel don outside the city by the ell of ater at the time of evening, the time that omen go out to dra ater.
He said, “ LORD, the God of my master Abraham, please give me success today, and sho kindness to my master Abraham.
Behold, I am standing by the spring of ater. The daughters of the men of the city are coming out to dra ater.

Let it happen, that the young lady to hom I ill say, ’ Please let don your pitcher, that I may drink,’ then she says, ’ Drink, and I ill also give your camels a drink,’— let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I ill kno that you have shon kindness to my master.”
Before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, ho as born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the ife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, ith her pitcher on her shoulder.
The young lady as very beautiful to look at, a virgin. No man had knon her. She ent don to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
The servant ran to meet her, and said, “ Please give me a drink, a little ater from your pitcher.”
She said, “ Drink, my lord.” She hurried, and let don her pitcher on her hand, and gave him a drink.
When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “ I ill also dra for your camels, until they have finished drinking.”
She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the ell to dra, and dre for all his camels.
The man looked steadfastly at her, remaining silent, to kno hether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
As the camels had finished drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel eight, and to bracelets for her hands of ten shekels eight of gold,
and said, “ Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to stay?”
She said to him, “ I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, hom she bore to Nahor.”
She said moreover to him, “We have both stra and feed enough, and room to lodge in.”
The man boed his head, and orshiped the LORD.

He said, “ Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, ho has not forsaken his loving kindness and his truth toard my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the ay to the house of my master’s relatives.”
The young lady ran, and told her mother’s house about these ords.
Rebekah had a brother, and his name as Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.

When he sa the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and hen he heard the ords of Rebekah his sister, saying, “ This is hat the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he as standing by the camels at the spring.
He said, “Come in, you blessed of the LORD. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. He gave stra and feed for the camels, and ater to ash his feet and the feet of the men ho ere ith him.
Food as set before him to eat, but he said, “ I ill not eat until I have told my message.” Laban said, “ Speak on.”
He said, “ I am Abraham’s servant.
The LORD has blessed my master greatly. He has become great. The LORD has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
Sarah, my master’s ife, bore a son to my master hen she as old. He has given all that he has to him.
My master made me sear, saying, ’ You shall not take a ife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in hose land I live,
but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my relatives, and take a ife for my son.’
I asked my master, ’What if the oman ill not follo me?’
He said to me, ’ The LORD, before hom I alk, ill send his angel ith you, and prosper your ay. You shall take a ife for my son from my relatives, and of my father’s house.
Then you ill be clear from my oath, hen you come to my relatives. If they don’t give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
I came today to the spring, and said, ’ The LORD, the God of my master Abraham, if no you do prosper my ay hich I go—
behold, I am standing by this spring of ater. Let it happen, that the maiden ho comes out to dra, to hom I ill say, “ Please give me a little ater from your pitcher to drink,”
then she tells me, “ Drink, and I ill also dra for your camels,”—let her be the oman hom the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.’
Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out ith her pitcher on her shoulder. She ent don to the spring, and dre. I said to her, ’ Please let me drink.’
She hurried and let don her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ’ Drink, and I ill also give your camels a drink.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
I asked her, and said, ’ Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ’ The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, hom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
I boed my head, and orshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, ho had led me in the right ay to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
No if you ill deal kindly and truly ith my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.”
Then Laban and Bethuel ansered, “ The thing proceeds from the LORD. We can’t speak to you bad or good.
Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s ife, as the LORD has spoken.”
When Abraham’s servant heard their ords, he boed himself don to the earth to the LORD.
The servant brought out jeels of silver, and jeels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.
They ate and drank, he and the men ho ere ith him, and stayed all night. They rose up in the morning, and he said, “ Send me aay to my master.”
Her brother and her mother said, “ Let the young lady stay ith us a fe days, at least ten. After that she ill go.”
He said to them, “Don’t hinder me, since the LORD has prospered my ay. Send me aay that I may go to my master.”
They said, “We ill call the young lady, and ask her.”
They called Rebekah, and said to her, “ Will you go ith this man?” She said, “ I ill go.”
They sent aay Rebekah, their sister, ith her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men.
They blessed Rebekah, and said to her, “ Our sister, may you be the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your offspring possess the gate of those ho hate them.”
Rebekah arose ith her ladies. They rode on the camels, and folloed the man. The servant took Rebekah, and ent his ay.
Isaac came from the ay of Beer Lahai Roi, for he lived in the land of the South.
Isaac ent out to meditate in the field at the evening. He lifted up his eyes and looked. Behold, there ere camels coming.
Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and hen she sa Isaac, she got off the camel.
She said to the servant, “ Who is the man ho is alking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “ It is my master.” She took her veil, and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his ife. He loved her. So Isaac as comforted after his mother’s death.
Abraham took another ife, and her name as Keturah.
She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan became the father of Sheba, and Dedan. The sons of Dedan ere Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
The sons of Midian ere Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these ere the children of Keturah.
Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac,
but Abraham gave gifts to the sons of Abraham’s concubines. While he still lived, he sent them aay from Isaac his son, eastard, to the east country.
These are the days of the years of Abraham’s life hich he lived: one hundred seventy-five years.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and as gathered to his people.
Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron, the son of Zohar the Hittite, hich is near Mamre,
the field hich Abraham purchased from the children of Heth. Abraham as buried there ith Sarah, his ife.
After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac, his son. Isaac lived by Beer Lahai Roi.
No this is the history of the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, hom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.
These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to the order of their birth: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments: telve princes, according to their nations.
These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He gave up his spirit and died, and as gathered to his people.
They lived from Havilah to Shur that is before Egypt, as you go toard Assyria. He lived opposite all his relatives.
This is the history of the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham became the father of Isaac.
Isaac as forty years old hen he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his ife.
Isaac entreated the LORD for his ife, because she as barren. The LORD as entreated by him, and Rebekah his ife conceived.
The children struggled together ithin her. She said, “ If it is like this, hy do I live?” She ent to inquire of the LORD.
The LORD said to her, “ To nations are in your omb. To peoples ill be separated from your body. The one people ill be stronger than the other people. The elder ill serve the younger.”
When her days to be delivered ere fulfilled, behold, there ere tins in her omb.
The first came out red all over, like a hairy garment. They named him Esau.
After that, his brother came out, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel. He as named Jacob. Isaac as sixty years old hen she bore them.
The boys gre. Esau as a skillful hunter, a man of the field. Jacob as a quiet man, living in tents.
No Isaac loved Esau, because he ate his venison. Rebekah loved Jacob.
Jacob boiled ste. Esau came in from the field, and he as famished.
Esau said to Jacob, “ Please feed me ith some of that red ste, for I am famished.” Therefore his name as called Edom.
Jacob said, “ First, sell me your birthright.”
Esau said, “ Behold, I am about to die. What good is the birthright to me?”
Jacob said, “ Sear to me first.” He sore to him. He sold his birthright to Jacob.
Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil ste. He ate and drank, rose up, and ent his ay. So Esau despised his birthright.
There as a famine in the land, in addition to the first famine that as in the days of Abraham. Isaac ent to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
The LORD appeared to him, and said, “Don’t go don into Egypt. Live in the land I ill tell you about.
Live in this land, and I ill be ith you, and ill bless you. For I ill give to you, and to your offspring, all these lands, and I ill establish the oath hich I sore to Abraham your father.
I ill multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky, and ill give all these lands to your offspring. In your offspring all the nations of the earth ill be blessed,
because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my requirements, my commandments, my statutes, and my las.”
Isaac lived in Gerar.

The men of the place asked him about his ife. He said, “ She is my sister,” for he as afraid to say, “ My ife”, lest, he thought, “ the men of the place might kill me for Rebekah, because she is beautiful to look at.”
When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a indo, and sa, and, behold, Isaac as caressing Rebekah, his ife.
Abimelech called Isaac, and said, “ Behold, surely she is your ife. Why did you say, ’ She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “ Because I said, ’ Lest I die because of her.’”
Abimelech said, “ What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain ith your ife, and you ould have brought guilt on us!”
Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, “ He ho touches this man or his ife ill surely be put to death.”
Isaac soed in that land, and reaped in the same year one hundred times hat he planted. The LORD blessed him.
The man gre great, and gre more and more until he became very great.
He had possessions of flocks, possessions of herds, and a great household. The Philistines envied him.
No all the ells hich his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped, and filled ith earth.
Abimelech said to Isaac, “ Go aay from us, for you are much mightier than e.”
Isaac departed from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and lived there.

Isaac dug again the ells of ater, hich they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham. He called their names after the names by hich his father had called them.
Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, and found there a ell of floing ater.
The herdsmen of Gerar argued ith Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “ The ater is ours.” So he called the name of the ell Esek, because they contended ith him.
They dug another ell, and they argued over that, also. So he called its name Sitnah.
He left that place, and dug another ell. They didn’t argue over that one. So he called it Rehoboth. He said, “ For no the LORD has made room for us, and e ill be fruitful in the land.”
He ent up from there to Beersheba.

The LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, “ I am the God of Abraham your father. Don’t be afraid, for I am ith you, and ill bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
He built an altar there, and called on the LORD’s name, and pitched his tent there. There Isaac’s servants dug a ell.
Then Abimelech ent to him from Gerar ith Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol the captain of his army.
Isaac said to them, “ Why have you come to me, since you hate me, and have sent me aay from you?”
They said, “ We sa plainly that the LORD as ith you. We said, ’ Let there no be an oath beteen us, even beteen us and you, and let’s make a covenant ith you,
that you ill do us no harm, as e have not touched you, and as e have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you aay in peace.’ You are no the blessed of the LORD.”
He made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
They rose up some time in the morning, and sore an oath to one another. Isaac sent them aay, and they departed from him in peace.
The same day, Isaac’s servants came, and told him concerning the ell hich they had dug, and said to him, “ We have found ater.”
He called it “ Shibah”. Therefore the name of the city is “Beersheba” to this day.
When Esau as forty years old, he took as ife Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
They grieved Isaac’s and Rebekah’s spirits.
When Isaac as old, and his eyes ere dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said to him, “ My son?” He said to him, “ Here I am.”
He said, “ See no, I am old. I don’t kno the day of my death.
No therefore, please take your eapons, your quiver and your bo, and go out to the field, and get me venison.
Make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”
Rebekah heard hen Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau ent to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, “ Behold, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,
’ Bring me venison, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless you before the LORD before my death.’
No therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that hich I command you.
Go no to the flock and get me to good young goats from there. I ill make them savory food for your father, such as he loves.
You shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”
Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “ Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
What if my father touches me? I ill seem to him as a deceiver, and I ould bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”
His mother said to him, “ Let your curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go get them for me.”
He ent, and got them, and brought them to his mother. His mother made savory food, such as his father loved.
Rebekah took the good clothes of Esau, her elder son, hich ere ith her in the house, and put them on Jacob, her younger son.
She put the skins of the young goats on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck.
She gave the savory food and the bread, hich she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
He came to his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “ Here I am. Who are you, my son?”
Jacob said to his father, “ I am Esau your firstborn. I have done hat you asked me to do. Please arise, sit and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me.”
Isaac said to his son, “ Ho is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He said, “ Because the LORD your God gave me success.”
Isaac said to Jacob, “ Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, hether you are really my son Esau or not.”
Jacob ent near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and said, “ The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
He didn’t recognize him, because his hands ere hairy, like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.
He said, “ Are you really my son Esau?” He said, “ I am.”
He said, “ Bring it near to me, and I ill eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless you.” He brought it near to him, and he ate. He brought him ine, and he drank.
His father Isaac said to him, “ Come near no, and kiss me, my son.”
He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and said, “ Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field hich the LORD has blessed.
God give you of the de of the sky, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and ne ine.
Let peoples serve you, and nations bo don to you. Be lord over your brothers. Let your mother’s sons bo don to you. Cursed be everyone ho curses you. Blessed be everyone ho blesses you.”
As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
He also made savory food, and brought it to his father. He said to his father, “ Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that your soul may bless me.”
Isaac his father said to him, “ Who are you?” He said, “ I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”
Isaac trembled violently, and said, “ Who, then, is he ho has taken venison, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, he ill be blessed.”
When Esau heard the ords of his father, he cried ith an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “ Bless me, even me also, my father.”
He said, “ Your brother came ith deceit, and has taken aay your blessing.”
He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these to times. He took aay my birthright. See, no he has taken aay my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”
Isaac ansered Esau, “ Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants. I have sustained him ith grain and ne ine. What then ill I do for you, my son?”
Esau said to his father, “Do you have just one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” Esau lifted up his voice, and ept.
Isaac his father ansered him, “ Behold, your delling ill be of the fatness of the earth, and of the de of the sky from above.
You ill live by your sord, and you ill serve your brother. It ill happen, hen you ill break loose, that you ill shake his yoke from off your neck.”
Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing ith hich his father blessed him. Esau said in his heart, “ The days of mourning for my father are at hand. Then I ill kill my brother Jacob.”
The ords of Esau, her elder son, ere told to Rebekah. She sent and called Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, “ Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself about you by planning to kill you.
No therefore, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.
Stay ith him a fe days, until your brother’s fury turns aay—
until your brother’s anger turns aay from you, and he forgets hat you have done to him. Then I ill send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”

Rebekah said to Isaac, “ I am eary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a ife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, hat good ill my life do me?”
Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him, “ You shall not take a ife of the daughters of Canaan.
Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father. Take a ife from there from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a company of peoples,
and give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring ith you, that you may inherit the land here you travel, hich God gave to Abraham.”
Isaac sent Jacob aay. He ent to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

No Esau sa that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him aay to Paddan Aram, to take him a ife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “ You shall not take a ife of the daughters of Canaan;”
and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and as gone to Paddan Aram.
Esau sa that the daughters of Canaan didn’t please Isaac, his father.
So Esau ent to Ishmael, and took, in addition to the ives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his ife.
Jacob ent out from Beersheba, and ent toard Haran.
He came to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay don in that place to sleep.
He dreamed and sa a stairay set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven. Behold, the angels of God ere ascending and descending on it.
Behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, “ I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I ill give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring.

Your offspring ill be as the dust of the earth, and you ill spread abroad to the est, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth ill be blessed.
Behold, I am ith you, and ill keep you, herever you go, and ill bring you again into this land. For I ill not leave you until I have done that hich I have spoken of to you.”
Jacob aakened out of his sleep, and he said, “ Surely the LORD is in this place, and I didn’t kno it.”
He as afraid, and said, “ Ho aesome this place is! This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city as Luz at the first.
Jacob voed a vo, saying, “ If God ill be ith me, and ill keep me in this ay that I go, and ill give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,
so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and the LORD ill be my God,
then this stone, hich I have set up for a pillar, ill be God’s house. Of all that you ill give me I ill surely give a tenth to you.”
Then Jacob ent on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
He looked, and sa a ell in the field, and sa three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that ell they atered the flocks. The stone on the ell’s mouth as large.
There all the flocks ere gathered. They rolled the stone from the ell’s mouth, and atered the sheep, and put the stone back on the ell’s mouth in its place.
Jacob said to them, “ My relatives, here are you from?” They said, “We are from Haran.”
He said to them, “Do you kno Laban, the son of Nahor?” They said, “We kno him.”
He said to them, “ Is it ell ith him?” They said, “ It is ell. See, Rachel, his daughter, is coming ith the sheep.”
He said, “ Behold, it is still the middle of the day, not time to gather the livestock together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.”
They said, “ We can’t, until all the flocks are gathered together, and they roll the stone from the ell’s mouth. Then e ill ater the sheep.”
While he as yet speaking ith them, Rachel came ith her father’s sheep, for she kept them.

When Jacob sa Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Jacob ent near, and rolled the stone from the ell’s mouth, and atered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and ept.
Jacob told Rachel that he as her father’s relative, and that he as Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.
When Laban heard the nes of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.” Jacob stayed ith him for a month.
Laban said to Jacob, “ Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, hat ill your ages be?”
Laban had to daughters. The name of the elder as Leah, and the name of the younger as Rachel.
Leah’s eyes ere eak, but Rachel as beautiful in form and attractive.
Jacob loved Rachel. He said, “ I ill serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.”
Laban said, “ It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man. Stay ith me.”
Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a fe days, for the love he had for her.
Jacob said to Laban, “ Give me my ife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
In the evening, he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to Jacob. He ent in to her.
Laban gave Zilpah his servant to his daughter Leah for a servant.
In the morning, behold, it as Leah! He said to Laban, “ What is this you have done to me? Didn’t I serve ith you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”
Laban said, “ It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
Fulfill the eek of this one, and e ill give you the other also for the service hich you ill serve ith me for seven more years.”
Jacob did so, and fulfilled her eek. He gave him Rachel his daughter as ife.
Laban gave Bilhah, his servant, to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.
He ent in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served ith him seven more years.
The LORD sa that Leah as hated, and he opened her omb, but Rachel as barren.
Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “ Because the LORD has looked at my affliction; for no my husband ill love me.”
She conceived again, and bore a son, and said, “ Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.
She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “ No this time my husband ill be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name as called Levi.
She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “ This time I ill praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
When Rachel sa that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. She said to Jacob, “ Give me children, or else I ill die.”
Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he said, “Am I in God’s place, ho has ithheld from you the fruit of the omb?”
She said, “ Behold, my maid Bilhah. Go in to her, that she may bear on my knees, and I also may obtain children by her.”
She gave him Bilhah her servant as ife, and Jacob ent in to her.
Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.
Rachel said, “ God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.
Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.
Rachel said, “ I have restled ith my sister ith mighty restlings, and have prevailed.” She named him Naphtali.
When Leah sa that she had finished bearing, she took Zilpah, her servant, and gave her to Jacob as a ife.
Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a son.
Leah said, “Ho fortunate!” She named him Gad.
Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a second son.
Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters ill call me happy.” She named him Asher.
Reuben ent in the days of heat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother, Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, “ Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

Leah said to her, “ Is it a small matter that you have taken aay my husband? Would you take aay my son’s mandrakes, also?” Rachel said, “ Therefore he ill lie ith you tonight for your son’s mandrakes.”
Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah ent out to meet him, and said, “ You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you ith my son’s mandrakes.” He lay ith her that night.
God listened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.
Leah said, “ God has given me my hire, because I gave my servant to my husband.” She named him Issachar.
Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
Leah said, “God has endoed me ith a good dory. No my husband ill live ith me, because I have borne him six sons.” She named him Zebulun.
Afterards, she bore a daughter, and named her Dinah.
God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her, and opened her omb.
She conceived, bore a son, and said, “God has taken aay my reproach.”
She named him Joseph, saying, “ May the LORD add another son to me.”
When Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “ Send me aay, that I may go to my on place, and to my country.
Give me my ives and my children for hom I have served you, and let me go; for you kno my service ith hich I have served you.”
Laban said to him, “ If no I have found favor in your eyes, stay here, for I have divined that the LORD has blessed me for your sake.”
He said, “ Appoint me your ages, and I ill give it.”
Jacob said to him, “ You kno ho I have served you, and ho your livestock have fared ith me.
For it as little hich you had before I came, and it has increased to a multitude. The LORD has blessed you herever I turned. No hen ill I provide for my on house also?”
Laban said, “ What shall I give you?” Jacob said, “ You shall not give me anything. If you ill do this thing for me, I ill again feed your flock and keep it.
I ill pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This ill be my hire.

So my righteousness ill anser for me hereafter, hen you come concerning my hire that is before you. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that might be ith me, ill be considered stolen.”
Laban said, “ Behold, let it be according to your ord.”

That day, he removed the male goats that ere streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that ere speckled and spotted, every one that had hite in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
He set three days’ journey beteen himself and Jacob, and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.
Jacob took to himself rods of fresh poplar, almond, and plane tree, peeled hite streaks in them, and made the hite appear hich as in the rods.
He set the rods hich he had peeled opposite the flocks in the atering troughs here the flocks came to drink. They conceived hen they came to drink.
The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks produced streaked, speckled, and spotted.
Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toard the streaked and all the black in Laban’s flock. He put his on droves apart, and didn’t put them into Laban’s flock.
Whenever the stronger of the flock conceived, Jacob laid the rods in front of the eyes of the flock in the atering troughs, that they might conceive among the rods;
but hen the flock ere feeble, he didn’t put them in. So the feebler ere Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.
The man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, female servants and male servants, and camels and donkeys.
Jacob heard Laban’s sons’ ords, saying, “ Jacob has taken aay all that as our father’s. He has obtained all this ealth from that hich as our father’s.”
Jacob sa the expression on Laban’s face, and, behold, it as not toard him as before.
The LORD said to Jacob, “ Return to the land of your fathers, and to your relatives, and I ill be ith you.”
Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field to his flock,
and said to them, “ I see the expression on your father’s face, that it is not toard me as before; but the God of my father has been ith me.
You kno that I have served your father ith all of my strength.
Your father has deceived me, and changed my ages ten times, but God didn’t allo him to hurt me.
If he said, ’ The speckled ill be your ages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he said, ’ The streaked ill be your ages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.
Thus God has taken aay your father’s livestock, and given them to me.
During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and sa in a dream, and behold, the male goats hich leaped on the flock ere streaked, speckled, and grizzled.
The angel of God said to me in the dream, ’ Jacob,’ and I said, ’ Here I am.’
He said, ’ No lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats hich leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.
I am the God of Bethel, here you anointed a pillar, here you voed a vo to me. No arise, get out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.’”
Rachel and Leah ansered him, “ Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?
Aren’t e considered as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also used up our money.
For all the riches hich God has taken aay from our father are ours and our children’s. No then, hatever God has said to you, do.”
Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his ives on the camels,
and he took aay all his livestock, and all his possessions hich he had gathered, including the livestock hich he had gained in Paddan Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
No Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the teraphim that ere her father’s.
Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he didn’t tell him that he as running aay.
So he fled ith all that he had. He rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toard the mountain of Gilead.
Laban as told on the third day that Jacob had fled.
He took his relatives ith him, and pursued him seven days’ journey. He overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.
God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said to him, “ Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.”
Laban caught up ith Jacob. No Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban ith his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.
Laban said to Jacob, “ What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried aay my daughters like captives of the sord?
Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you aay ith mirth and ith songs, ith tambourine and ith harp;
and didn’t allo me to kiss my sons and my daughters? No you have done foolishly.
It is in the poer of my hand to hurt you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ’ Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.’
No, you ant to be gone, because you greatly longed for your father’s house, but hy have you stolen my gods?”
Jacob ansered Laban, “ Because I as afraid, for I said, ’ Lest you should take your daughters from me by force.’
Anyone you find your gods ith shall not live. Before our relatives, discern hat is yours ith me, and take it.” For Jacob didn’t kno that Rachel had stolen them.
Laban ent into Jacob’s tent, into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the to female servants; but he didn’t find them. He ent out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
No Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.
She said to her father, “Don’t let my lord be angry that I can’t rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.
Jacob as angry, and argued ith Laban. Jacob ansered Laban, “ What is my trespass? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?
No that you have felt around in all my stuff, hat have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge beteen us to.
“ These tenty years I have been ith you. Your ees and your female goats have not cast their young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of your flocks.
That hich as torn of animals, I didn’t bring to you. I bore its loss. Of my hand you required it, hether stolen by day or stolen by night.
This as my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.
These tenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your to daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my ages ten times.

Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been ith me, surely no you ould have sent me aay empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

Laban ansered Jacob, “ The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine! What can I do today to these my daughters, or to their children hom they have borne?
No come, let’s make a covenant, you and I. Let it be for a itness beteen me and you.”
Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
Jacob said to his relatives, “ Gather stones.” They took stones, and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.
Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.
Laban said, “ This heap is itness beteen me and you today.” Therefore it as named Galeed
and Mizpah, for he said, “ The LORD atch beteen me and you, hen e are absent one from another.
If you afflict my daughters, or if you take ives in addition to my daughters, no man is ith us; behold, God is itness beteen me and you.”
Laban said to Jacob, “ See this heap, and see the pillar, hich I have set beteen me and you.
May this heap be a itness, and the pillar be a itness, that I ill not pass over this heap to you, and that you ill not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge beteen us.” Then Jacob sore by the fear of his father, Isaac.
Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.
Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.
Jacob ent on his ay, and the angels of God met him.
When he sa them, Jacob said, “ This is God’s army.” He called the name of that place Mahanaim.
Jacob sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
He commanded them, saying, “ This is hat you shall tell my lord, Esau: ’ This is hat your servant, Jacob, says. I have lived as a foreigner ith Laban, and stayed until no.
I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.’”
The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “ We came to your brother Esau. He is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are ith him.”
Then Jacob as greatly afraid and as distressed. He divided the people ho ere ith him, along ith the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into to companies.
He said, “If Esau comes to the one company, and strikes it, then the company hich is left ill escape.”
Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, the LORD, ho said to me, ’Return to your country, and to your relatives, and I ill do you good,’

I am not orthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, hich you have shon to your servant; for ith just my staff I crossed over this Jordan; and no I have become to companies.
Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and strike me and the mothers ith the children.
You said, ’ I ill surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, hich can’t be counted because there are so many.’”
He stayed there that night, and took from that hich he had ith him a present for Esau, his brother:
to hundred female goats and tenty male goats, to hundred ees and tenty rams,
thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cos, ten bulls, tenty female donkeys and ten foals.
He delivered them into the hands of his servants, every herd by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put a space beteen herd and herd.”
He commanded the foremost, saying, “ When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, saying, ’ Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?’
Then you shall say, ’ They are your servant, Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord, Esau. Behold, he also is behind us.’”
He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that folloed the herds, saying, “ This is ho you shall speak to Esau, hen you find him.

You shall say, ’ Not only that, but behold, your servant, Jacob, is behind us.’” For, he said, “ I ill appease him ith the present that goes before me, and afterard I ill see his face. Perhaps he ill accept me.”
So the present passed over before him, and he himself stayed that night in the camp.
He rose up that night, and took his to ives, and his to servants, and his eleven sons, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.
He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that hich he had.
Jacob as left alone, and restled ith a man there until the breaking of the day.
When he sa that he didn’t prevail against him, the man touched the hollo of his thigh, and the hollo of Jacob’s thigh as strained as he restled.
The man said, “ Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob said, “ I on’t let you go unless you bless me.”
He said to him, “ What is your name?” He said, “ Jacob”.
He said, “ Your name ill no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought ith God and ith men, and have prevailed.”
Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” He said, “ Why is it that you ask hat my name is?” So he blessed him there.
Jacob called the name of the place Peniel; for he said, “ I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
The sun rose on him as he passed over Peniel, and he limped because of his thigh.
Therefore the children of Israel don’t eat the sine of the hip, hich is on the hollo of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollo of Jacob’s thigh in the sine of the hip.
Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau as coming, and ith him four hundred men. He divided the children beteen Leah, Rachel, and the to servants.
He put the servants and their children in front, Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.
He himself passed over in front of them, and boed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they ept.
He lifted up his eyes, and sa the omen and the children; and said, “ Who are these ith you?” He said, “ The children hom God has graciously given your servant.”
Then the servants came near ith their children, and they boed themselves.
Leah also and her children came near, and boed themselves. After them, Joseph came near ith Rachel, and they boed themselves.
Esau said, “ What do you mean by all this company hich I met?” Jacob said, “ To find favor in the sight of my lord.”
Esau said, “ I have enough, my brother; let that hich you have be yours.”
Jacob said, “ Please, no, if I have no found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you ere pleased ith me.
Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously ith me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.
Esau said, “ Let’s take our journey, and let’s go, and I ill go before you.”
Jacob said to him, “ My lord knos that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds ith me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks ill die.

Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I ill lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”
Esau said, “ Let me no leave ith you some of the people ho are ith me.” He said, “ Why? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”
So Esau returned that day on his ay to Seir.

Dinah, the daughter of Leah, hom she bore to Jacob, ent out to see the daughters of the land.

Then Jacob said to his household, and to all ho ere ith him, “ Put aay the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.

They traveled from Bethel. There as still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.

These ere the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s ife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs ho came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Adah.

This is the history of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, as feeding the flock ith his brothers. He as a boy ith the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s ives. Joseph brought an evil report of them to their father.

Come no therefore, and let’s kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and e ill say, ’ An evil animal has devoured him.’ We ill see hat ill become of his dreams.”

She yet again bore a son, and named him Shelah. He as at Chezib hen she bore him.
Judah took a ife for Er, his firstborn, and her name as Tamar.
Er, Judah’s firstborn, as icked in the LORD’s sight. So the LORD killed him.

Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-la, “ Remain a ido in your father’s house, until Shelah, my son, is gron up;” for he said, “ Lest he also die, like his brothers.” Tamar ent and lived in her father’s house.

From the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake. The LORD’s blessing as on all that he had, in the house and in the field.

When she sa that he had left his garment in her hand, and had run outside,
