When he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”
She laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.
She spoke to him according to these ords, saying, “ The Hebre servant, hom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me,
and as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”
When his master heard the ords of his ife, hich she spoke to him, saying, “ This is hat your servant did to me,” his rath as kindled.
Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place here the king’s prisoners ere bound, and he as there in custody.
But the LORD as ith Joseph, and shoed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners ho ere in the prison. Whatever they did there, he as responsible for it.
The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that as under his hand, because the LORD as ith him; and that hich he did, the LORD made it prosper.
After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh as angry ith his to officers, the chief cup bearer and the chief baker.
He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place here Joseph as bound.
The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.
They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, ho ere bound in the prison.
Joseph came in to them in the morning, and sa them, and sa that they ere sad.
He asked Pharaoh’s officers ho ere ith him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “ Why do you look so sad today?”
They said to him, “ We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one ho can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”
The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “ In my dream, behold, a vine as in front of me,
and in the vine ere three branches. It as as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.
Pharaoh’s cup as in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”
Joseph said to him, “ This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
Within three more days, Pharaoh ill lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You ill give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the ay you did hen you ere his cup bearer.
But remember me hen it is ell ith you. Please sho kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
For indeed, I as stolen aay out of the land of the Hebres, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”
When the chief baker sa that the interpretation as good, he said to Joseph, “ I also as in my dream, and behold, three baskets of hite bread ere on my head.
In the uppermost basket there ere all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”
Joseph ansered, “ This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.
Within three more days, Pharaoh ill lift up your head from off you, and ill hang you on a tree; and the birds ill eat your flesh from off you.”
On the third day, hich as Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;
but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.
At the end of to full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.
Behold, seven cattle came up out of the river. They ere sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.
Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.
The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh aoke.
He slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.
Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted ith the east ind, sprung up after them.
The thin heads of grain salloed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh aoke, and behold, it as a dream.
In the morning, his spirit as troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and ise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there as no one ho could interpret them to Pharaoh.
Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “ I remember my faults today.
Pharaoh as angry ith his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, ith the chief baker.
We dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.
There as ith us there a young man, a Hebre, servant to the captain of the guard, and e told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. He interpreted to each man according to his dream.
As he interpreted to us, so it as. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”
Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “ I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one ho can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that hen you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
Joseph ansered Pharaoh, saying, “ It isn’t in me. God ill give Pharaoh an anser of peace.”
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “ In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river;
and behold, seven fat and sleek cattle came up out of the river. They fed in the marsh grass;
and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never sa in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle;
and hen they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be knon that they had eaten them, but they ere still ugly, as at the beginning. So I aoke.
I sa in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good;
and behold, seven heads of grain, ithered, thin, and blasted ith the east ind, sprung up after them.
The thin heads of grain salloed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there as no one ho could explain it to me.”
Joseph said to Pharaoh, “ The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.
The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.
The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted ith the east ind; they ill be seven years of famine.
That is the thing hich I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shon Pharaoh hat he is about to do.
Behold, seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt are coming.
Seven years of famine ill arise after them, and all the plenty ill be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine ill consume the land,
and the plenty ill not be knon in the land by reason of that famine hich follos; for it ill be very grievous.
The dream as doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God ill shortly bring it to pass.
“ No therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and ise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.
Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
The food ill be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, hich ill be in the land of Egypt; so that the land ill not perish through the famine.”
The thing as good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
Pharaoh said to his servants, “ Can e find such a one as this, a man in hom is the Spirit of God?”
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “ Because God has shon you all of this, there is no one so discreet and ise as you.
You shall be over my house. All my people ill be ruled according to your ord. Only in the throne I ill be greater than you.”
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “ Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
He made him ride in the second chariot hich he had. They cried before him, “Bo the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “ I am Pharaoh. Without you, no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a ife. Joseph ent out over the land of Egypt.
Joseph as thirty years old hen he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph ent out from the presence of Pharaoh, and ent throughout all the land of Egypt.
In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.
He gathered up all the food of the seven years hich ere in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. He stored food in each city from the fields around that city.
Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it as ithout number.
To Joseph ere born to sons before the year of famine came, hom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “ For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
The name of the second, he called Ephraim: “ For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
The seven years of plenty, that ere in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There as famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there as bread.
When all the land of Egypt as famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “ Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
The famine as over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine as severe in the land of Egypt.
All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine as severe in all the earth.
No Jacob sa that there as grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “ Why do you look at one another?”
He said, “ Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go don there, and buy for us from there, so that e may live, and not die.”
Joseph’s ten brothers ent don to buy grain from Egypt.
But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, ith his brothers; for he said, “ Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”
The sons of Israel came to buy among those ho came, for the famine as in the land of Canaan.
Joseph as the governor over the land. It as he ho sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and boed themselves don to him ith their faces to the earth.

Joseph sa his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly ith them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?” They said, “ From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”
Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.
Joseph remembered the dreams hich he dreamed about them, and said to them, “ You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
They said to him, “ No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
We are all one man’s sons; e are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”
He said to them, “ No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”
They said, “ We, your servants, are telve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today ith our father, and one is no more.”
Joseph said to them, “ It is like I told you, saying, ’ You are spies!’
By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.
Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your ords may be tested, hether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”
He put them all together into custody for three days.
Joseph said to them the third day, “ Do this, and live, for I fear God.
If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
Bring your youngest brother to me; so ill your ords be verified, and you on’t die.” They did so.
They said to one another, “ We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that e sa the distress of his soul, hen he begged us, and e ouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”
Reuben ansered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ’Don’t sin against the child,’ and you ouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”
They didn’t kno that Joseph understood them; for there as an interpreter beteen them.
He turned himself aay from them, and ept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags ith grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the ay. So it as done to them.
They loaded their donkeys ith their grain, and departed from there.
As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he sa his money. Behold, it as in the mouth of his sack.
He said to his brothers, “ My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “ What is this that God has done to us?”
They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,
“ The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly ith us, and took us for spies of the country.
We said to him, ’We are honest men. We are no spies.
We are telve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today ith our father in the land of Canaan.’
The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ’ By this I ill kno that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers ith me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your ay.
Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I ill kno that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I ill deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”
As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money as in his sack. When they and their father sa their bundles of money, they ere afraid.
Jacob, their father, said to them, “ You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you ant to take Benjamin aay. All these things are against me.”
Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “ Kill my to sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I ill bring him to you again.”
He said, “ My son shall not go don ith you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the ay in hich you go, then you ill bring don my gray hairs ith sorro to Sheol.”
The famine as severe in the land.
When they had eaten up the grain hich they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “ Go again, buy us a little more food.”
Judah spoke to him, saying, “ The man solemnly arned us, saying, ’ You shall not see my face, unless your brother is ith you.’
If you’ll send our brother ith us, e’ll go don and buy you food;
but if you don’t send him, e on’t go don, for the man said to us, ’ You shall not see my face, unless your brother is ith you.’”
Israel said, “ Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”

They said, “ The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ’ Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just ansered his questions. Is there any ay e could kno that he ould say, ’ Bring your brother don’?”
Judah said to Israel, his father, “ Send the boy ith me, and e’ll get up and go, so that e may live, and not die, both e, and you, and also our little ones.
I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand ill you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;
for if e hadn’t delayed, surely e ould have returned a second time by no.”

Their father, Israel, said to them, “ If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry don a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that as returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it as an oversight.
Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.
May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”
The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, ent don to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
When Joseph sa Benjamin ith them, he said to the steard of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men ill dine ith me at noon.”
The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.

The men ere afraid, because they ere brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “ Because of the money that as returned in our sacks the first time, e’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along ith our donkeys.”
They came near to the steard of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,
and said, “Oh, my lord, e indeed came don the first time to buy food.
When e came to the lodging place, e opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money as in the mouth of his sack, our money in full eight. We have brought it back in our hand.
We have brought don other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t kno ho put our money in our sacks.”
He said, “ Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.
The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them ater, and they ashed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.
They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.
When Joseph came home, they brought him the present hich as in their hand into the house, and boed themselves don to the earth before him.
He asked them of their elfare, and said, “ Is your father ell, the old man of hom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”
They said, “ Your servant, our father, is ell. He is still alive.” They boed don humbly.
He lifted up his eyes, and sa Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “ Is this your youngest brother, of hom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to eep. He entered into his room, and ept there.
He ashed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “ Serve the meal.”
They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians ho ate ith him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat ith the Hebres, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled ith one another.
He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion as five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and ere merry ith him.
He commanded the steard of his house, saying, “ Fill the men’s sacks ith food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, ith his grain money.” He did according to the ord that Joseph had spoken.
As soon as the morning as light, the men ere sent aay, they and their donkeys.
When they had gone out of the city, and ere not yet far off, Joseph said to his steard, “ Up, follo after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ’ Why have you rearded evil for good?
Isn’t this that from hich my lord drinks, and by hich he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”
He overtook them, and he spoke these ords to them.
They said to him, “ Why does my lord speak such ords as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
Behold, the money, hich e found in our sacks’ mouths, e brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. Ho then should e steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?
With homever of your servants it is found, let him die, and e also ill be my lord’s slaves.”
He said, “ No also let it be according to your ords. He ith hom it is found ill be my slave; and you ill be blameless.”
Then they hurried, and each man took his sack don to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
He searched, beginning ith the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup as found in Benjamin’s sack.
Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.
Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he as still there. They fell on the ground before him.
Joseph said to them, “ What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you kno that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”

Judah said, “ What ill e tell my lord? What ill e speak? Ho ill e clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, e are my lord’s slaves, both e and he also in hose hand the cup is found.”
He said, “ Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in hose hand the cup is found, he ill be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
Then Judah came near to him, and said, “ Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a ord in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, saying, ’ Have you a father, or a brother?’
We said to my lord, ’ We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
You said to your servants, ’ Bring him don to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
We said to my lord, ’ The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father ould die.’
You said to your servants, ’ Unless your youngest brother comes don ith you, you ill see my face no more.’
When e came up to your servant my father, e told him the ords of my lord.
Our father said, ’ Go again and buy us a little food.’
We said, ’ We can’t go don. If our youngest brother is ith us, then e ill go don: for e may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is ith us.’
Your servant, my father, said to us, ’ You kno that my ife bore me to sons.
One ent out from me, and I said, “ Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.
If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you ill bring don my gray hairs ith sorro to Sheol.’
No therefore hen I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not ith us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
it ill happen, hen he sees that the boy is no more, that he ill die. Your servants ill bring don the gray hairs of your servant, our father, ith sorro to Sheol.
For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ’ If I don’t bring him to you, then I ill bear the blame to my father forever.’
No therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up ith his brothers.
For ho ill I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t ith me?— lest I see the evil that ill come on my father.”

Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those ho stood before him, and he called out, “ Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood ith him, hile Joseph made himself knon to his brothers.
He ept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
Joseph said to his brothers, “ I am Joseph! Does my father still live?” His brothers couldn’t anser him; for they ere terrified at his presence.
Joseph said to his brothers, “ Come near to me, please.” They came near. He said, “ I am Joseph, your brother, hom you sold into Egypt.
No don’t be grieved, nor angry ith yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
For these to years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in hich there ill be no ploing and no harvest.
God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
So no it asn’t you ho sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ’ This is hat your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come don to me. Don’t ait.
You shall dell in the land of Goshen, and you ill be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
There I ill provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’
Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father don here.”
He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and ept, and Benjamin ept on his neck.
He kissed all his brothers, and ept on them. After that his brothers talked ith him.
The report of it as heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “ Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh ell, and his servants.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ’ Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.
Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I ill give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you ill eat the fat of the land.’
No you are commanded to do this: Take agons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your ives, and bring your father, and come.
Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them agons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the ay.
He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
He sent the folloing to his father: ten donkeys loaded ith the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded ith grain and bread and provision for his father by the ay.
So he sent his brothers aay, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the ay.”
They ent up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
They told him, saying, “ Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
They told him all the ords of Joseph, hich he had said to them. When he sa the agons hich Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.
Israel said, “ It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I ill go and see him before I die.”
Israel traveled ith all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “ Jacob, Jacob!” He said, “ Here I am.”
He said, “ I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go don into Egypt, for there I ill make of you a great nation.
I ill go don ith you into Egypt. I ill also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand ill close your eyes.”
Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their ives, in the agons hich Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
They took their livestock, and their goods, hich they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt— Jacob, and all his offspring ith him,
his sons, and his sons’ sons ith him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring ith him into Egypt.
These are the names of the children of Israel, ho came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite oman.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez ere Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, hom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, ith his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters ere thirty-three.
The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, hom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s ife: Joseph and Benjamin.
To Joseph in the land of Egypt ere born Manasseh and Ephraim, hom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, ho ere born to Jacob: all the souls ere fourteen.
The son of Dan: Hushim.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, hom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls ere seven.
All the souls ho came ith Jacob into Egypt, ho ere his direct offspring, in addition to Jacob’s sons’ ives, all the souls ere sixty-six.
The sons of Joseph, ho ere born to him in Egypt, ere to souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, ho came into Egypt, ere seventy.
Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to sho the ay before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.
Joseph prepared his chariot, and ent up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and ept on his neck a good hile.
Israel said to Joseph, “ No let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”
Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “ I ill go up, and speak ith Pharaoh, and ill tell him, ’ My brothers, and my father’s house, ho ere in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’
It ill happen, hen Pharaoh summons you, and ill say, ’ What is your occupation?’

that you shall say, ’ Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until no, both e, and our fathers:’ that you may dell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

Then Joseph ent in and told Pharaoh, and said, “ My father and my brothers, ith their flocks, their herds, and all that they on, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”
From among his brothers he took five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to his brothers, “ What is your occupation?” They said to Pharaoh, “ Your servants are shepherds, both e, and our fathers.”

They also said to Pharaoh, “ We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. No therefore, please let your servants dell in the land of Goshen.”
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “ Your father and your brothers have come to you.

The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dell in the best of the land. Let them dell in the land of Goshen. If you kno any able men among them, then put them in charge of my livestock.”
Joseph brought in Jacob, his father, and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Jacob, “ Ho old are you?”

Jacob said to Pharaoh, “ The years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. The days of the years of my life have been fe and evil. They have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”
Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and ent out from the presence of Pharaoh.
Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
Joseph provided his father, his brothers, and all of his father’s household ith bread, according to the sizes of their families.
There as no bread in all the land; for the famine as very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
Joseph gathered up all the money that as found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain hich they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.
When the money as all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “ Give us bread, for hy should e die in your presence? For our money fails.”
Joseph said, “ Give me your livestock; and I ill give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone.”

They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed them ith bread in exchange for all their livestock for that year.

When that year as ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, “ We ill not hide from my lord ho our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord’s. There is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

Why should e die before your eyes, both e and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and e and our land ill be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that e may live, and not die, and that the land on’t be desolate.”
So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every man of the Egyptians sold his field, because the famine as severe on them, and the land became Pharaoh’s.
As for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end of it.
Only he didn’t buy the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and ate their portion hich Pharaoh gave them. That is hy they didn’t sell their land.
Then Joseph said to the people, “ Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall so the land.

It ill happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts ill be your on, for seed of the field, for your food, for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.”
They said, “ You have saved our lives! Let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and e ill be Pharaoh’s servants.”
Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone didn’t become Pharaoh’s.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they got themselves possessions therein, and ere fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, ere one hundred forty-seven years.

The time came near that Israel must die, and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, “ If no I have found favor in your sight, please put your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly ith me. Please don’t bury me in Egypt,

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“ Speak to the children of Israel, that they take an offering for me. From everyone hose heart makes him illing you shall take my offering.
This is the offering hich you shall take from them: gold, silver, bronze,
blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
rams’ skins dyed red, sea co hides, acacia ood,
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the seet incense,
onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dell among them.
According to all that I sho you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
“ They shall make an ark of acacia ood. Its length shall be to and a half cubits, its idth a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
You shall overlay it ith pure gold. You shall overlay it inside and outside, and you shall make a gold molding around it.
You shall cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in its four feet. To rings shall be on the one side of it, and to rings on the other side of it.
You shall make poles of acacia ood, and overlay them ith gold.
You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
The poles shall be in the rings of the ark. They shall not be taken from it.
You shall put the covenant hich I shall give you into the ark.
You shall make a mercy seat of pure gold. To and a half cubits shall be its length, and a cubit and a half its idth.
You shall make to cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the to ends of the mercy seat.
Make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim on its to ends of one piece ith the mercy seat.
The cherubim shall spread out their ings upard, covering the mercy seat ith their ings, ith their faces toard one another. The faces of the cherubim shall be toard the mercy seat.
You shall put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and in the ark you shall put the covenant that I ill give you.
There I ill meet ith you, and I ill tell you from above the mercy seat, from beteen the to cherubim hich are on the ark of the covenant, all that I command you for the children of Israel.
“ You shall make a table of acacia ood. Its length shall be to cubits, and its idth a cubit, and its height one and a half cubits.
You shall overlay it ith pure gold, and make a gold molding around it.
You shall make a rim of a hand idth around it. You shall make a golden molding on its rim around it.

The rings shall be close to the rim, for places for the poles to carry the table.

Each board had to tenons, joined to one another. He made all the boards of the tabernacle this ay.

He made forty sockets of silver under the tenty boards: to sockets under one board for its to tenons, and to sockets under another board for its to tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made tenty boards
and their forty sockets of silver: to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
For the far part of the tabernacle estard he made six boards.
He made to boards for the corners of the tabernacle in the far part.
They ere double beneath, and in the same ay they ere all the ay to its top to one ring. He did this to both of them in the to corners.
There ere eight boards and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets— under every board to sockets.
He made bars of acacia ood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the hinder part estard.
He made the middle bar to pass through in the middle of the boards from the one end to the other.
He overlaid the boards ith gold, and made their rings of gold as places for the bars, and overlaid the bars ith gold.
He made the veil of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen, ith cherubim. He made it the ork of a skillful orkman.
He made four pillars of acacia for it, and overlaid them ith gold. Their hooks ere of gold. He cast four sockets of silver for them.
He made a screen for the door of the tent, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen, the ork of an embroiderer;
and the five pillars of it ith their hooks. He overlaid their capitals and their fillets ith gold, and their five sockets ere of bronze.
Bezalel made the ark of acacia ood. Its length as to and a half cubits, and its idth a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
He overlaid it ith pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold for it around it.
He cast four rings of gold for it in its four feet— to rings on its one side, and to rings on its other side.
He made poles of acacia ood and overlaid them ith gold.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
He made a mercy seat of pure gold. Its length as to and a half cubits, and a cubit and a half its idth.
He made to cherubim of gold. He made them of beaten ork, at the to ends of the mercy seat:
one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece ith the mercy seat at its to ends.
The cherubim spread out their ings above, covering the mercy seat ith their ings, ith their faces toard one another. The faces of the cherubim ere toard the mercy seat.
He made the table of acacia ood. Its length as to cubits, and its idth as a cubit, and its height as a cubit and a half.
He overlaid it ith pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.
He made a border of a hand’s idth around it, and made a golden molding on its border around it.
He cast four rings of gold for it, and put the rings in the four corners that ere on its four feet.
The rings ere close by the border, the places for the poles to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith gold, to carry the table.
He made the vessels hich ere on the table, its dishes, its spoons, its bols, and its pitchers ith hich to pour out, of pure gold.
He made the lamp stand of pure gold. He made the lamp stand of beaten ork. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its floers ere of one piece ith it.
There ere six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side:

three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a floer, and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a floer; so for the six branches going out of the lamp stand.
In the lamp stand ere four cups made like almond blossoms, its buds and its floers;
and a bud under to branches of one piece ith it, and a bud under to branches of one piece ith it, and a bud under to branches of one piece ith it, for the six branches going out of it.
Their buds and their branches ere of one piece ith it. The hole thing as one beaten ork of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, of pure gold.
He made it of a talent of pure gold, ith all its vessels.
He made the altar of incense of acacia ood. It as square: its length as a cubit, and its idth a cubit. Its height as to cubits. Its horns ere of one piece ith it.
He overlaid it ith pure gold: its top, its sides around it, and its horns. He made a gold molding around it.
He made to golden rings for it under its molding cron, on its to ribs, on its to sides, for places for poles ith hich to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of seet spices, after the art of the perfumer.
He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia ood. It as square. Its length as five cubits, its idth as five cubits, and its height as three cubits.
He made its horns on its four corners. Its horns ere of one piece ith it, and he overlaid it ith bronze.
He made all the vessels of the altar: the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. He made all its vessels of bronze.
He made for the altar a grating of a netork of bronze, under the ledge around it beneath, reaching halfay up.
He cast four rings for the four corners of bronze grating, to be places for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith bronze.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, ith hich to carry it. He made it hollo ith planks.
He made the basin of bronze, and its base of bronze, out of the mirrors of the ministering omen ho ministered at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He made the court: for the south side southard the hangings of the court ere of fine tined linen, one hundred cubits;
their pillars ere tenty, and their sockets tenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets ere of silver.
For the north side one hundred cubits, their pillars tenty, and their sockets tenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
For the est side ere hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
For the east side eastard fifty cubits,
the hangings for the one side ere fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three;
and so for the other side: on this hand and that hand by the gate of the court ere hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
All the hangings around the court ere of fine tined linen.
The sockets for the pillars ere of bronze. The hooks of the pillars and their fillets ere of silver. Their capitals ere overlaid ith silver. All the pillars of the court had silver bands.

The screen for the gate of the court as the ork of the embroiderer, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen. Tenty cubits as the length, and the height along the idth as five cubits, like the hangings of the court.
Their pillars ere four, and their sockets four, of bronze; their hooks of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals, and their fillets, of silver.
All the pins of the tabernacle, and around the court, ere of bronze.

These are the amounts of materials used for the tabernacle, even the Tabernacle of the Testimony, as they ere counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the LORD commanded Moses.
With him as Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a skillful orkman, and an embroiderer in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen.
All the gold that as used for the ork in all the ork of the sanctuary, even the gold of the offering, as tenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
The silver of those ho ere counted of the congregation as one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary:

a beka a head, that is, half a shekel, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, for everyone ho passed over to those ho ere counted, from tenty years old and upard, for six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.
The one hundred talents of silver ere for casting the sockets of the sanctuary and the sockets of the veil: one hundred sockets for the one hundred talents, one talent per socket.
From the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and made fillets for them.
The bronze of the offering as seventy talents and to thousand four hundred shekels.
With this he made the sockets to the door of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, the bronze grating for it, all the vessels of the altar,
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins around the court.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely orked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen.
They beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into ires, to ork it in ith the blue, the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen, the ork of the skillful orkman.
They made shoulder straps for it, joined together. It as joined together at the to ends.
The skillfully oven band that as on it, ith hich to fasten it on, as of the same piece, like its ork: of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen, as the LORD commanded Moses.
They orked the onyx stones, enclosed in settings of gold, engraved ith the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the children of Israel.
He put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He made the breastplate, the ork of a skillful orkman, like the ork of the ephod: of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen.
It as square. They made the breastplate double. Its length as a span, and its idth a span, being double.
They set in it four ros of stones. A ro of ruby, topaz, and beryl as the first ro;
and the second ro, a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald;
and the third ro, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth ro, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They ere enclosed in gold settings.
The stones ere according to the names of the children of Israel, telve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, for the telve tribes.
They made on the breastplate chains like cords, of braided ork of pure gold.
They made to settings of gold, and to gold rings, and put the to rings on the to ends of the breastplate.
They put the to braided chains of gold in the to rings at the ends of the breastplate.
The other to ends of the to braided chains they put on the to settings, and put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod, in its front.
They made to rings of gold, and put them on the to ends of the breastplate, on its edge, hich as toard the side of the ephod inard.
They made to more rings of gold, and put them on the to shoulder straps of the ephod underneath, in its front, close by its coupling, above the skillfully oven band of the ephod.

They bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod ith a lace of blue, that it might be on the skillfully oven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod of oven ork, all of blue.
The opening of the robe in the middle of it as like the opening of a coat of mail, ith a binding around its opening, that it should not be torn.
They made on the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, scarlet, and tined linen.
They made bells of pure gold, and put the bells beteen the pomegranates around the skirts of the robe, beteen the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, around the skirts of the robe, to minister in, as the LORD commanded Moses.
They made the tunics of fine linen of oven ork for Aaron and for his sons,
the turban of fine linen, the linen headbands of fine linen, the linen trousers of fine tined linen,
the sash of fine tined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet, the ork of the embroiderer, as the LORD commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the holy cron of pure gold, and rote on it an inscription, like the engravings of a signet: “ HOLY TO THE LORD”.
They tied to it a lace of blue, to fasten it on the turban above, as the LORD commanded Moses.
Thus all the ork of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting as finished. The children of Israel did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses; so they did.
They brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent, ith all its furniture, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,
the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, the covering of sea co hides, the veil of the screen,
the ark of the covenant ith its poles, the mercy seat,
the table, all its vessels, the sho bread,
the pure lamp stand, its lamps, even the lamps to be set in order, all its vessels, the oil for the light,
the golden altar, the anointing oil, the seet incense, the screen for the door of the Tent,
the bronze altar, its grating of bronze, its poles, all of its vessels, the basin and its base,
the hangings of the court, its pillars, its sockets, the screen for the gate of the court, its cords, its pins, and all the instruments of the service of the tabernacle, for the Tent of Meeting,
the finely orked garments for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.
According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the ork.
Moses sa all the ork, and behold, they had done it as the LORD had commanded. They had done so; and Moses blessed them.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“ On the first day of the first month you shall raise up the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.
You shall put the ark of the covenant in it, and you shall screen the ark ith the veil.
You shall bring in the table, and set in order the things that are on it. You shall bring in the lamp stand, and light its lamps.
You shall set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the covenant, and put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
“ You shall set the altar of burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.
You shall set the basin beteen the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and shall put ater therein.
You shall set up the court around it, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.
“ You shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it, and shall make it holy, and all its furniture, and it ill be holy.
You shall anoint the altar of burnt offering, ith all its vessels, and sanctify the altar, and the altar ill be most holy.
You shall anoint the basin and its base, and sanctify it.
“ You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall ash them ith ater.
You shall put on Aaron the holy garments; and you shall anoint him, and sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
You shall bring his sons, and put tunics on them.
You shall anoint them, as you anointed their father, that they may minister to me in the priest’s office. Their anointing shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”
Moses did so. According to all that the LORD commanded him, so he did.
In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle as raised up.
Moses raised up the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up its boards, and put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.
He spread the covering over the tent, and put the roof of the tabernacle above on it, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He took and put the covenant into the ark, and set the poles on the ark, and put the mercy seat above on the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the covenant, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside of the veil.
He set the bread in order on it before the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He put the lamp stand in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He lit the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He put the golden altar in the Tent of Meeting before the veil;
and he burned incense of seet spices on it, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He put up the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
He set the altar of burnt offering at the door of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the meal offering, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He set the basin beteen the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put ater therein, ith hich to ash.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons ashed their hands and their feet there.
When they ent into the Tent of Meeting, and hen they came near to the altar, they ashed, as the LORD commanded Moses.
He raised up the court around the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the ork.
Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the LORD’s glory filled the tabernacle.
Moses asn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and the LORD’s glory filled the tabernacle.
When the cloud as taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel ent onard, throughout all their journeys;
but if the cloud asn’t taken up, then they didn’t travel until the day that it as taken up.
For the cloud of the LORD as on the tabernacle by day, and there as fire in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
The LORD called to Moses, and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
“ Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ’ When anyone of you offers an offering to the LORD, you shall offer your offering of the livestock, from the herd and from the flock.
“’If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male ithout defect. He shall offer it at the door of the Tent of Meeting, that he may be accepted before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.
He shall kill the bull before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood and sprinkle the blood around on the altar that is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar, and lay ood in order on the fire;
and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces, the head, and the fat in order on the ood that is on the fire hich is on the altar;
but he shall ash its innards and its legs ith ater. The priest shall burn all of it on the altar, for a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
“’If his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall offer a male ithout defect.
He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
He shall cut it into its pieces, ith its head and its fat. The priest shall lay them in order on the ood that is on the fire hich is on the altar,
but the innards and the legs he shall ash ith ater. The priest shall offer the hole, and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
“’ If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, then he shall offer his offering from turtledoves or of young pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, and ring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar;
and he shall take aay its crop and its feathers, and cast it beside the altar on the east part, in the place of the ashes.

He shall tear it by its ings, but shall not divide it apart. The priest shall burn it on the altar, on the ood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
“’ When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.

He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. He shall take his handful of its fine flour, and of its oil, ith all its frankincense, and the priest shall burn its memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
That hich is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy part of the offerings of the LORD made by fire.
“’ When you offer an offering of a meal offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed ith oil, or unleavened afers anointed ith oil.
If your offering is a meal offering made on a griddle, it shall be of unleavened fine flour, mixed ith oil.
You shall cut it in pieces, and pour oil on it. It is a meal offering.
If your offering is a meal offering of the pan, it shall be made of fine flour ith oil.
You shall bring the meal offering that is made of these things to the LORD. It shall be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take from the meal offering its memorial, and shall burn it on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
That hich is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy part of the offerings of the LORD made by fire.
“’ No meal offering hich you shall offer to the LORD shall be made ith yeast; for you shall burn no yeast, nor any honey, as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
As an offering of first fruits you shall offer them to the LORD, but they shall not rise up as a pleasant aroma on the altar.

Every offering of your meal offering you shall season ith salt. You shall not allo the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your meal offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
“’If you offer a meal offering of first fruits to the LORD, you shall offer for the meal offering of your first fruits fresh heads of grain parched ith fire and crushed.
You shall put oil on it and lay frankincense on it. It is a meal offering.
The priest shall burn as its memorial part of its crushed grain and part of its oil, along ith all its frankincense. It is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
“’ If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings, if he offers it from the herd, hether male or female, he shall offer it ithout defect before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar.
He shall offer of the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to the LORD. The fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, ith the kidneys, he shall take aay.
Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar on the burnt offering, hich is on the ood that is on the fire: it is an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
“’If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD is from the flock, either male or female, he shall offer it ithout defect.
If he offers a lamb for his offering, then he shall offer it before the LORD;
and he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.

He shall offer from the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to the LORD; its fat, the entire tail fat, he shall take aay close to the backbone; and the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, ith the kidneys, he shall take aay.
The priest shall burn it on the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire to the LORD.
“’If his offering is a goat, then he shall offer it before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on its head, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting; and the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.
He shall offer from it as his offering, an offering made by fire to the LORD; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, ith the kidneys, he shall take aay.
The priest shall burn them on the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma; all the fat is the LORD’s.
“’ It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“ Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ’ If anyone sins unintentionally, in any of the things hich the LORD has commanded not to be done, and does any one of them,
if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin hich he has sinned a young bull ithout defect to the LORD for a sin offering.
He shall bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD; and he shall lay his hand on the head of the bull, and kill the bull before the LORD.
The anointed priest shall take some of the blood of the bull, and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the LORD, before the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of seet incense before the LORD, hich is in the Tent of Meeting; and he shall pour out the rest of the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of burnt offering, hich is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall take all the fat of the bull of the sin offering from it: the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, ith the kidneys, he shall remove,
as it is removed from the bull of the sacrifice of peace offerings. The priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
He shall carry the bull’s skin, all its meat, ith its head, and ith its legs, its innards, and its dung
— all the rest of the bull— outside of the camp to a clean place here the ashes are poured out, and burn it on ood ith fire. It shall be burned here the ashes are poured out.
“’If the hole congregation of Israel sins, and the thing is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done any of the things hich the LORD has commanded not to be done, and are guilty;
hen the sin in hich they have sinned is knon, then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before the LORD; and the bull shall be killed before the LORD.
The anointed priest shall bring some of the blood of the bull to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, before the veil.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar hich is before the LORD, that is in the Tent of Meeting; and the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, hich is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
All its fat he shall take from it, and burn it on the altar.
He shall do this ith the bull; as he did ith the bull of the sin offering, so he shall do ith this; and the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
“’ When a ruler sins, and unittingly does any one of all the things hich the LORD his God has commanded not to be done, and is guilty,
if his sin in hich he has sinned is made knon to him, he shall bring as his offering a goat, a male ithout defect.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and kill it in the place here they kill the burnt offering before the LORD. It is a sin offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering ith his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
All its fat he shall burn on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and he ill be forgiven.
“’ If anyone of the common people sins unittingly, in doing any of the things hich the LORD has commanded not to be done, and is guilty,
if his sin hich he has sinned is made knon to him, then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female ithout defect, for his sin hich he has sinned.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill the sin offering in the place of burnt offering.
The priest shall take some of its blood ith his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall take aay, like the fat is taken aay from the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma to the LORD; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he ill be forgiven.
“’If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring a female ithout defect.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill it for a sin offering in the place here they kill the burnt offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering ith his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and all the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

“’ If anyone sins, in that he hears a public adjuration to testify, he being a itness, hether he has seen or knon, if he doesn’t report it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

“’ Or if anyone touches any unclean thing, hether it is the carcass of an unclean animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean creeping things, and it is hidden from him, and he is unclean, then he shall be guilty.
“’ Or if he touches the uncleanness of man, hatever his uncleanness is ith hich he is unclean, and it is hidden from him; hen he knos of it, then he shall be guilty.

and he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD for his sin hich he has sinned: a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin.

“’ If he can’t afford a lamb, then he shall bring his trespass offering for that in hich he has sinned, to turtledoves, or to young pigeons, to the LORD; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.

“’ But if he can’t afford to turtledoves or to young pigeons, then he shall bring as his offering for that in hich he has sinned, one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it, and he shall not put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned in any of these things, and he ill be forgiven; and the rest shall be the priest’s, as the meal offering.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“ If anyone commits a trespass, and sins unittingly regarding the LORD’s holy things, then he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD: a ram ithout defect from the flock, according to your estimation in silver by shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass offering.

“ If anyone sins, doing any of the things hich the LORD has commanded not to be done, though he didn’t kno it, he is still guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“ If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against the LORD, and deals falsely ith his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ’ This is the la of the burnt offering: the burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.

“’ This is the la of the meal offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before the LORD, before the altar.

Every male among the children of Aaron shall eat of it, as their portion forever throughout your generations, from the offerings of the LORD made by fire. Whoever touches them shall be holy.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“ This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons, hich they shall offer to the LORD in the day hen he is anointed: one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening.

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ’This is the la of the sin offering: in the place here the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering shall be killed before the LORD. It is most holy.

But the earthen vessel in hich it is boiled shall be broken; and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in ater.

No sin offering, of hich any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be eaten. It shall be burned ith fire.
“’ This is the la of the trespass offering: It is most holy.
In the place here they kill the burnt offering, he shall kill the trespass offering; and its blood he shall sprinkle around on the altar.
He shall offer all of its fat: the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards,
and he shall take aay the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, ith the kidneys;

“’ As is the sin offering, so is the trespass offering; there is one la for them. The priest ho makes atonement ith them shall have it.

“’ This is the la of the sacrifice of peace offerings, hich one shall offer to the LORD:

“’ But if the sacrifice of his offering is a vo, or a free ill offering, it shall be eaten on the day that he offers his sacrifice. On the next day hat remains of it shall be eaten,

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
