If she cannot afford a lamb, then she shall take to turtledoves or to young pigeons: the one for a burnt offering, and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

“ When a man shall have a selling in his body’s skin, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his body the plague of leprosy, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

The priest shall examine the plague in the skin of the body. If the hair in the plague has turned hite, and the appearance of the plague is deeper than the body’s skin, it is the plague of leprosy; so the priest shall examine him and pronounce him unclean.
If the bright spot is hite in the skin of his body, and its appearance isn’t deeper than the skin, and its hair hasn’t turned hite, then the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. Behold, if in his eyes the plague is arrested and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall isolate him for seven more days.

The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day. Behold, if the plague has faded and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. It is a scab. He shall ash his clothes, and be clean.
But if the scab spreads on the skin after he has shon himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall sho himself to the priest again.
The priest shall examine him; and behold, if the scab has spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is leprosy.
“ When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought to the priest;
and the priest shall examine him. Behold, if there is a hite selling in the skin, and it has turned the hair hite, and there is ra flesh in the selling,
it is a chronic leprosy in the skin of his body, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He shall not isolate him, for he is already unclean.
“If the leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the infected person from his head even to his feet, as far as it appears to the priest,
then the priest shall examine him. Behold, if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean of the plague. It has all turned hite: he is clean.
But henever ra flesh appears in him, he shall be unclean.
The priest shall examine the ra flesh, and pronounce him unclean: the ra flesh is unclean. It is leprosy.
Or if the ra flesh turns again, and is changed to hite, then he shall come to the priest.
The priest shall examine him. Behold, if the plague has turned hite, then the priest shall pronounce him clean of the plague. He is clean.
“ When the body has a boil on its skin, and it has healed,
and in the place of the boil there is a hite selling, or a bright spot, reddish-hite, then it shall be shon to the priest.

The priest shall examine it. Behold, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and its hair has turned hite, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy. It has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it, and behold, there are no hite hairs in it, and it isn’t deeper than the skin, but is dim, then the priest shall isolate him seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a plague.
But if the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread, it is the scar from the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
“ Or hen the body has a burn from fire on its skin, and the ra flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-hite, or hite,

then the priest shall examine it; and behold, if the hair in the bright spot has turned hite, and its appearance is deeper than the skin, it is leprosy. It has broken out in the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it, and behold, there is no hite hair in the bright spot, and it isn’t deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the priest shall isolate him seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.
If the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread in the skin, but is faded, it is the selling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar from the burn.
“ When a man or oman has a plague on the head or on the beard,

then the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yello and thin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an itch. It is leprosy of the head or of the beard.

If the priest examines the plague of itching, and behold, its appearance isn’t deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the priest shall isolate the person infected ith itching seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if the itch hasn’t spread, and there is no yello hair in it, and the appearance of the itch isn’t deeper than the skin,
then he shall be shaved, but he shall not shave the itch. Then the priest shall isolate the one ho has the itch seven more days.

On the seventh day, the priest shall examine the itch; and behold, if the itch hasn’t spread in the skin, and its appearance isn’t deeper than the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. He shall ash his clothes and be clean.
But if the itch spreads in the skin after his cleansing,
then the priest shall examine him; and behold, if the itch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not look for the yello hair; he is unclean.
But if in his eyes the itch is arrested and black hair has gron in it, then the itch is healed. He is clean. The priest shall pronounce him clean.
“ When a man or a oman has bright spots in the skin of the body, even hite bright spots,
then the priest shall examine them. Behold, if the bright spots on the skin of their body are a dull hite, it is a harmless rash. It has broken out in the skin. He is clean.
“ If a man’s hair has fallen from his head, he is bald. He is clean.
If his hair has fallen off from the front part of his head, his forehead is bald. He is clean.
But if a reddish-hite plague is in the bald head or the bald forehead, it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head or his bald forehead.
Then the priest shall examine him. Behold, if the selling of the plague is reddish-hite in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the body,
he is a leprous man. He is unclean. The priest shall surely pronounce him unclean. His plague is on his head.
“ The leper in hom the plague is shall ear torn clothes, and the hair of his head shall hang loose. He shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, ’ Unclean! Unclean!’
All the days in hich the plague is in him he shall be unclean. He is unclean. He shall dell alone. His delling shall be outside of the camp.
“ The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, hether it is a oolen garment, or a linen garment;
hether it is in arp or oof; of linen or of ool; hether in leather, or in anything made of leather;
if the plague is greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the leather, or in the arp, or in the oof, or in anything made of leather; it is the plague of leprosy, and shall be shon to the priest.
The priest shall examine the plague, and isolate the plague seven days.

He shall examine the plague on the seventh day. If the plague has spread in the garment, either in the arp, or in the oof, or in the skin, hatever use the skin is used for, the plague is a destructive milde. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, hether the arp or the oof, in ool or in linen, or anything of leather, in hich the plague is, for it is a destructive milde. It shall be burned in the fire.
“ If the priest examines it, and behold, the plague hasn’t spread in the garment, either in the arp, or in the oof, or in anything of skin;
then the priest shall command that they ash the thing that the plague is in, and he shall isolate it seven more days.

Then the priest shall examine it, after the plague is ashed; and behold, if the plague hasn’t changed its color, and the plague hasn’t spread, it is unclean; you shall burn it in the fire. It is a mildeed spot, hether the bareness is inside or outside.
If the priest looks, and behold, the plague has faded after it is ashed, then he shall tear it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the arp, or out of the oof;
and if it appears again in the garment, either in the arp, or in the oof, or in anything of skin, it is spreading. You shall burn hat the plague is in ith fire.
The garment, either the arp, or the oof, or hatever thing of skin it is, hich you shall ash, if the plague has departed from them, then it shall be ashed the second time, and it ill be clean.”
This is the la of the plague of milde in a garment of ool or linen, either in the arp, or the oof, or in anything of skin, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“ This shall be the la of the leper in the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought to the priest,
and the priest shall go out of the camp. The priest shall examine him. Behold, if the plague of leprosy is healed in the leper,
then the priest shall command them to take for him ho is to be cleansed to living clean birds, cedar ood, scarlet, and hyssop.
The priest shall command them to kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running ater.
As for the living bird, he shall take it, the cedar ood, the scarlet, and the hyssop, and shall dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that as killed over the running ater.
He shall sprinkle on him ho is to be cleansed from the leprosy seven times, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let the living bird go into the open field.

“ He ho is to be cleansed shall ash his clothes, and shave off all his hair, and bathe himself in ater; and he shall be clean. After that he shall come into the camp, but shall dell outside his tent seven days.

It shall be on the seventh day, that he shall shave all his hair off his head and his beard and his eyebros. He shall shave off all his hair. He shall ash his clothes, and he shall bathe his body in ater. Then he shall be clean.
“ On the eighth day he shall take to male lambs ithout defect, one ee lamb a year old ithout defect, three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed ith oil, and one log of oil.
The priest ho cleanses him shall set the man ho is to be cleansed, and those things, before the LORD, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
“ The priest shall take one of the male lambs, and offer him for a trespass offering, ith the log of oil, and ave them for a ave offering before the LORD.

He shall kill the male lamb in the place here they kill the sin offering and the burnt offering, in the place of the sanctuary; for as the sin offering is the priest’s, so is the trespass offering. It is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering, and the priest shall put it on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his on left hand.
The priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle some of the oil ith his finger seven times before the LORD.

The priest shall put some of the rest of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, upon the blood of the trespass offering.
The rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put on the head of him ho is to be cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD.
“ The priest shall offer the sin offering, and make atonement for him ho is to be cleansed because of his uncleanness. Afterard he shall kill the burnt offering;
then the priest shall offer the burnt offering and the meal offering on the altar. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

“ If he is poor, and can’t afford so much, then he shall take one male lamb for a trespass offering to be aved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed ith oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil;
and to turtledoves, or to young pigeons, such as he is able to afford; and the one shall be a sin offering, and the other a burnt offering.
“ On the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, before the LORD.
The priest shall take the lamb of the trespass offering, and the log of oil, and the priest shall ave them for a ave offering before the LORD.

He shall kill the lamb of the trespass offering. The priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering and put it on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the palm of his on left hand;
and the priest shall sprinkle ith his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before the LORD.

Then the priest shall put some of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him ho is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the trespass offering.
The rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put on the head of him ho is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
He shall offer one of the turtledoves, or of the young pigeons, hich ever he is able to afford,
of the kind he is able to afford, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, ith the meal offering. The priest shall make atonement for him ho is to be cleansed before the LORD.”
This is the la for him in hom is the plague of leprosy, ho is not able to afford the sacrifice for his cleansing.
The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“ When you have come into the land of Canaan, hich I give to you for a possession, and I put a spreading milde in a house in the land of your possession,
then he ho ons the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, ’ There seems to me to be some sort of plague in the house.’

The priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest goes in to examine the plague, that all that is in the house not be made unclean. Afterard the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
He shall examine the plague; and behold, if the plague is in the alls of the house ith hollo streaks, greenish or reddish, and it appears to be deeper than the all,
then the priest shall go out of the house to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.
The priest shall come again on the seventh day, and look. If the plague has spread in the alls of the house,
then the priest shall command that they take out the stones in hich is the plague, and cast them into an unclean place outside of the city.
He shall cause the inside of the house to be scraped all over. They shall pour out the mortar that they scraped off outside of the city into an unclean place.
They shall take other stones, and put them in the place of those stones; and he shall take other mortar, and shall plaster the house.
“If the plague comes again, and breaks out in the house after he has taken out the stones, and after he has scraped the house, and after it as plastered,
then the priest shall come in and look; and behold, if the plague has spread in the house, it is a destructive milde in the house. It is unclean.
He shall break don the house, its stones, and its timber, and all the house’s mortar. He shall carry them out of the city into an unclean place.
“Moreover he ho goes into the house hile it is shut up shall be unclean until the evening.
He ho lies don in the house shall ash his clothes; and he ho eats in the house shall ash his clothes.

“ If the priest shall come in, and examine it, and behold, the plague hasn’t spread in the house, after the house as plastered, then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
To cleanse the house he shall take to birds, cedar ood, scarlet, and hyssop.
He shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running ater.
He shall take the cedar ood, the hyssop, the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird, and in the running ater, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He shall cleanse the house ith the blood of the bird, and ith the running ater, ith the living bird, ith the cedar ood, ith the hyssop, and ith the scarlet;
but he shall let the living bird go out of the city into the open field. So shall he make atonement for the house; and it shall be clean.”
This is the la for any plague of leprosy, and for an itch,
and for the destructive milde of a garment, and for a house,
and for a selling, and for a scab, and for a bright spot;
to teach hen it is unclean, and hen it is clean. This is the la of leprosy.
The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“ Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ’ When any man has a discharge from his body, because of his discharge he is unclean.
This shall be his uncleanness in his discharge: hether his body runs ith his discharge, or his body has stopped from his discharge, it is his uncleanness.
“’ Every bed on hich he ho has the discharge lies shall be unclean; and everything he sits on shall be unclean.
Whoever touches his bed shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
He ho sits on anything on hich the man ho has the discharge sat shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ He ho touches the body of him ho has the discharge shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ If he ho has the discharge spits on him ho is clean, then he shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ Whatever saddle he ho has the discharge rides on shall be unclean.
Whoever touches anything that as under him shall be unclean until the evening. He ho carries those things shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ Whomever he ho has the discharge touches, ithout having rinsed his hands in ater, he shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ The earthen vessel, hich he ho has the discharge touches, shall be broken; and every vessel of ood shall be rinsed in ater.

“’ When he ho has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count to himself seven days for his cleansing, and ash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running ater, and shall be clean.
“’ On the eighth day he shall take to turtledoves, or to young pigeons, and come before the LORD to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest shall offer them, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.
“’ If any man has an emission of semen, then he shall bathe all his flesh in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
Every garment and every skin hich the semen is on shall be ashed ith ater, and be unclean until the evening.
If a man lies ith a oman and there is an emission of semen, they shall both bathe themselves in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ If a oman has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is blood, she shall be in her impurity seven days. Whoever touches her shall be unclean until the evening.
“’ Everything that she lies on in her impurity shall be unclean. Everything also that she sits on shall be unclean.
Whoever touches her bed shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
Whoever touches anything that she sits on shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
If it is on the bed, or on anything she sits on, hen he touches it, he shall be unclean until the evening.
“’ If any man lies ith her, and her monthly flo is on him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed he lies on shall be unclean.

“’ If a oman has a discharge of her blood many days not in the time of her period, or if she has a discharge beyond the time of her period, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness shall be as in the days of her period. She is unclean.
Every bed she lies on all the days of her discharge shall be to her as the bed of her period. Everything she sits on shall be unclean, as the uncleanness of her period.
Whoever touches these things shall be unclean, and shall ash his clothes and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening.
“’ But if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take to turtledoves, or to young pigeons, and bring them to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering; and the priest shall make atonement for her before the LORD for the uncleanness of her discharge.
“’ Thus you shall separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, so they ill not die in their uncleanness hen they defile my tabernacle that is among them.’”
This is the la of him ho has a discharge, and of him ho has an emission of semen, so that he is unclean by it;
and of her ho has her period, and of a man or oman ho has a discharge, and of him ho lies ith her ho is unclean.
The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of the to sons of Aaron, hen they came near before the LORD, and died;

and the LORD said to Moses, “ Tell Aaron your brother not to come at just any time into the Most Holy Place ithin the veil, before the mercy seat hich is on the ark; lest he die; for I ill appear in the cloud on the mercy seat.
“Aaron shall come into the sanctuary ith a young bull for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.

He shall put on the holy linen tunic. He shall have the linen trousers on his body, and shall put on the linen sash, and he shall be clothed ith the linen turban. They are the holy garments. He shall bathe his body in ater, and put them on.
He shall take from the congregation of the children of Israel to male goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.
“Aaron shall offer the bull of the sin offering, hich is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house.
He shall take the to goats, and set them before the LORD at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots for the to goats: one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat.
Aaron shall present the goat on hich the lot fell for the LORD, and offer him for a sin offering.
But the goat on hich the lot fell for the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make atonement for him, to send him aay as the scapegoat into the ilderness.
“Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering, hich is for himself, and shall make atonement for himself and for his house, and shall kill the bull of the sin offering hich is for himself.
He shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar before the LORD, and to handfuls of seet incense beaten small, and bring it ithin the veil.
He shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy seat that is on the covenant, so that he ill not die.
He shall take some of the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it ith his finger on the mercy seat on the east; and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood ith his finger seven times.

“ Then he shall kill the goat of the sin offering that is for the people, and bring his blood ithin the veil, and do ith his blood as he did ith the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the mercy seat and before the mercy seat.

He shall make atonement for the Holy Place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions, even all their sins; and so he shall do for the Tent of Meeting that dells ith them in the middle of their uncleanness.

No one shall be in the Tent of Meeting hen he enters to make atonement in the Holy Place, until he comes out, and has made atonement for himself and for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.
“ He shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it, and shall take some of the bull’s blood, and some of the goat’s blood, and put it around on the horns of the altar.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it ith his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and make it holy from the uncleanness of the children of Israel.
“ When he has finished atoning for the Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions, even all their sins; and he shall put them on the head of the goat, and shall send him aay into the ilderness by the hand of a man ho is ready.
The goat shall carry all their iniquities on himself to a solitary land, and he shall release the goat in the ilderness.
“Aaron shall come into the Tent of Meeting, and shall take off the linen garments hich he put on hen he ent into the Holy Place, and shall leave them there.

Then he shall bathe himself in ater in a holy place, put on his garments, and come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
The fat of the sin offering he shall burn on the altar.
“ He ho lets the goat go as the scapegoat shall ash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in ater, and afterard he shall come into the camp.

The bull for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, hose blood as brought in to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be carried outside the camp; and they shall burn their skins, their flesh, and their dung ith fire.
He ho burns them shall ash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in ater, and afterard he shall come into the camp.

“ It shall be a statute to you forever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no kind of ork, hether native-born or a stranger ho lives as a foreigner among you;
for on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you. You shall be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
It is a Sabbath of solemn rest to you, and you shall afflict your souls. It is a statute forever.
The priest, ho is anointed and ho is consecrated to be priest in his father’s place, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, even the holy garments.

Then he shall make atonement for the Holy Sanctuary; and he shall make atonement for the Tent of Meeting and for the altar; and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
“ This shall be an everlasting statute for you, to make atonement for the children of Israel once in the year because of all their sins.” It as done as the LORD commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“ Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them, ’ This is the thing hich the LORD has commanded:
Whatever man there is of the house of Israel ho kills a bull, or lamb, or goat in the camp, or ho kills it outside the camp,

and hasn’t brought it to the door of the Tent of Meeting to offer it as an offering to the LORD before the LORD’s tabernacle: blood shall be imputed to that man. He has shed blood. That man shall be cut off from among his people.

This is to the end that the children of Israel may bring their sacrifices, hich they sacrifice in the open field, that they may bring them to the LORD, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them for sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood on the LORD’s altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and burn the fat for a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
They shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat idols, after hich they play the prostitute. This shall be a statute forever to them throughout their generations.’
“ You shall say to them, ’ Any man there is of the house of Israel, or of the strangers ho live as foreigners among them, ho offers a burnt offering or sacrifice,
and doesn’t bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting to sacrifice it to the LORD, that man shall be cut off from his people.

“’ Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers ho live as foreigners among them, ho eats any kind of blood, I ill set my face against that soul ho eats blood, and ill cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood. I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
Therefore I have said to the children of Israel, “ No person among you may eat blood, nor may any stranger ho lives as a foreigner among you eat blood.”

“’Whatever man there is of the children of Israel, or of the strangers ho live as foreigners among them, ho takes in hunting any animal or bird that may be eaten, he shall pour out its blood, and cover it ith dust.

For as to the life of all flesh, its blood is ith its life. Therefore I said to the children of Israel, “ You shall not eat the blood of any kind of flesh; for the life of all flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.”

“’ Every person that eats hat dies of itself, or that hich is torn by animals, hether he is native-born or a foreigner, shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the evening. Then he shall be clean.
But if he doesn’t ash them, or bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquity.’”
The LORD said to Moses,
“ Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, ’ I am the LORD your God.
You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, here you lived. You shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, here I am bringing you. You shall not follo their statutes.
You shall do my ordinances. You shall keep my statutes and alk in them. I am the LORD your God.
You shall therefore keep my statutes and my ordinances, hich if a man does, he shall live in them. I am the LORD.
“’ None of you shall approach any close relatives, to uncover their nakedness: I am the LORD.
“’ You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, nor the nakedness of your mother: she is your mother. You shall not uncover her nakedness.
“’ You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s ife. It is your father’s nakedness.
“’ You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother, hether born at home or born abroad.
“’ You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter, or of your daughter’s daughter, even their nakedness; for theirs is your on nakedness.

Yet you ouldn’t go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the LORD your God.
You murmured in your tents, and said, “ Because the LORD hated us, he has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.

Where are e going up? Our brothers have made our heart melt, saying, ’ The people are greater and taller than e. The cities are great and fortified up to the sky. Moreover e have seen the sons of the Anakim there!’”
Then I said to you, “Don’t be terrified. Don’t be afraid of them.
The LORD your God, ho goes before you, he ill fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
and in the ilderness here you have seen ho that the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the ay that you ent, until you came to this place.”
Yet in this thing you didn’t believe the LORD your God,
ho ent before you on the ay, to seek out a place for you to pitch your tents in: in fire by night, to sho you by hat ay you should go, and in the cloud by day.
The LORD heard the voice of your ords and as angry, and sore, saying,
“ Surely not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land hich I sore to give to your fathers,
except Caleb the son of Jephunneh. He shall see it. I ill give the land that he has trodden on to him and to his children, because he has holly folloed the LORD.”
Also the LORD as angry ith me for your sakes, saying, “ You also shall not go in there.
Joshua the son of Nun, ho stands before you, shall go in there. Encourage him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.
Moreover your little ones, hom you said ould be captured or killed, your children, ho today have no knoledge of good or evil, shall go in there. I ill give it to them, and they shall possess it.
But as for you, turn, and take your journey into the ilderness by the ay to the Red Sea.”

Then you ansered and said to me, “ We have sinned against the LORD. We ill go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us.” Every man of you put on his eapons of ar, and presumed to go up into the hill country.
The LORD said to me, “Tell them, ’Don’t go up and don’t fight; for I am not among you, lest you be struck before your enemies.’”
So I spoke to you, and you didn’t listen; but you rebelled against the commandment of the LORD, and ere presumptuous, and ent up into the hill country.
The Amorites, ho lived in that hill country, came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you don in Seir, even to Hormah.
You returned and ept before the LORD, but the LORD didn’t listen to your voice, nor turn his ear to you.
So you stayed in Kadesh many days, according to the days that you remained.
Then e turned, and took our journey into the ilderness by the ay to the Red Sea, as the LORD spoke to me; and e encircled Mount Seir many days.
The LORD spoke to me, saying,
“ You have encircled this mountain long enough. Turn northard.
Command the people, saying, ’ You are to pass through the border of your brothers, the children of Esau, ho dell in Seir; and they ill be afraid of you. Therefore be careful.
Don’t contend ith them; for I ill not give you any of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession.
You shall purchase food from them for money, that you may eat. You shall also buy ater from them for money, that you may drink.’”

For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the ork of your hands. He has knon your alking through this great ilderness. These forty years, the LORD your God has been ith you. You have lacked nothing.
So e passed by from our brothers, the children of Esau, ho dell in Seir, from the ay of the Arabah from Elath and from Ezion Geber. We turned and passed by the ay of the ilderness of Moab.
The LORD said to me, “Don’t bother Moab, neither contend ith them in battle; for I ill not give you any of his land for a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession.”
( The Emim lived there before, a great and numerous people, and tall as the Anakim.
These also are considered to be Rephaim, as the Anakim; but the Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites also lived in Seir in the past, but the children of Esau succeeded them. They destroyed them from before them, and lived in their place, as Israel did to the land of his possession, hich the LORD gave to them.)
“ No rise up and cross over the brook Zered.” We ent over the brook Zered.

The days in hich e came from Kadesh Barnea until e had come over the brook Zered ere thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of ar ere consumed from the middle of the camp, as the LORD sore to them.
Moreover the LORD’s hand as against them, to destroy them from the middle of the camp, until they ere consumed.
So, hen all the men of ar ere consumed and dead from among the people,
the LORD spoke to me, saying,
“ You are to pass over Ar, the border of Moab, today.

When you come near the border of the children of Ammon, don’t bother them, nor contend ith them; for I ill not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession, because I have given it to the children of Lot for a possession.”
( That also is considered a land of Rephaim. Rephaim lived there in the past, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a great people, many, and tall, as the Anakim; but the LORD destroyed them from before Israel, and they succeeded them, and lived in their place,
as he did for the children of Esau ho dell in Seir, hen he destroyed the Horites from before them; and they succeeded them, and lived in their place even to this day.
Then the Avvim, ho lived in villages as far as Gaza: the Caphtorim, ho came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and lived in their place.)

“ Rise up, take your journey, and pass over the valley of the Arnon. Behold, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend ith him in battle.
Today I ill begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples ho are under the hole sky, ho shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you.”
I sent messengers out of the ilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon ith ords of peace, saying,
“ Let me pass through your land. I ill go along by the highay. I ill turn neither to the right hand nor to the left.
You shall sell me food for money, that I may eat; and give me ater for money, that I may drink. Just let me pass through on my feet,
as the children of Esau ho dell in Seir, and the Moabites ho dell in Ar, did to me, until I pass over the Jordan into the land hich the LORD our God gives us.”
But Sihon king of Heshbon ould not let us pass by him, for the LORD your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into your hand, as it is today.
The LORD said to me, “ Behold, I have begun to deliver up Sihon and his land before you. Begin to possess, that you may inherit his land.”
Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz.
The LORD our God delivered him up before us; and e struck him, his sons, and all his people.
We took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed every inhabited city, ith the omen and the little ones. We left no one remaining.
Only the livestock e took for plunder for ourselves, ith the plunder of the cities hich e had taken.
From Aroer, hich is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the valley, even to Gilead, there as not a city too high for us. The LORD our God delivered up all before us.
Only to the land of the children of Ammon you didn’t come near: all the banks of the river Jabbok, and the cities of the hill country, and herever the LORD our God forbade us.
Then e turned, and ent up the ay to Bashan. Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, “Don’t fear him; for I have delivered him, ith all his people and his land, into your hand. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, ho lived at Heshbon.”
So the LORD our God also delivered into our hand Og, the king of Bashan, and all his people. We struck him until no one as left to him remaining.
We took all his cities at that time. There as not a city hich e didn’t take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these ere cities fortified ith high alls, gates, and bars, in addition to a great many villages ithout alls.
We utterly destroyed them, as e did to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying every inhabited city, ith the omen and the little ones.
But all the livestock, and the plunder of the cities, e took for plunder for ourselves.
We took the land at that time out of the hand of the to kings of the Amorites ho ere beyond the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon.
( The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
We took all the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, to Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

( For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. Behold, his bedstead as a bedstead of iron. Isn’t it in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits as its length, and four cubits its idth, after the cubit of a man.)
This land e took in possession at that time: from Aroer, hich is by the valley of the Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead ith its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites;
and the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh— all the region of Argob, even all Bashan. ( The same is called the land of Rephaim.
Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them, even Bashan, after his on name, Havvoth Jair, to this day.)
I gave Gilead to Machir.

To the Reubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gilead even to the valley of the Arnon, the middle of the valley, and its border, even to the river Jabbok, hich is the border of the children of Ammon;
the Arabah also, and the Jordan and its border, from Chinnereth even to the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah eastard.
I commanded you at that time, saying, “ The LORD your God has given you this land to possess it. All of you men of valor shall pass over armed before your brothers, the children of Israel.
But your ives, and your little ones, and your livestock, ( I kno that you have much livestock), shall live in your cities hich I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your brothers, as to you, and they also possess the land hich the LORD your God gives them beyond the Jordan. Then you shall each return to his on possession, hich I have given you.”
I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, “ Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these to kings. So shall the LORD do to all the kingdoms here you go over.
You shall not fear them; for the LORD your God himself fights for you.”
I begged GOD at that time, saying,
“ Lord GOD, you have begun to sho your servant your greatness, and your strong hand. For hat god is there in heaven or in earth that can do orks like yours, and mighty acts like yours?
Please let me go over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that fine mountain, and Lebanon.”
But the LORD as angry ith me because of you, and didn’t listen to me. The LORD said to me, “ That is enough! Speak no more to me of this matter.
Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes estard, and northard, and southard, and eastard, and see ith your eyes; for you shall not go over this Jordan.
But commission Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land hich you shall see.”
So e stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.
No, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances hich I teach you, to do them, that you may live and go in and possess the land hich the LORD, the God of your fathers, gives you.
You shall not add to the ord hich I command you, neither shall you take aay from it, that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God hich I command you.
Your eyes have seen hat the LORD did because of Baal Peor; for the LORD your God has destroyed all the men ho folloed Baal Peor from among you.
But you ho ere faithful to the LORD your God are all alive today.
Behold, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, even as the LORD my God commanded me, that you should do so in the middle of the land here you go in to possess it.

Keep therefore and do them; for this is your isdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples ho shall hear all these statutes and say, “ Surely this great nation is a ise and understanding people.”
For hat great nation is there that has a god so near to them as the LORD our God is henever e call on him?
What great nation is there that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this la hich I set before you today?

Only be careful, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things hich your eyes sa, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; but make them knon to your children and your children’s children—

the day that you stood before the LORD your God in Horeb, hen the LORD said to me, “ Assemble the people to me, and I ill make them hear my ords, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children.”
You came near and stood under the mountain. The mountain burned ith fire to the heart of the sky, ith darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
The LORD spoke to you out of the middle of the fire: you heard the voice of ords, but you sa no form; you only heard a voice.
He declared to you his covenant, hich he commanded you to perform, even the ten commandments. He rote them on to stone tablets.
The LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might do them in the land here you go over to possess it.
Be very careful, for you sa no kind of form on the day that the LORD spoke to you in Horeb out of the middle of the fire,
lest you corrupt yourselves, and make yourself a carved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any inged bird that flies in the sky,
the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the ater under the earth;

and lest you lift up your eyes to the sky, and hen you see the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the army of the sky, you are dran aay and orship them, and serve them, hich the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under the hole sky.
But the LORD has taken you, and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be to him a people of inheritance, as it is today.
Furthermore the LORD as angry ith me for your sakes, and sore that I should not go over the Jordan, and that I should not go in to that good land hich the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance;
but I must die in this land. I must not go over the Jordan, but you shall go over and possess that good land.
Be careful, lest you forget the covenant of the LORD your God, hich he made ith you, and make yourselves a carved image in the form of anything hich the LORD your God has forbidden you.
For the LORD your God is a devouring fire, a jealous God.

When you father children and children’s children, and you have been long in the land, and then corrupt yourselves, and make a carved image in the form of anything, and do that hich is evil in the LORD your God’s sight to provoke him to anger,

I call heaven and earth to itness against you today, that you ill soon utterly perish from off the land hich you go over the Jordan to possess it. You ill not prolong your days on it, but ill utterly be destroyed.
The LORD ill scatter you among the peoples, and you ill be left fe in number among the nations here the LORD ill lead you aay.
There you ill serve gods, the ork of men’s hands, ood and stone, hich neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
But from there you shall seek the LORD your God, and you ill find him hen you search after him ith all your heart and ith all your soul.
When you are in oppression, and all these things have come on you, in the latter days you shall return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
For the LORD your God is a merciful God. He ill not fail you nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers hich he sore to them.

For ask no of the days that are past, hich ere before you, since the day that God created man on the earth, and from the one end of the sky to the other, hether there has been anything as great as this thing is, or has been heard like it?
Did a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the middle of the fire, as you have heard, and live?

Or has God tried to go and take a nation for himself from among another nation, by trials, by signs, by onders, by ar, by a mighty hand, by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
It as shon to you so that you might kno that the LORD is God. There is no one else besides him.
Out of heaven he made you to hear his voice, that he might instruct you. On earth he made you to see his great fire; and you heard his ords out of the middle of the fire.
Because he loved your fathers, therefore he chose their offspring after them, and brought you out ith his presence, ith his great poer, out of Egypt;
to drive out nations from before you greater and mightier than you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as it is today.
Kno therefore today, and take it to heart, that the LORD himself is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath. There is no one else.

You shall keep his statutes and his commandments hich I command you today, that it may go ell ith you and ith your children after you, and that you may prolong your days in the land hich the LORD your God gives you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toard the sunrise,
that the man slayer might flee there, ho kills his neighbor unintentionally and didn’t hate him in time past, and that fleeing to one of these cities he might live:
Bezer in the ilderness, in the plain country, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the la hich Moses set before the children of Israel.
These are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances hich Moses spoke to the children of Israel hen they came out of Egypt,
beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, ho lived at Heshbon, hom Moses and the children of Israel struck hen they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the to kings of the Amorites, ho ere beyond the Jordan toard the sunrise;
from Aroer, hich is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, even to Mount Siyon ( also called Hermon),
and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastard, even to the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses called to all Israel, and said to them, “ Hear, Israel, the statutes and the ordinances hich I speak in your ears today, that you may learn them, and observe to do them.”
The LORD our God made a covenant ith us in Horeb.
The LORD didn’t make this covenant ith our fathers, but ith us, even us, ho are all of us here alive today.
The LORD spoke ith you face to face on the mountain out of the middle of the fire,
( I stood beteen the LORD and you at that time, to sho you the LORD’s ord; for you ere afraid because of the fire, and didn’t go up onto the mountain) saying,
“ I am the LORD your God, ho brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
“ You shall have no other gods before me.
“ You shall not make a carved image for yourself— any likeness of hat is in heaven above, or hat is on the earth beneath, or that is in the ater under the earth.

You shall not bo yourself don to them, nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children and on the third and on the fourth generation of those ho hate me
and shoing loving kindness to thousands of those ho love me and keep my commandments.
“ You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God; for the LORD ill not hold him guiltless ho misuses his name.
“ Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
You shall labor six days, and do all your ork;

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, in hich you shall not do any ork— neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor your stranger ho is ithin your gates; that your male servant and your female servant may rest as ell as you.

You shall remember that you ere a servant in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
“ Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, that your days may be long and that it may go ell ith you in the land hich the LORD your God gives you.
“ You shall not murder.
“ You shall not commit adultery.
“ You shall not steal.
“ You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.

“ You shall not covet your neighbor’s ife. Neither shall you desire your neighbor’s house, his field, or his male servant, or his female servant, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor’s.”

The LORD spoke these ords to all your assembly on the mountain out of the middle of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, ith a great voice. He added no more. He rote them on to stone tablets, and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice out of the middle of the darkness, hile the mountain as burning ith fire, you came near to me, even all the heads of your tribes, and your elders;

and you said, “ Behold, the LORD our God has shon us his glory and his greatness, and e have heard his voice out of the middle of the fire. We have seen today that God does speak ith man, and he lives.
No therefore, hy should e die? For this great fire ill consume us. If e hear the LORD our God’s voice any more, then e shall die.
For ho is there of all flesh ho has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the middle of the fire, as e have, and lived?
Go near, and hear all that the LORD our God shall say, and tell us all that the LORD our God tells you; and e ill hear it, and do it.”

The LORD heard the voice of your ords hen you spoke to me; and the LORD said to me, “ I have heard the voice of the ords of this people hich they have spoken to you. They have ell said all that they have spoken.
Oh that there ere such a heart in them that they ould fear me and keep all my commandments alays, that it might be ell ith them and ith their children forever!
“ Go tell them, ’ Return to your tents.’

But as for you, stand here by me, and I ill tell you all the commandments, and the statutes, and the ordinances, hich you shall teach them, that they may do them in the land hich I give them to possess.”
You shall observe to do therefore as the LORD your God has commanded you. You shall not turn aay to the right hand or to the left.
You shall alk in all the ay hich the LORD your God has commanded you, that you may live and that it may be ell ith you, and that you may prolong your days in the land hich you shall possess.
No these are the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances, hich the LORD your God commanded to teach you, that you might do them in the land that you go over to possess;

that you might fear the LORD your God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments, hich I command you— you, your son, and your son’s son, all the days of your life; and that your days may be prolonged.

Hear therefore, Israel, and observe to do it, that it may be ell ith you, and that you may increase mightily, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised to you, in a land floing ith milk and honey.
Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God. The LORD is one.
You shall love the LORD your God ith all your heart, ith all your soul, and ith all your might.
These ords, hich I command you today, shall be on your heart;
and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them hen you sit in your house, and hen you alk by the ay, and hen you lie don, and hen you rise up.
You shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets beteen your eyes.
You shall rite them on the door posts of your house and on your gates.
It shall be, hen the LORD your God brings you into the land hich he sore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give you, great and goodly cities hich you didn’t build,
and houses full of all good things hich you didn’t fill, and cisterns dug out hich you didn’t dig, vineyards and olive trees hich you didn’t plant, and you shall eat and be full;
then beare lest you forget the LORD, ho brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
You shall fear the LORD your God; and you shall serve him, and shall sear by his name.
You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples ho are around you,
for the LORD your God among you is a jealous God, lest the anger of the LORD your God be kindled against you, and he destroy you from off the face of the earth.
You shall not tempt the LORD your God, as you tempted him in Massah.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, hich he has commanded you.
You shall do that hich is right and good in the LORD’s sight, that it may be ell ith you and that you may go in and possess the good land hich the LORD sore to your fathers,
to thrust out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.
When your son asks you in time to come, saying, “ What do the testimonies, the statutes, and the ordinances, hich the LORD our God has commanded you mean?”
then you shall tell your son, “We ere Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt. The LORD brought us out of Egypt ith a mighty hand;
and the LORD shoed great and aesome signs and onders on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on all his house, before our eyes;
and he brought us out from there, that he might bring us in, to give us the land hich he sore to our fathers.
The LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good alays, that he might preserve us alive, as e are today.
It shall be righteousness to us, if e observe to do all these commandments before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us.”

When the LORD your God brings you into the land here you go to possess it, and casts out many nations before you— the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite— seven nations greater and mightier than you;
and hen the LORD your God delivers them up before you, and you strike them, then you shall utterly destroy them. You shall make no covenant ith them, nor sho mercy to them.
You shall not make marriages ith them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor shall you take his daughter for your son.
For that ould turn aay your sons from folloing me, that they may serve other gods. So the LORD’s anger ould be kindled against you, and he ould destroy you quickly.
But you shall deal ith them like this: you shall break don their altars, dash their pillars in pieces, cut don their Asherah poles, and burn their engraved images ith fire.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for his on possession, above all peoples ho are on the face of the earth.
The LORD didn’t set his love on you nor choose you, because you ere more in number than any people; for you ere the feest of all peoples;

but because the LORD loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath hich he sore to your fathers, the LORD has brought you out ith a mighty hand and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Kno therefore that the LORD your God himself is God, the faithful God, ho keeps covenant and loving kindness to a thousand generations ith those ho love him and keep his commandments,
and repays those ho hate him to their face, to destroy them. He ill not be slack to him ho hates him. He ill repay him to his face.
You shall therefore keep the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances hich I command you today, to do them.
It shall happen, because you listen to these ordinances and keep and do them, that the LORD your God ill keep ith you the covenant and the loving kindness hich he sore to your fathers.

He ill love you, bless you, and multiply you. He ill also bless the fruit of your body and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your ne ine and your oil, the increase of your livestock and the young of your flock, in the land hich he sore to your fathers to give you.
You ill be blessed above all peoples. There on’t be male or female barren among you, or among your livestock.
The LORD ill take aay from you all sickness; and he ill put none of the evil diseases of Egypt, hich you kno, on you, but ill lay them on all those ho hate you.
You shall consume all the peoples hom the LORD your God shall deliver to you. Your eye shall not pity them. You shall not serve their gods; for that ould be a snare to you.
If you shall say in your heart, “These nations are more than I; ho can I dispossess them?”
you shall not be afraid of them. You shall remember ell hat the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

the great trials hich your eyes sa, the signs, the onders, the mighty hand, and the outstretched arm, by hich the LORD your God brought you out. So shall the LORD your God do to all the peoples of hom you are afraid.
Moreover the LORD your God ill send the hornet among them, until those ho are left, and hide themselves, perish from before you.
You shall not be scared of them; for the LORD your God is among you, a great and aesome God.
The LORD your God ill cast out those nations before you little by little. You may not consume them at once, lest the animals of the field increase on you.
But the LORD your God ill deliver them up before you, and ill confuse them ith a great confusion, until they are destroyed.

No, Israel, hat does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to alk in all his ays, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God ith all your heart and ith all your soul,

Kno this day— for I don’t speak ith your children ho have not knon, and ho have not seen the chastisement of the LORD your God, his greatness, his mighty hand, his outstretched arm,
his signs, and his orks, hich he did in the middle of Egypt to Pharaoh the king of Egypt, and to all his land;

Therefore you shall keep the entire commandment hich I command you today, that you may be strong, and go in and possess the land that you go over to possess;
