You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God, of the flock and the herd, in the place hich the LORD shall choose to cause his name to dell there.

You shall eat no leavened bread ith it. You shall eat unleavened bread ith it seven days, even the bread of affliction ( for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste) that you may remember the day hen you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
No yeast shall be seen ith you in all your borders seven days; neither shall any of the meat, hich you sacrifice the first day at evening, remain all night until the morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover ithin any of your gates hich the LORD your God gives you;

but at the place hich the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dell in, there you shall sacrifice the Passover at evening, at the going don of the sun, at the season that you came out of Egypt.
You shall roast and eat it in the place hich the LORD your God chooses. In the morning you shall return to your tents.
Six days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God. You shall do no ork.
You shall count for yourselves seven eeks. From the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven eeks.
You shall keep the feast of eeks to the LORD your God ith a tribute of a free ill offering of your hand, hich you shall give according to ho the LORD your God blesses you.

You shall rejoice before the LORD your God: you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite ho is ithin your gates, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the ido ho are among you, in the place hich the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dell there.
You shall remember that you ere a slave in Egypt. You shall observe and do these statutes.
You shall keep the feast of booths seven days, after you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your ine press.
You shall rejoice in your feast, you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the ido ho are ithin your gates.

You shall keep a feast to the LORD your God seven days in the place hich the LORD chooses, because the LORD your God ill bless you in all your increase and in all the ork of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

Three times in a year all of your males shall appear before the LORD your God in the place hich he chooses: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of eeks, and in the feast of booths. They shall not appear before the LORD empty.
Every man shall give as he is able, according to the LORD your God’s blessing hich he has given you.
You shall make judges and officers in all your gates, hich the LORD your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people ith righteous judgment.
You shall not pervert justice. You shall not sho partiality. You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the ise and perverts the ords of the righteous.
You shall follo that hich is altogether just, that you may live and inherit the land hich the LORD your God gives you.
You shall not plant for yourselves an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the LORD your God’s altar, hich you shall make for yourselves.
Neither shall you set yourself up a sacred stone hich the LORD your God hates.
You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep in hich is a defect or anything evil; for that is an abomination to the LORD your God.
If there is found among you, ithin any of your gates hich the LORD your God gives you, a man or oman ho does that hich is evil in the LORD your God’s sight in transgressing his covenant,
and has gone and served other gods and orshiped them, or the sun, or the moon, or any of the stars of the sky, hich I have not commanded,
and you are told, and you have heard of it, then you shall inquire diligently. Behold, if it is true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is done in Israel,
then you shall bring out that man or that oman ho has done this evil thing to your gates, even that same man or oman; and you shall stone them to death ith stones.
At the mouth of to itnesses, or three itnesses, he ho is to die shall be put to death. At the mouth of one itness he shall not be put to death.
The hands of the itnesses shall be first on him to put him to death, and afterard the hands of all the people. So you shall remove the evil from among you.

If there arises a matter too hard for you in judgment, beteen blood and blood, beteen plea and plea, and beteen stroke and stroke, being matters of controversy ithin your gates, then you shall arise, and go up to the place hich the LORD your God chooses.
You shall come to the priests ho are Levites and to the judge ho shall be in those days. You shall inquire, and they shall give you the verdict.
You shall do according to the decisions of the verdict hich they shall give you from that place hich the LORD chooses. You shall observe to do according to all that they shall teach you.

According to the decisions of the la hich they shall teach you, and according to the judgment hich they shall tell you, you shall do. You shall not turn aay from the sentence hich they announce to you, to the right hand, nor to the left.
The man ho does presumptuously in not listening to the priest ho stands to minister there before the LORD your God, or to the judge, even that man shall die. You shall put aay the evil from Israel.
All the people shall hear and fear, and do no more presumptuously.
When you have come to the land hich the LORD your God gives you, and possess it and dell in it, and say, “ I ill set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me,”

you shall surely set him hom the LORD your God chooses as king over yourselves. You shall set as king over you one from among your brothers. You may not put a foreigner over you, ho is not your brother.

Only he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt, to the end that he may multiply horses; because the LORD has said to you, “ You shall not go back that ay again.”
He shall not multiply ives to himself, that his heart not turn aay. He shall not greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.
It shall be, hen he sits on the throne of his kingdom, that he shall rite himself a copy of this la in a book, out of that hich is before the Levitical priests.
It shall be ith him, and he shall read from it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the ords of this la and these statutes, to do them;

that his heart not be lifted up above his brothers, and that he not turn aay from the commandment to the right hand, or to the left, to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the middle of Israel.
The priests and the Levites— all the tribe of Levi— shall have no portion nor inheritance ith Israel. They shall eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire and his portion.
They shall have no inheritance among their brothers. The LORD is their inheritance, as he has spoken to them.
This shall be the priests’ due from the people, from those ho offer a sacrifice, hether it be ox or sheep, that they shall give to the priest: the shoulder, the to cheeks, and the inner parts.
You shall give him the first fruits of your grain, of your ne ine, and of your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep.
For the LORD your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand to minister in the LORD’s name, him and his sons forever.
If a Levite comes from any of your gates out of all Israel here he lives, and comes ith all the desire of his soul to the place hich the LORD shall choose,
then he shall minister in the name of the LORD his God, as all his brothers the Levites do, ho stand there before the LORD.
They shall have like portions to eat, in addition to that hich comes from the sale of his family possessions.
When you have come into the land hich the LORD your God gives you, you shall not learn to imitate the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found ith you anyone ho makes his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, one ho uses divination, one ho tells fortunes, or an enchanter, or a sorcerer,
or a charmer, or someone ho consults ith a familiar spirit, or a izard, or a necromancer.
For hoever does these things is an abomination to the LORD. Because of these abominations, the LORD your God drives them out from before you.
You shall be blameless ith the LORD your God.
For these nations that you shall dispossess listen to those ho practice sorcery and to diviners; but as for you, the LORD your God has not alloed you so to do.
The LORD your God ill raise up to you a prophet from among you, of your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him.

This is according to all that you desired of the LORD your God in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, “ Let me not hear again the LORD my God’s voice, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I not die.”
The LORD said to me, “ They have ell said that hich they have spoken.
I ill raise them up a prophet from among their brothers, like you. I ill put my ords in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I shall command him.
It shall happen, that hoever ill not listen to my ords hich he shall speak in my name, I ill require it of him.
But the prophet ho speaks a ord presumptuously in my name, hich I have not commanded him to speak, or ho speaks in the name of other gods, that same prophet shall die.”
You may say in your heart, “ Ho shall e kno the ord hich the LORD has not spoken?”

When a prophet speaks in the LORD’s name, if the thing doesn’t follo, nor happen, that is the thing hich the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You shall not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God cuts off the nations hose land the LORD your God gives you, and you succeed them and dell in their cities and in their houses,
you shall set apart three cities for yourselves in the middle of your land, hich the LORD your God gives you to possess.
You shall prepare the ay, and divide the borders of your land hich the LORD your God causes you to inherit into three parts, that every man slayer may flee there.
This is the case of the man slayer ho shall flee there and live: Whoever kills his neighbor unintentionally, and didn’t hate him in time past—

as hen a man goes into the forest ith his neighbor to chop ood and his hand sings the ax to cut don the tree, and the head slips from the handle and hits his neighbor so that he dies— he shall flee to one of these cities and live.

Otherise, the avenger of blood might pursue the man slayer hile hot anger is in his heart and overtake him, because the ay is long, and strike him mortally, even though he as not orthy of death, because he didn’t hate him in time past.
Therefore I command you to set apart three cities for yourselves.
If the LORD your God enlarges your border, as he has sorn to your fathers, and gives you all the land hich he promised to give to your fathers;

and if you keep all this commandment to do it, hich I command you today, to love the LORD your God, and to alk ever in his ays, then you shall add three cities more for yourselves, in addition to these three.
This is so that innocent blood ill not be shed in the middle of your land hich the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance, leaving blood guilt on you.
But if any man hates his neighbor, lies in ait for him, rises up against him, strikes him mortally so that he dies, and he flees into one of these cities;
then the elders of his city shall send and bring him there, and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.
Your eye shall not pity him, but you shall purge the innocent blood from Israel that it may go ell ith you.
You shall not remove your neighbor’s landmark, hich they of old time have set, in your inheritance hich you shall inherit, in the land that the LORD your God gives you to possess.
One itness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin that he sins. At the mouth of to itnesses, or at the mouth of three itnesses, shall a matter be established.
If an unrighteous itness rises up against any man to testify against him of rongdoing,
then both the men, beteen hom the controversy is, shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges ho shall be in those days;
and the judges shall make diligent inquisition; and behold, if the itness is a false itness, and has testified falsely against his brother,
then you shall do to him as he had thought to do to his brother. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
Those ho remain shall hear, and fear, and ill never again commit any such evil among you.
Your eyes shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see horses, chariots, and a people more numerous than you, you shall not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, ho brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is ith you.
It shall be, hen you dra near to the battle, that the priest shall approach and speak to the people,
and shall tell them, “ Hear, Israel, you dra near today to battle against your enemies. Don’t let your heart faint! Don’t be afraid, nor tremble, neither be scared of them;
for the LORD your God is he ho goes ith you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

The officers shall speak to the people, saying, “ What man is there ho has built a ne house, and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.
What man is there ho has planted a vineyard, and has not used its fruit? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man use its fruit.
What man is there ho has pledged to be married to a ife, and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her.”

The officers shall speak further to the people, and they shall say, “ What man is there ho is fearful and faint-hearted? Let him go and return to his house, lest his brother’s heart melt as his heart.”
It shall be, hen the officers have finished speaking to the people, that they shall appoint captains of armies at the head of the people.
When you dra near to a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace to it.
It shall be, if it gives you anser of peace and opens to you, then it shall be that all the people ho are found therein shall become forced laborers to you, and shall serve you.
If it ill make no peace ith you, but ill make ar against you, then you shall besiege it.
When the LORD your God delivers it into your hand, you shall strike every male of it ith the edge of the sord;

but the omen, the little ones, the livestock, and all that is in the city, even all its plunder, you shall take for plunder for yourself. You may use the plunder of your enemies, hich the LORD your God has given you.
Thus you shall do to all the cities hich are very far off from you, hich are not of the cities of these nations.
But of the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance, you shall save alive nothing that breathes;
but you shall utterly destroy them: the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, as the LORD your God has commanded you;
that they not teach you to follo all their abominations, hich they have done for their gods; so ould you sin against the LORD your God.

When you shall besiege a city a long time, in making ar against it to take it, you shall not destroy its trees by ielding an ax against them; for you may eat of them. You shall not cut them don, for is the tree of the field man, that it should be besieged by you?
Only the trees that you kno are not trees for food, you shall destroy and cut them don. You shall build bularks against the city that makes ar ith you, until it falls.
If someone is found slain in the land hich the LORD your God gives you to possess, lying in the field, and it isn’t knon ho has struck him,
then your elders and your judges shall come out, and they shall measure to the cities hich are around him ho is slain.
It shall be that the elders of the city hich is nearest to the slain man shall take a heifer of the herd, hich hasn’t been orked ith and hich has not dran in the yoke.
The elders of that city shall bring the heifer don to a valley ith running ater, hich is neither ploed nor son, and shall break the heifer’s neck there in the valley.

The priests the sons of Levi shall come near, for them the LORD your God has chosen to minister to him, and to bless in the LORD’s name; and according to their ord shall every controversy and every assault be decided.
All the elders of that city hich is nearest to the slain man shall ash their hands over the heifer hose neck as broken in the valley.
They shall anser and say, “ Our hands have not shed this blood, neither have our eyes seen it.
Forgive, LORD, your people Israel, hom you have redeemed, and don’t allo innocent blood among your people Israel.” The blood shall be forgiven them.
So you shall put aay the innocent blood from among you, hen you shall do that hich is right in the LORD’s eyes.
When you go out to battle against your enemies, and the LORD your God delivers them into your hands and you carry them aay captive,
and see among the captives a beautiful oman, and you are attracted to her, and desire to take her as your ife,
then you shall bring her home to your house. She shall shave her head and trim her nails.

She shall take off the clothing of her captivity, and shall remain in your house, and beail her father and her mother a full month. After that you shall go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your ife.

It shall be, if you have no delight in her, then you shall let her go here she desires; but you shall not sell her at all for money. You shall not deal ith her as a slave, because you have humbled her.
If a man has to ives, the one beloved and the other hated, and they have borne him children, both the beloved and the hated, and if the firstborn son is hers ho as hated,

then it shall be, in the day that he causes his sons to inherit that hich he has, that he may not give the son of the beloved the rights of the firstborn before the son of the hated, ho is the firstborn;
but he shall acknoledge the firstborn, the son of the hated, by giving him a double portion of all that he has; for he is the beginning of his strength. The right of the firstborn is his.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son ho ill not obey the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and though they chasten him, ill not listen to them,
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.
They shall tell the elders of his city, “ This our son is stubborn and rebellious. He ill not obey our voice. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
All the men of his city shall stone him to death ith stones. So you shall remove the evil from among you. All Israel shall hear, and fear.
If a man has committed a sin orthy of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his body shall not remain all night on the tree, but you shall surely bury him the same day; for he ho is hanged is accursed of God. Don’t defile your land hich the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance.
You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep go astray and hide yourself from them. You shall surely bring them again to your brother.

If your brother isn’t near to you, or if you don’t kno him, then you shall bring it home to your house, and it shall be ith you until your brother comes looking for it, and you shall restore it to him.
So you shall do ith his donkey. So you shall do ith his garment. So you shall do ith every lost thing of your brother’s, hich he has lost and you have found. You may not hide yourself.
You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen don by the ay, and hide yourself from them. You shall surely help him to lift them up again.
A oman shall not ear men’s clothing, neither shall a man put on omen’s clothing; for hoever does these things is an abomination to the LORD your God.
If you come across a bird’s nest on the ay, in any tree or on the ground, ith young ones or eggs, and the hen sitting on the young, or on the eggs, you shall not take the hen ith the young.
You shall surely let the hen go, but the young you may take for yourself, that it may be ell ith you, and that you may prolong your days.
When you build a ne house, then you shall make a railing around your roof, so that you don’t bring blood on your house if anyone falls from there.
You shall not so your vineyard ith to kinds of seed, lest all the fruit be defiled, the seed hich you have son, and the increase of the vineyard.
You shall not plo ith an ox and a donkey together.
You shall not ear clothes of ool and linen oven together.
You shall make yourselves fringes on the four corners of your cloak ith hich you cover yourself.
If any man takes a ife, and goes in to her, hates her,
accuses her of shameful things, gives her a bad name, and says, “ I took this oman, and hen I came near to her, I didn’t find in her the tokens of virginity;”
then the young lady’s father and mother shall take and bring the tokens of the young lady’s virginity to the elders of the city in the gate.
The young lady’s father shall tell the elders, “ I gave my daughter to this man as his ife, and he hates her.

Behold, he has accused her of shameful things, saying, ’ I didn’t find in your daughter the tokens of virginity;’ and yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity.” They shall spread the cloth before the elders of the city.
The elders of that city shall take the man and chastise him.

They shall fine him one hundred shekels of silver, and give them to the father of the young lady, because he has given a bad name to a virgin of Israel. She shall be his ife. He may not put her aay all his days.
But if this thing is true, that the tokens of virginity ere not found in the young lady,

then they shall bring out the young lady to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death ith stones, because she has done folly in Israel, to play the prostitute in her father’s house. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
If a man is found lying ith a oman married to a husband, then they shall both die, the man ho lay ith the oman and the oman. So you shall remove the evil from Israel.
If there is a young lady ho is a virgin pledged to be married to a husband, and a man finds her in the city, and lies ith her,

then you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city, and you shall stone them to death ith stones; the lady, because she didn’t cry, being in the city; and the man, because he has humbled his neighbor’s ife. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
But if the man finds the lady ho is pledged to be married in the field, and the man forces her and lies ith her, then only the man ho lay ith her shall die;
but to the lady you shall do nothing. There is in the lady no sin orthy of death; for as hen a man rises against his neighbor and kills him, even so is this matter;
for he found her in the field, the pledged to be married lady cried, and there as no one to save her.
If a man finds a lady ho is a virgin, ho is not pledged to be married, grabs her and lies ith her, and they are found,
then the man ho lay ith her shall give to the lady’s father fifty shekels of silver. She shall be his ife, because he has humbled her. He may not put her aay all his days.
A man shall not take his father’s ife, and shall not uncover his father’s skirt.
He ho is emasculated by crushing or cutting shall not enter into the LORD’s assembly.
A person born of a forbidden union shall not enter into the LORD’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall no one of his enter into the LORD’s assembly.
An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the LORD’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall no one belonging to them enter into the LORD’s assembly forever,
because they didn’t meet you ith bread and ith ater on the ay hen you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you.
Nevertheless the LORD your God ouldn’t listen to Balaam, but the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing to you, because the LORD your God loved you.
You shall not seek their peace nor their prosperity all your days forever.
You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
The children of the third generation ho are born to them may enter into the LORD’s assembly.
When you go out and camp against your enemies, then you shall keep yourselves from every evil thing.
If there is among you any man ho is not clean by reason of that hich happens to him by night, then shall he go outside of the camp. He shall not come ithin the camp;
but it shall be, hen evening comes, he shall bathe himself in ater. When the sun is don, he shall come ithin the camp.
You shall have a place also outside of the camp here you go relieve yourself.
You shall have a troel among your eapons. It shall be, hen you relieve yourself, you shall dig ith it, and shall turn back and cover your excrement;

for the LORD your God alks in the middle of your camp, to deliver you, and to give up your enemies before you. Therefore your camp shall be holy, that he may not see an unclean thing in you, and turn aay from you.
You shall not deliver to his master a servant ho has escaped from his master to you.
He shall dell ith you, among you, in the place hich he shall choose ithin one of your gates, here it pleases him best. You shall not oppress him.
There shall be no prostitute of the daughters of Israel, neither shall there be a sodomite of the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, or the ages of a male prostitute, into the house of the LORD your God for any vo; for both of these are an abomination to the LORD your God.
You shall not lend on interest to your brother: interest of money, interest of food, interest of anything that is lent on interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest; but you shall not charge your brother interest, that the LORD your God may bless you in all that you put your hand to, in the land here you go in to possess it.
When you vo a vo to the LORD your God, you shall not be slack to pay it, for the LORD your God ill surely require it of you; and it ould be sin in you.
But if you refrain from making a vo, it shall be no sin in you.
You shall observe and do that hich has gone out of your lips. Whatever you have voed to the LORD your God as a free ill offering, hich you have promised ith your mouth, you must do.
When you come into your neighbor’s vineyard, then you may eat your fill of grapes at your on pleasure; but you shall not put any in your container.
When you come into your neighbor’s standing grain, then you may pluck the ears ith your hand; but you shall not use a sickle on your neighbor’s standing grain.

When a man takes a ife and marries her, then it shall be, if she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall rite her a certificate of divorce, put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
When she has departed out of his house, she may go and be another man’s ife.
If the latter husband hates her, and rites her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house; or if the latter husband dies, ho took her to be his ife;

her former husband, ho sent her aay, may not take her again to be his ife after she is defiled; for that ould be an abomination to the LORD. You shall not cause the land to sin, hich the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance.
When a man takes a ne ife, he shall not go out in the army, neither shall he be assigned any business. He shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer his ife hom he has taken.
No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge, for he takes a life in pledge.
If a man is found stealing any of his brothers of the children of Israel, and he deals ith him as a slave, or sells him, then that thief shall die. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
Be careful in the plague of leprosy, that you observe diligently and do according to all that the Levitical priests teach you. As I commanded them, so you shall observe to do.
Remember hat the LORD your God did to Miriam, by the ay as you came out of Egypt.
When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man to hom you lend shall bring the pledge outside to you.
If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep ith his pledge.
You shall surely restore to him the pledge hen the sun goes don, that he may sleep in his garment and bless you. It shall be righteousness to you before the LORD your God.
You shall not oppress a hired servant ho is poor and needy, hether he is one of your brothers or one of the foreigners ho are in your land ithin your gates.
In his day you shall give him his ages, neither shall the sun go don on it, for he is poor and sets his heart on it, lest he cry against you to the LORD, and it be sin to you.
The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers. Every man shall be put to death for his on sin.
You shall not deprive the foreigner or the fatherless of justice, nor take a ido’s clothing in pledge;
but you shall remember that you ere a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you there. Therefore I command you to do this thing.

When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the ido, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the ork of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the ido.
When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean it after yourselves. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the ido.
You shall remember that you ere a slave in the land of Egypt. Therefore I command you to do this thing.
If there is a controversy beteen men, and they come to judgment and the judges judge them, then they shall justify the righteous and condemn the icked.
It shall be, if the icked man is orthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie don and to be beaten before his face, according to his ickedness, by number.
He may sentence him to no more than forty stripes. He shall not give more, lest if he should give more and beat him more than that many stripes, then your brother ill be degraded in your sight.
You shall not muzzle the ox hen he treads out the grain.

If brothers dell together, and one of them dies and has no son, the ife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and take her as his ife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.
It shall be that the firstborn hom she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother ho is dead, that his name not be blotted out of Israel.

If the man doesn’t ant to take his brother’s ife, then his brother’s ife shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, “ My husband’s brother refuses to raise up to his brother a name in Israel. He ill not perform the duty of a husband’s brother to me.”
Then the elders of his city shall call him, and speak to him. If he stands and says, “ I don’t ant to take her,”

then his brother’s ife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and loose his sandal from off his foot, and spit in his face. She shall anser and say, “ So shall it be done to the man ho does not build up his brother’s house.”
His name shall be called in Israel, “ The house of him ho had his sandal removed.”
When men strive against each other, and the ife of one dras near to deliver her husband out of the hand of him ho strikes him, and puts out her hand, and grabs him by his private parts,
then you shall cut off her hand. Your eye shall have no pity.
You shall not have in your bag diverse eights, one heavy and one light.
You shall not have in your house diverse measures, one large and one small.
You shall have a perfect and just eight. You shall have a perfect and just measure, that your days may be long in the land hich the LORD your God gives you.
For all ho do such things, all ho do unrighteously, are an abomination to the LORD your God.
Remember hat Amalek did to you by the ay as you came out of Egypt,
ho he met you by the ay, and struck the rearmost of you, all ho ere feeble behind you, hen you ere faint and eary; and he didn’t fear God.

Therefore it shall be, hen the LORD your God has given you rest from all your enemies all around, in the land hich the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance to possess it, that you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky. You shall not forget.
It shall be, hen you have come in to the land hich the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance, possess it, and dell in it,

that you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground, hich you shall bring in from your land that the LORD your God gives you. You shall put it in a basket, and shall go to the place hich the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dell there.
You shall come to the priest ho shall be in those days, and tell him, “ I profess today to the LORD your God, that I have come to the land hich the LORD sore to our fathers to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket out of your hand, and set it don before the LORD your God’s altar.
You shall anser and say before the LORD your God, “ My father as a Syrian ready to perish. He ent don into Egypt, and lived there, fe in number. There he became a great, mighty, and populous nation.
The Egyptians mistreated us, afflicted us, and imposed hard labor on us.
Then e cried to the LORD, the God of our fathers. The LORD heard our voice, and sa our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
The LORD brought us out of Egypt ith a mighty hand, ith an outstretched arm, ith great terror, ith signs, and ith onders;
and he has brought us into this place, and has given us this land, a land floing ith milk and honey.
No, behold, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground, hich you, the LORD, have given me.” You shall set it don before the LORD your God, and orship before the LORD your God.
You shall rejoice in all the good hich the LORD your God has given to you, and to your house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner ho is among you.

When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your increase in the third year, hich is the year of tithing, then you shall give it to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the ido, that they may eat ithin your gates and be filled.

You shall say before the LORD your God, “ I have put aay the holy things out of my house, and also have given them to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the ido, according to all your commandment hich you have commanded me. I have not transgressed any of your commandments, neither have I forgotten them.

I have not eaten of it in my mourning, neither have I removed any of it hile I as unclean, nor given of it for the dead. I have listened to the LORD my God’s voice. I have done according to all that you have commanded me.
Look don from your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless your people Israel, and the ground hich you have given us, as you sore to our fathers, a land floing ith milk and honey.”
Today the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances. You shall therefore keep and do them ith all your heart and ith all your soul.
You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you ould alk in his ays, keep his statutes, his commandments, and his ordinances, and listen to his voice.
The LORD has declared today that you are a people for his on possession, as he has promised you, and that you should keep all his commandments.
He ill make you high above all nations that he has made, in praise, in name, and in honor, and that you may be a holy people to the LORD your God, as he has spoken.
Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, “ Keep all the commandment hich I command you today.
It shall be on the day hen you shall pass over the Jordan to the land hich the LORD your God gives you, that you shall set yourself up great stones, and coat them ith plaster.

You shall rite on them all the ords of this la, hen you have passed over, that you may go in to the land hich the LORD your God gives you, a land floing ith milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you.
It shall be, hen you have crossed over the Jordan, that you shall set up these stones, hich I command you today, on Mount Ebal, and you shall coat them ith plaster.
There you shall build an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You shall not use any iron tool on them.
You shall build the LORD your God’s altar of uncut stones. You shall offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
You shall sacrifice peace offerings, and shall eat there. You shall rejoice before the LORD your God.
You shall rite on the stones all the ords of this la very plainly.”
Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, “ Be silent and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
You shall therefore obey the LORD your God’s voice, and do his commandments and his statutes, hich I command you today.”
Moses commanded the people the same day, saying,
“ These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people, hen you have crossed over the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
With a loud voice, the Levites shall say to all the men of Israel,
’Cursed is the man ho makes an engraved or molten image, an abomination to the LORD, the ork of the hands of the craftsman, and sets it up in secret.’ All the people shall anser and say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho dishonors his father or his mother.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho removes his neighbor’s landmark.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho leads the blind astray on the road.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho ithholds justice from the foreigner, fatherless, and ido.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho lies ith his father’s ife, because he dishonors his father’s bed.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho lies ith any kind of animal.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho lies ith his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho lies ith his mother-in-la.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho secretly kills his neighbor.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’
’Cursed is he ho doesn’t uphold the ords of this la by doing them.’ All the people shall say, ’Amen.’”

It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to the LORD your God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments hich I command you today, that the LORD your God ill set you high above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings ill come upon you, and overtake you, if you listen to the LORD your God’s voice.
You shall be blessed in the city, and you shall be blessed in the field.
You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock.
Your basket and your kneading trough shall be blessed.
You shall be blessed hen you come in, and you shall be blessed hen you go out.
The LORD ill cause your enemies ho rise up against you to be struck before you. They ill come out against you one ay, and ill flee before you seven ays.
The LORD ill command the blessing on you in your barns, and in all that you put your hand to. He ill bless you in the land hich the LORD your God gives you.
The LORD ill establish you for a holy people to himself, as he has sorn to you, if you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and alk in his ays.
All the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by the LORD’s name, and they ill be afraid of you.
The LORD ill grant you abundant prosperity in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land hich the LORD sore to your fathers to give you.
The LORD ill open to you his good treasure in the sky, to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the ork of your hand. You ill lend to many nations, and you ill not borro.

The LORD ill make you the head, and not the tail. You ill be above only, and you ill not be beneath, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God hich I command you today, to observe and to do,
and shall not turn aay from any of the ords hich I command you today, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

But it shall come to pass, if you ill not listen to the LORD your God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes hich I command you today, that all these curses ill come on you and overtake you.
You ill be cursed in the city, and you ill be cursed in the field.
Your basket and your kneading trough ill be cursed.
The fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock ill be cursed.
You ill be cursed hen you come in, and you ill be cursed hen you go out.

The LORD ill send on you cursing, confusion, and rebuke in all that you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your doings, by hich you have forsaken me.
The LORD ill make the pestilence cling to you, until he has consumed you from off the land here you go in to possess it.
The LORD ill strike you ith consumption, ith fever, ith inflammation, ith fiery heat, ith the sord, ith blight, and ith milde. They ill pursue you until you perish.
Your sky that is over your head ill be bronze, and the earth that is under you ill be iron.
The LORD ill make the rain of your land poder and dust. It ill come don on you from the sky, until you are destroyed.
The LORD ill cause you to be struck before your enemies. You ill go out one ay against them, and ill flee seven ays before them. You ill be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead bodies ill be food to all birds of the sky, and to the animals of the earth; and there ill be no one to frighten them aay.
The LORD ill strike you ith the boils of Egypt, ith the tumors, ith the scurvy, and ith the itch, of hich you can not be healed.
The LORD ill strike you ith madness, ith blindness, and ith astonishment of heart.
You ill grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ays. You ill only be oppressed and robbed alays, and there ill be no one to save you.
You ill betroth a ife, and another man shall lie ith her. You ill build a house, and you on’t dell in it. You ill plant a vineyard, and not use its fruit.

Your ox ill be slain before your eyes, and you ill not eat any of it. Your donkey ill be violently taken aay from before your face, and ill not be restored to you. Your sheep ill be given to your enemies, and you ill have no one to save you.
Your sons and your daughters ill be given to another people. Your eyes ill look and fail ith longing for them all day long. There ill be no poer in your hand.
A nation hich you don’t kno ill eat the fruit of your ground and all of your ork. You ill only be oppressed and crushed alays,
so that the sights that you see ith your eyes ill drive you mad.
The LORD ill strike you in the knees and in the legs ith a sore boil, of hich you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the cron of your head.
The LORD ill bring you, and your king hom you ill set over yourselves, to a nation that you have not knon, you nor your fathers. There you ill serve other gods of ood and stone.
You ill become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byord among all the peoples here the LORD ill lead you aay.
You ill carry much seed out into the field, and ill gather little in, for the locust ill consume it.
You ill plant vineyards and dress them, but you ill neither drink of the ine, nor harvest, because orms ill eat them.
You ill have olive trees throughout all your borders, but you on’t anoint yourself ith the oil, for your olives ill drop off.
You ill father sons and daughters, but they ill not be yours, for they ill go into captivity.
Locusts ill consume all of your trees and the fruit of your ground.
The foreigner ho is among you ill mount up above you higher and higher, and you ill come don loer and loer.
He ill lend to you, and you on’t lend to him. He ill be the head, and you ill be the tail.

All these curses ill come on you, and ill pursue you and overtake you, until you are destroyed, because you didn’t listen to the LORD your God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes hich he commanded you.
They ill be for a sign and for a onder to you and to your offspring forever.
Because you didn’t serve the LORD your God ith joyfulness and ith gladness of heart, by reason of the abundance of all things;
therefore you ill serve your enemies hom the LORD sends against you, in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in lack of all things. He ill put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
The LORD ill bring a nation against you from far aay, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies: a nation hose language you ill not understand,
a nation of fierce facial expressions, that doesn’t respect the elderly, nor sho favor to the young.

They ill eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground, until you are destroyed. They also on’t leave you grain, ne ine, oil, the increase of your livestock, or the young of your flock, until they have caused you to perish.

They ill besiege you in all your gates until your high and fortified alls in hich you trusted come don throughout all your land. They ill besiege you in all your gates throughout all your land hich the LORD your God has given you.
You ill eat the fruit of your on body, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters, hom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress ith hich your enemies ill distress you.
The man ho is tender among you, and very delicate, his eye ill be evil toard his brother, toard the ife hom he loves, and toard the remnant of his children hom he has remaining,

so that he ill not give to any of them of the flesh of his children hom he ill eat, because he has nothing left to him, in the siege and in the distress ith hich your enemy ill distress you in all your gates.

The tender and delicate oman among you, ho ould not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground for delicateness and tenderness, her eye ill be evil toard the husband that she loves, toard her son, toard her daughter,

toard her young one ho comes out from beteen her feet, and toard her children hom she bears; for she ill eat them secretly for lack of all things in the siege and in the distress ith hich your enemy ill distress you in your gates.
If you ill not observe to do all the ords of this la that are ritten in this book, that you may fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD your God,
then the LORD ill make your plagues and the plagues of your offspring fearful, even great plagues, and of long duration, and severe sicknesses, and of long duration.
He ill bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt, hich you ere afraid of; and they ill cling to you.
Also every sickness and every plague hich is not ritten in the book of this la, the LORD ill bring them on you until you are destroyed.
You ill be left fe in number, even though you ere as the stars of the sky for multitude, because you didn’t listen to the LORD your God’s voice.

It ill happen that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so the LORD ill rejoice over you to cause you to perish and to destroy you. You ill be plucked from the land that you are going in to possess.
The LORD ill scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. There you ill serve other gods hich you have not knon, you nor your fathers, even ood and stone.
Among these nations you ill find no ease, and there ill be no rest for the sole of your foot; but the LORD ill give you there a trembling heart, failing of eyes, and pining of soul.
Your life ill hang in doubt before you. You ill be afraid night and day, and ill have no assurance of your life.
In the morning you ill say, “ I ish it ere evening!” and at evening you ill say, “ I ish it ere morning!” for the fear of your heart hich you ill fear, and for the sights hich your eyes ill see.

The LORD ill bring you into Egypt again ith ships, by the ay of hich I told you that you ould never see it again. There you ill offer yourselves to your enemies for male and female slaves, and nobody ill buy you.
These are the ords of the covenant hich the LORD commanded Moses to make ith the children of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant hich he made ith them in Horeb.
Moses called to all Israel, and said to them: Your eyes have seen all that the LORD did in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;
the great trials hich your eyes sa, the signs, and those great onders.
But the LORD has not given you a heart to kno, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
I have led you forty years in the ilderness. Your clothes have not gron old on you, and your sandals have not gron old on your feet.
You have not eaten bread, neither have you drunk ine or strong drink, that you may kno that I am the LORD your God.
When you came to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king of Bashan came out against us to battle, and e struck them.
We took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.
Therefore keep the ords of this covenant and do them, that you may prosper in all that you do.
All of you stand today in the presence of the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, even all the men of Israel,
your little ones, your ives, and the foreigners ho are in the middle of your camps, from the one ho cuts your ood to the one ho dras your ater,
that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God, and into his oath, hich the LORD your God makes ith you today,
that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, as he spoke to you and as he sore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
Neither do I make this covenant and this oath ith you only,
but ith those ho stand here ith us today before the LORD our God, and also ith those ho are not here ith us today
( for you kno ho e lived in the land of Egypt, and ho e came through the middle of the nations through hich you passed;
and you have seen their abominations and their idols of ood, stone, silver, and gold, hich ere among them);

lest there should be among you man, oman, family, or tribe hose heart turns aay today from the LORD our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; lest there should be among you a root that produces bitter poison;
and it happen, hen he hears the ords of this curse, that he bless himself in his heart, saying, “ I shall have peace, though I alk in the stubbornness of my heart,” to destroy the moist ith the dry.

The LORD ill not pardon him, but then the LORD’s anger and his jealousy ill smoke against that man, and all the curse that is ritten in this book ill fall on him, and the LORD ill blot out his name from under the sky.
The LORD ill set him apart for evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant ritten in this book of the la.

The generation to come— your children ho ill rise up after you, and the foreigner ho ill come from a far land— ill say, hen they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses ith hich the LORD has made it sick,

that all of its land is sulfur, salt, and burning, that it is not son, doesn’t produce, nor does any grass gro in it, like the overthro of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, hich the LORD overthre in his anger, and in his rath.
Even all the nations ill say, “ Why has the LORD done this to this land? What does the heat of this great anger mean?”
Then men ill say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, hich he made ith them hen he brought them out of the land of Egypt,
and ent and served other gods and orshiped them, gods that they didn’t kno and that he had not given to them.
Therefore the LORD’s anger burned against this land, to bring on it all the curses that are ritten in this book.
The LORD rooted them out of their land in anger, in rath, and in great indignation, and thrust them into another land, as it is today.”
The secret things belong to the LORD our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that e may do all the ords of this la.

It shall happen, hen all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse, hich I have set before you, and you shall call them to mind among all the nations here the LORD your God has driven you,
and return to the LORD your God and obey his voice according to all that I command you today, you and your children, ith all your heart and ith all your soul,
that then the LORD your God ill release you from captivity, have compassion on you, and ill return and gather you from all the peoples here the LORD your God has scattered you.
If your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the heavens, from there the LORD your God ill gather you, and from there he ill bring you back.
The LORD your God ill bring you into the land hich your fathers possessed, and you ill possess it. He ill do you good, and increase your numbers more than your fathers.
The LORD your God ill circumcise your heart, and the heart of your offspring, to love the LORD your God ith all your heart and ith all your soul, that you may live.
The LORD your God ill put all these curses on your enemies and on those ho hate you, ho persecuted you.
You shall return and obey the LORD’s voice, and do all his commandments hich I command you today.

The LORD your God ill make you prosperous in all the ork of your hand, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, for good; for the LORD ill again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers,
if you ill obey the LORD your God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes hich are ritten in this book of the la, if you turn to the LORD your God ith all your heart and ith all your soul.
For this commandment hich I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant.
It is not in heaven, that you should say, “ Who ill go up for us to heaven, bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that e may do it?”
Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “ Who ill go over the sea for us, bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that e may do it?”
But the ord is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.
Behold, I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and evil.

For I command you today to love the LORD your God, to alk in his ays and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that the LORD your God may bless you in the land here you go in to possess it.
But if your heart turns aay, and you ill not hear, but are dran aay and orship other gods, and serve them,
I declare to you today that you ill surely perish. You ill not prolong your days in the land here you pass over the Jordan to go in to possess it.
I call heaven and earth to itness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants,

to love the LORD your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is your life, and the length of your days, that you may dell in the land hich the LORD sore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.
Moses ent and spoke these ords to all Israel.
He said to them, “ I am one hundred tenty years old today. I can no more go out and come in. The LORD has said to me, ’ You shall not go over this Jordan.’
The LORD your God himself ill go over before you. He ill destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua ill go over before you, as the LORD has spoken.
The LORD ill do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, hen he destroyed them.
The LORD ill deliver them up before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment hich I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them, for the LORD your God himself is ho goes ith you. He ill not fail you nor forsake you.”

Moses called to Joshua, and said to him in the sight of all Israel, “ Be strong and courageous, for you shall go ith this people into the land hich the LORD has sorn to their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.
The LORD himself is ho goes before you. He ill be ith you. He ill not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
Moses rote this la and delivered it to the priests the sons of Levi, ho bore the ark of the LORD’s covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses commanded them, saying, “ At the end of every seven years, in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of booths,
hen all Israel has come to appear before the LORD your God in the place hich he ill choose, you shall read this la before all Israel in their hearing.

Assemble the people, the men and the omen and the little ones, and the foreigners ho are ithin your gates, that they may hear, learn, fear the LORD your God, and observe to do all the ords of this la,
and that their children, ho have not knon, may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land here you go over the Jordan to possess it.”

The LORD said to Moses, “ Behold, your days approach that you must die. Call Joshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting, that I may commission him.” Moses and Joshua ent, and presented themselves in the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD appeared in the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the Tent’s door.

The LORD said to Moses, “ Behold, you shall sleep ith your fathers. This people ill rise up and play the prostitute after the strange gods of the land here they go to be among them, and ill forsake me and break my covenant hich I have made ith them.

Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I ill forsake them, and I ill hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall come on them; so that they ill say in that day, ’Haven’t these evils come on us because our God is not among us?’
I ill surely hide my face in that day for all the evil hich they have done, in that they have turned to other gods.
“ No therefore rite this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Israel. Put it in their mouths, that this song may be a itness for me against the children of Israel.

For hen I have brought them into the land hich I sore to their fathers, floing ith milk and honey, and they have eaten and filled themselves, and gron fat, then they ill turn to other gods, and serve them, and despise me, and break my covenant.

It ill happen, hen many evils and troubles have come on them, that this song ill testify before them as a itness; for it ill not be forgotten out of the mouths of their descendants; for I kno their ays and hat they are doing today, before I have brought them into the land hich I promised them.”
So Moses rote this song the same day, and taught it to the children of Israel.
He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun, and said, “ Be strong and courageous; for you shall bring the children of Israel into the land hich I sore to them. I ill be ith you.”
When Moses had finished riting the ords of this la in a book, until they ere finished,
Moses commanded the Levites, ho bore the ark of the LORD’s covenant, saying,
“ Take this book of the la, and put it by the side of the ark of the LORD your God’s covenant, that it may be there for a itness against you.
For I kno your rebellion and your stiff neck. Behold, hile I am yet alive ith you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD. Ho much more after my death?
Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, that I may speak these ords in their ears, and call heaven and earth to itness against them.

For I kno that after my death you ill utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aay from the ay hich I have commanded you; and evil ill happen to you in the latter days, because you ill do that hich is evil in the LORD’s sight, to provoke him to anger through the ork of your hands.”
Moses spoke in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the ords of this song, until they ere finished.
Give ear, you heavens, and I ill speak. Let the earth hear the ords of my mouth.
My doctrine ill drop as the rain. My speech ill condense as the de, as the misty rain on the tender grass, as the shoers on the herb.
For I ill proclaim the LORD’s name. Ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock: his ork is perfect, for all his ays are just. A God of faithfulness ho does no rong, just and right is he.
They have dealt corruptly ith him. They are not his children, because of their defect. They are a perverse and crooked generation.

and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan’s bank, to the uttermost part of the sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan eastard.
This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and its villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It as for the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.
Their border as from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair, hich are in Bashan, sixty cities.

Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, ere for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.

But Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he spoke to them.

These are the inheritances hich the children of Israel took in the land of Canaan, hich Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed to them,
by the lot of their inheritance, as the LORD commanded by Moses, for the nine tribes, and for the half-tribe.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the to tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

For the children of Joseph ere to tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dell in, ith their pasture lands for their livestock and for their property.
The children of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses, and they divided the land.

Then the children of Judah came near to Joshua in Gilgal. Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “ You kno the thing that the LORD spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you in Kadesh Barnea.

“ No, behold, the LORD has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years, from the time that the LORD spoke this ord to Moses, hile Israel alked in the ilderness. No, behold, I am eighty-five years old, today.
As yet I am as strong today as I as in the day that Moses sent me. As my strength as then, even so is my strength no for ar, to go out and to come in.

Joshua blessed him; and he gave Hebron to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance.

The lot for the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families as to the border of Edom, even to the ilderness of Zin southard, at the uttermost part of the south.

and it ent out southard of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and ent up by the south of Kadesh Barnea, and passed along by Hezron, ent up to Addar, and turned toard Karka;
and it passed along to Azmon, ent out at the brook of Egypt; and the border ended at the sea. This shall be your south border.
The east border as the Salt Sea, even to the end of the Jordan. The border of the north quarter as from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan.
The border ent up to Beth Hoglah, and passed along by the north of Beth Arabah; and the border ent up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.

The border ent up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northard, looking toard Gilgal, that faces the ascent of Adummim, hich is on the south side of the river. The border passed along to the aters of En Shemesh, and ended at En Rogel.

The border ent up by the valley of the son of Hinnom to the side of the Jebusite ( also called Jerusalem) southard; and the border ent up to the top of the mountain that lies before the valley of Hinnom estard, hich is at the farthest part of the valley of Rephaim northard.
The border extended from the top of the mountain to the spring of the aters of Nephtoah, and ent out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah ( also called Kiriath Jearim);

and the border turned about from Baalah estard to Mount Seir, and passed along to the side of Mount Jearim ( also called Chesalon) on the north, and ent don to Beth Shemesh, and passed along by Timnah;
and the border ent out to the side of Ekron northard; and the border extended to Shikkeron, and passed along to Mount Baalah, and ent out at Jabneel; and the goings out of the border ere at the sea.
The est border as to the shore of the great sea. This is the border of the children of Judah according to their families.

He gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh a portion among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the LORD to Joshua, even Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak ( also called Hebron).

This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.

Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,

Libnah, Ether, Ashan,

Ekron, ith its tons and its villages;
from Ekron even to the sea, all that ere by the side of Ashdod, ith their villages.
Ashdod, its tons and its villages; Gaza, its tons and its villages; to the brook of Egypt, and the great sea ith its coastline.
In the hill country, Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Dannah, Kiriath Sannah ( hich is Debir),

Arab, Dumah, Eshan,

As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah couldn’t drive them out; but the Jebusites live ith the children of Judah at Jerusalem to this day.
The lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the aters of Jericho on the east, even the ilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.

and it ent don estard to the border of the Japhletites, to the border of Beth Horon the loer, and on to Gezer; and ended at the sea.
The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.
This as the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families. The border of their inheritance eastard as Ataroth Addar, to Beth Horon the upper.
The border ent out estard at Michmethath on the north. The border turned about eastard to Taanath Shiloh, and passed along it on the east of Janoah.
It ent don from Janoah to Ataroth, to Naarah, reached to Jericho, and ent out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border ent along estard to the brook of Kanah; and ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families;
together ith the cities hich ere set apart for the children of Ephraim in the middle of the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities ith their villages.

They came to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the princes, saying, “ The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” Therefore according to the commandment of the LORD he gave them an inheritance among the brothers of their father.

Joshua said to the children of Israel, “ Ho long ill you neglect to go in to possess the land, hich the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?
Appoint for yourselves three men from each tribe. I ill send them, and they shall arise, alk through the land, and describe it according to their inheritance; then they shall come to me.
They shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall live in his borders on the south, and the house of Joseph shall live in their borders on the north.
You shall survey the land into seven parts, and bring the description here to me; and I ill cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.

Hoever, the Levites have no portion among you; for the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance east of the Jordan, hich Moses the servant of the LORD gave them.”
The men arose and ent. Joshua commanded those ho ent to survey the land, saying, “ Go alk through the land, survey it, and come again to me. I ill cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh.”

The LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,

If the avenger of blood pursues him, then they shall not deliver up the man slayer into his hand; because he struck his neighbor unintentionally, and didn’t hate him before.

He shall dell in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days. Then the man slayer shall return, and come to his on city, and to his on house, to the city he fled from.’”
They set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba ( also called Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.

Then the heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel.
They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “ The LORD commanded through Moses to give us cities to dell in, ith their pasture lands for our livestock.”
The children of Israel gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of the LORD, these cities ith their pasture lands.

They gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities hich are mentioned by name:
and they ere for the children of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, ho ere of the children of Levi; for theirs as the first lot.
They gave them Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak ( also called Hebron), in the hill country of Judah, ith its pasture lands around it.
But they gave the fields of the city and its villages to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession.
To the children of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron ith its pasture lands, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Libnah ith its pasture lands,
Jattir ith its pasture lands, Eshtemoa ith its pasture lands,
Holon ith its pasture lands, Debir ith its pasture lands,

Out of the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon ith its pasture lands, Geba ith its pasture lands,

Out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion ith its pasture lands, Daberath ith its pasture lands,

Out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal ith its pasture lands, Abdon ith its pasture lands,

Out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee ith its pasture lands, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Hammothdor ith its pasture lands, and Kartan ith its pasture lands: three cities.

To the families of the children of Merari, the rest of the Levites, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam ith its pasture lands, Kartah ith its pasture lands,

Out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer ith its pasture lands, Jahaz ith its pasture lands,

The children of Israel again did that hich as evil in the LORD’s sight, and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD, and didn’t serve him.

Then they ent through the ilderness, and ent around the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but they didn’t come ithin the border of Moab, for the Arnon as the border of Moab.

So no the LORD, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and should you possess them?

Therefore I have not sinned against you, but you do me rong to ar against me. May the LORD the Judge be judge today beteen the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.”

Then Manoah entreated the LORD, and said, “ Oh, Lord, please let the man of God hom you sent come again to us, and teach us hat e should do to the child ho shall be born.”

Then Ahimelech ansered the king, and said, “ Who among all your servants is so faithful as David, ho is the king’s son-in-la, captain of your body guard, and honored in your house?

Have I today begun to inquire of God for him? Be it far from me! Don’t let the king impute anything to his servant, nor to all the house of my father; for your servant kne nothing of all this, less or more.”
The king said, “ You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house.”

The king said to the guard ho stood about him, “ Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is ith David, and because they kne that he fled and didn’t disclose it to me.” But the servants of the king ouldn’t put out their hand to fall on the priests of the LORD.
The king said to Doeg, “ Turn and attack the priests!” Doeg the Edomite turned, and he attacked the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five people ho ore a linen ephod.
He struck Nob, the city of the priests, ith the edge of the sord—both men and omen, children and nursing babies, and cattle, donkeys, and sheep, ith the edge of the sord.
One of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.
Abiathar told David that Saul had slain the LORD’s priests.
David said to Abiathar, “ I kne on that day, hen Doeg the Edomite as there, that he ould surely tell Saul. I am responsible for the death of all the persons of your father’s house.
Stay ith me. Don’t be afraid, for he ho seeks my life seeks your life. You ill be safe ith me.”
David as told, “ Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing floors.”
Therefore David inquired of the LORD, saying, “ Shall I go and strike these Philistines?” The LORD said to David, “ Go strike the Philistines, and save Keilah.”
David’s men said to him, “ Behold, e are afraid here in Judah. Ho much more then if e go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
Then David inquired of the LORD yet again. The LORD ansered him, and said, “ Arise, go don to Keilah; for I ill deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
David and his men ent to Keilah and fought ith the Philistines, and brought aay their livestock, and killed them ith a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
When Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, he came don ith an ephod in his hand.
Saul as told that David had come to Keilah. Saul said, “ God has delivered him into my hand, for he is shut in by entering into a ton that has gates and bars.”
Saul summoned all the people to ar, to go don to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
David kne that Saul as devising mischief against him. He said to Abiathar the priest, “ Bring the ephod here.”
Then David said, “ O LORD, the God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy the city for my sake.
Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? Will Saul come don, as your servant has heard? LORD, the God of Israel, I beg you, tell your servant.” The LORD said, “ He ill come don.”
Then David said, “ Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?” The LORD said, “ They ill deliver you up.”
Then David and his men, ho ere about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah and ent herever they could go. Saul as told that David had escaped from Keilah; and he gave up going there.
David stayed in the ilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the ilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God didn’t deliver him into his hand.
David sa that Saul had come out to seek his life. David as in the ilderness of Ziph in the oods.
Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose and ent to David into the oods, and strengthened his hand in God.
He said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father on’t find you; and you ill be king over Israel, and I ill be next to you; and Saul my father knos that also.”
They both made a covenant before the LORD. Then David stayed in the oods and Jonathan ent to his house.
Then the Ziphites came up to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “Doesn’t David hide himself ith us in the strongholds in the oods, in the hill of Hachilah, hich is on the south of the desert?
No therefore, O king, come don. According to all the desire of your soul to come don; and our part ill be to deliver him up into the king’s hand.”
Saul said, “ You are blessed by the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.
Please go make yet more sure, and kno and see his place here his haunt is, and ho has seen him there; for I have been told that he is very cunning.

See therefore, and take knoledge of all the lurking places here he hides himself; and come again to me ith certainty, and I ill go ith you. It shall happen, if he is in the land, that I ill search him out among all the thousands of Judah.”
They arose, and ent to Ziph before Saul; but David and his men ere in the ilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the south of the desert.
Saul and his men ent to seek him. When David as told, he ent don to the rock, and stayed in the ilderness of Maon. When Saul heard that, he pursued David in the ilderness of Maon.

Saul ent on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain; and David hurried to get aay for fear of Saul, for Saul and his men surrounded David and his men to take them.
But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “ Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on the land!”
