David ent up from there and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.
When Saul had returned from folloing the Philistines, he as told, “Behold, David is in the ilderness of En Gedi.”
Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and ent to seek David and his men on the rocks of the ild goats.
He came to the sheep pens by the ay, here there as a cave; and Saul ent in to relieve himself. No David and his men ere staying in the innermost parts of the cave.

David’s men said to him, “Behold, the day of hich the LORD said to you, ’Behold, I ill deliver your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem good to you.’” Then David arose and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe secretly.
Afterard, David’s heart struck him because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
He said to his men, “ The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
So David checked his men ith these ords, and didn’t allo them to rise against Saul. Saul rose up out of the cave, and ent on his ay.
David also arose afterard, and ent out of the cave and cried after Saul, saying, “ My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David boed ith his face to the earth, and shoed respect.
David said to Saul, “ Why do you listen to men’s ords, saying, ’ Behold, David seeks to harm you’?

Behold, today your eyes have seen ho the LORD had delivered you today into my hand in the cave. Some urged me to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ’ I ill not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD’s anointed.’

Moreover, my father, behold, yes, see the skirt of your robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe and didn’t kill you, kno and see that there is neither evil nor disobedience in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my life to take it.
May the LORD judge beteen me and you, and may the LORD avenge me of you; but my hand ill not be on you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, ’ Out of the icked comes ickedness;’ but my hand ill not be on you.
Against hom has the king of Israel come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
May the LORD therefore be judge, and give sentence beteen me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of your hand.”
It came to pass, hen David had finished speaking these ords to Saul, that Saul said, “ Is that your voice, my son David?” Saul lifted up his voice and ept.
He said to David, “ You are more righteous than I; for you have done good to me, hereas I have done evil to you.
You have declared today ho you have dealt ell ith me, because hen the LORD had delivered me up into your hand, you didn’t kill me.
For if a man finds his enemy, ill he let him go aay unharmed? Therefore may the LORD reard you good for that hich you have done to me today.
No, behold, I kno that you ill surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel ill be established in your hand.
Sear no therefore to me by the LORD that you ill not cut off my offspring after me, and that you ill not destroy my name out of my father’s house.”
David sore to Saul. Saul ent home, but David and his men ent up to the stronghold.
Samuel died; and all Israel gathered themselves together and mourned for him, and buried him at his house at Ramah. Then David arose and ent don to the ilderness of Paran.
There as a man in Maon hose possessions ere in Carmel; and the man as very great. He had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and he as shearing his sheep in Carmel.
No the name of the man as Nabal; and the name of his ife Abigail. This oman as intelligent and had a beautiful face; but the man as surly and evil in his doings. He as of the house of Caleb.
David heard in the ilderness that Nabal as shearing his sheep.
David sent ten young men; and David said to the young men, “ Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name.
Tell him, ’ Long life to you! Peace be to you! Peace be to your house! Peace be to all that you have!
No I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds have no been ith us, and e didn’t harm them. Nothing as missing from them all the time they ere in Carmel.

Ask your young men, and they ill tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes, for e come on a good day. Please give hatever comes to your hand to your servants and to your son David.’”
When David’s young men came, they spoke to Nabal all those ords in the name of David, and aited.
Nabal ansered David’s servants and said, “ Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants ho break aay from their masters these days.
Shall I then take my bread, my ater, and my meat that I have killed for my shearers, and give it to men ho I don’t kno here they come from?”
So David’s young men turned on their ay and ent back, and came and told him all these ords.
David said to his men, “ Every man put on his sord!” Every man put on his sord. David also put on his sord. About four hundred men folloed David, and to hundred stayed by the baggage.
But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s ife, saying, “ Behold, David sent messengers out of the ilderness to greet our master; and he insulted them.
But the men ere very good to us, and e ere not harmed, and e didn’t miss anything as long as e ent ith them, hen e ere in the fields.
They ere a all to us both by night and by day, all the hile e ere ith them keeping the sheep.
No therefore kno and consider hat you ill do; for evil is determined against our master and against all his house, for he is such a orthless fello that one can’t speak to him.”

Then Abigail hurried and took to hundred loaves of bread, to containers of ine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs of parched grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and to hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on donkeys.
She said to her young men, “ Go on before me. Behold, I am coming after you.” But she didn’t tell her husband, Nabal.
As she rode on her donkey, and came don hidden by the mountain, behold, David and his men came don toard her, and she met them.
No David had said, “ Surely in vain I have kept all that this fello has in the ilderness, so that nothing as missed of all that pertained to him. He has returned me evil for good.
God do so to the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave of all that belongs to him by the morning light so much as one ho urinates on a all.”
When Abigail sa David, she hurried and got off her donkey, and fell before David on her face and boed herself to the ground.
She fell at his feet and said, “ On me, my lord, on me be the blame! Please let your servant speak in your ears. Hear the ords of your servant.

Please don’t let my lord pay attention to this orthless fello, Nabal, for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is ith him; but I, your servant, didn’t see my lord’s young men hom you sent.

No therefore, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, since the LORD has ithheld you from blood guiltiness and from avenging yourself ith your on hand, no therefore let your enemies and those ho seek evil to my lord be as Nabal.
No this present hich your servant has brought to my lord, let it be given to the young men ho follo my lord.
Please forgive the trespass of your servant. For the LORD ill certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fights the LORD’s battles. Evil ill not be found in you all your days.

Though men may rise up to pursue you and to seek your soul, yet the soul of my lord ill be bound in the bundle of life ith the LORD your God. He ill sling out the souls of your enemies as from a sling’s pocket.
It ill come to pass, hen the LORD has done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you prince over Israel,

that this shall be no grief to you, nor offense of heart to my lord, either that you have shed blood ithout cause, or that my lord has avenged himself. When the LORD has dealt ell ith my lord, then remember your servant.”
David said to Abigail, “ Blessed is the LORD, the God of Israel, ho sent you today to meet me!
Blessed is your discretion, and blessed are you, ho have kept me today from blood guiltiness, and from avenging myself ith my on hand.

For indeed, as the LORD the God of Israel lives, ho has ithheld me from harming you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely there ouldn’t have been left to Nabal by the morning light so much as one ho urinates on a all.”
So David received from her hand that hich she had brought him. Then he said to her, “ Go up in peace to your house. Behold, I have listened to your voice and have granted your request.”

Abigail came to Nabal; and behold, he held a feast in his house like the feast of a king. Nabal’s heart as merry ithin him, for he as very drunk. Therefore she told him nothing until the morning light.
In the morning, hen the ine had gone out of Nabal, his ife told him these things; and his heart died ithin him, and he became as a stone.

When David heard that Nabal as dead, he said, “ Blessed is the LORD, ho has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept back his servant from evil. The LORD has returned the evildoing of Nabal on his on head.” David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her to himself as ife.
When David’s servants had come to Abigail to Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, “ David has sent us to you, to take you to him as ife.”
She arose and boed herself ith her face to the earth, and said, “ Behold, your servant is a servant to ash the feet of the servants of my lord.”
Abigail hurriedly arose and rode on a donkey ith her five maids ho folloed her; and she ent after the messengers of David, and became his ife.
David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they both became his ives.
No Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s ife, to Palti the son of Laish, ho as of Gallim.
The Ziphites came to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “Doesn’t David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, hich is before the desert?”
Then Saul arose and ent don to the ilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel ith him, to seek David in the ilderness of Ziph.
Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, hich is before the desert, by the ay. But David stayed in the ilderness, and he sa that Saul came after him into the ilderness.

Then David arose and came to the place here Saul had encamped; and David sa the place here Saul lay, ith Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his army. Saul lay ithin the place of the agons, and the people ere encamped around him.
Then David ansered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, “ Who ill go don ith me to Saul to the camp?” Abishai said, “ I ill go don ith you.”
So David and Abishai came to the people by night; and, behold, Saul lay sleeping ithin the place of the agons, ith his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay around him.

Then Abishai said to David, “ God has delivered up your enemy into your hand today. No therefore please let me strike him ith the spear to the earth at one stroke, and I ill not strike him the second time.”
David said to Abishai, “Don’t destroy him, for ho can stretch out his hand against the LORD’s anointed, and be guiltless?”
David said, “ As the LORD lives, the LORD ill strike him; or his day shall come to die, or he shall go don into battle and perish.
The LORD forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed; but no please take the spear that is at his head and the jar of ater, and let’s go.”

So David took the spear and the jar of ater from Saul’s head, and they ent aay. No man sa it, or kne it, nor did any aake; for they ere all asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
Then David ent over to the other side, and stood on the top of the mountain far aay, a great space being beteen them;
and David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, “Don’t you anser, Abner?” Then Abner ansered, “ Who are you ho calls to the king?”
David said to Abner, “Aren’t you a man? Who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept atch over your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy your lord the king.

This thing isn’t good that you have done. As the LORD lives, you are orthy to die, because you have not kept atch over your lord, the LORD’s anointed. No see here the king’s spear is, and the jar of ater that as at his head.”
Saul recognized David’s voice, and said, “ Is this your voice, my son David?” David said, “ It is my voice, my lord, O king.”
He said, “ Why does my lord pursue his servant? For hat have I done? What evil is in my hand?

No therefore, please let my lord the king hear the ords of his servant. If it is so that the LORD has stirred you up against me, let him accept an offering. But if it is the children of men, they are cursed before the LORD; for they have driven me out today that I shouldn’t cling to the LORD’s inheritance, saying, ’ Go, serve other gods!’
No therefore, don’t let my blood fall to the earth aay from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a flea, as hen one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
Then Saul said, “ I have sinned. Return, my son David; for I ill no more do you harm, because my life as precious in your eyes today. Behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.”
David ansered, “ Behold the spear, O king! Let one of the young men come over and get it.
The LORD ill give to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness; because the LORD delivered you into my hand today, and I ouldn’t stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
Behold, as your life as respected today in my eyes, so let my life be respected in the LORD’s eyes, and let him deliver me out of all oppression.”
Then Saul said to David, “ You are blessed, my son David. You ill both do mightily, and ill surely prevail.” So David ent his ay, and Saul returned to his place.

David said in his heart, “ I ill no perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I should escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul ill despair of me, to seek me any more in all the borders of Israel. So I ill escape out of his hand.”
David arose and passed over, he and the six hundred men ho ere ith him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
David lived ith Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man ith his household, even David ith his to ives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s ife.

David said to Achish, “If no I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities in the country, that I may dell there. For hy should your servant dell in the royal city ith you?”

The number of the days that David lived in the country of the Philistines as a full year and four months.
David and his men ent up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for those ere the inhabitants of the land ho ere of old, on the ay to Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
David struck the land, and saved no man or oman alive, and took aay the sheep, the cattle, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing. Then he returned, and came to Achish.

David saved neither man nor oman alive to bring them to Gath, saying, “ Lest they should tell about us, saying, ’ David did this, and this has been his ay all the time he has lived in the country of the Philistines.’”

No Samuel as dead, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, even in his on city. Saul had sent aay those ho had familiar spirits and the izards out of the land.

When Saul sa the army of the Philistines, he as afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
When Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD didn’t anser him by dreams, by Urim, or by prophets.

Then Saul said to his servants, “ Seek for me a oman ho has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her and inquire of her.” His servants said to him, “ Behold, there is a oman ho has a familiar spirit at Endor.”

Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing, and ent, he and to men ith him, and they came to the oman by night. Then he said, “Please consult for me by the familiar spirit, and bring me up homever I shall name to you.”

Then the oman said, “ Whom shall I bring up to you?” He said, “ Bring Samuel up for me.”
When the oman sa Samuel, she cried ith a loud voice; and the oman spoke to Saul, saying, “ Why have you deceived me? For you are Saul!”

Moreover the LORD ill deliver Israel also ith you into the hand of the Philistines; and tomorro you and your sons ill be ith me. The LORD ill deliver the army of Israel also into the hand of the Philistines.”

The oman came to Saul and sa that he as very troubled, and said to him, “ Behold, your servant has listened to your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have listened to your ords hich you spoke to me.

She brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. Then they rose up and ent aay that night.
No the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek; and the Israelites encamped by the spring hich is in Jezreel.

Then the princes of the Philistines said, “ What about these Hebres?” Achish said to the princes of the Philistines, “Isn’t this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, ho has been ith me these days, or rather these years? I have found no fault in him since he fell aay until today.”

But the princes of the Philistines ere angry ith him; and the princes of the Philistines said to him, “ Make the man return, that he may go back to his place here you have appointed him, and let him not go don ith us to battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us. Then Achish called David and said to him, “ As the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in ith me in the army is good in my sight; for I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me to this day. Nevertheless, the lords don’t favor you.

David said to Achish, “ But hat have I done? What have you found in your servant so long as I have been before you to this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
Achish ansered David, “ I kno that you are good in my sight, as an angel of God. Notithstanding, the princes of the Philistines have said, ’ He shall not go up ith us to the battle.’
Therefore no rise up early in the morning ith the servants of your lord ho have come ith you; and as soon as you are up early in the morning and have light, depart.”
So David rose up early, he and his men, to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines; and the Philistines ent up to Jezreel.
When David and his men had come to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it ith fire,
and had taken captive the omen and all ho ere in it, both small and great. They didn’t kill any, but carried them off and ent their ay.

Then David and the people ho ere ith him lifted up their voice and ept until they had no more poer to eep.
David’s to ives ere taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the ife of Nabal the Carmelite.

David as greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the souls of all the people ere grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters; but David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “ Please bring the ephod here to me.” Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
David inquired of the LORD, saying, “ If I pursue after this troop, ill I overtake them?” He ansered him, “ Pursue, for you ill surely overtake them, and ill ithout fail recover all.”
So David ent, he and the six hundred men ho ere ith him, and came to the brook Besor, here those ho ere left behind stayed.

This as yet a small thing in your eyes, Lord GOD, but you have spoken also of your servant’s house for a great hile to come; and this among men, Lord GOD!
What more can David say to you? For you kno your servant, Lord GOD.
For your ord’s sake, and according to your on heart, you have orked all this greatness, to make your servant kno it.
Therefore you are great, LORD God. For there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that e have heard ith our ears.

What one nation on the earth is like your people, even like Israel, hom God ent to redeem to himself for a people, and to make himself a name, and to do great things for you, and aesome things for your land, before your people, hom you redeemed to yourself out of Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
You established for yourself your people Israel to be your people forever; and you, LORD, became their God.
“ No, LORD God, the ord that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as you have spoken.
Let your name be magnified forever, saying, ’ The LORD of Armies is God over Israel; and the house of your servant David ill be established before you.’
For you, LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, have revealed to your servant, saying, ’ I ill build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found in his heart to pray this prayer to you.
“ No, O Lord GOD, you are God, and your ords are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.

No therefore, let it please you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, Lord GOD, have spoken it. Let the house of your servant be blessed forever ith your blessing.”
After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued them; and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.

He defeated Moab, and measured them ith the line, making them to lie don on the ground; and he measured to lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. The Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.
David also struck Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he ent to recover his dominion at the River.
David took from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and tenty thousand footmen. David hamstrung the chariot horses, but reserved enough of them for one hundred chariots.
When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck tenty to thousand men of the Syrians.
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. The LORD gave victory to David herever he ent.
David took the shields of gold that ere on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.
When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer,

then Toi sent Joram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him; for Hadadezer had ars ith Toi. Joram brought ith him vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze.
King David also dedicated these to the LORD, ith the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations hich he subdued—
of Syria, of Moab, of the children of Ammon, of the Philistines, of Amalek, and of the plunder of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
David earned a reputation hen he returned from striking don eighteen thousand men of the Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
He put garrisons in Edom. Throughout all Edom, he put garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. The LORD gave victory to David herever he ent.
David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab the son of Zeruiah as over the army, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud as recorder,
Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar ere priests, Seraiah as scribe,
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada as over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons ere chief ministers.
David said, “ Is there yet any ho is left of Saul’s house, that I may sho him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
There as of Saul’s house a servant hose name as Ziba, and they called him to David; and the king said to him, “ Are you Ziba?” He said, “ I am your servant.”
The king said, “ Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may sho the kindness of God to him?” Ziba said to the king, “ Jonathan still has a son, ho is lame in his feet.”
The king said to him, “ Where is he?” Ziba said to the king, “ Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.”
Then King David sent and brought him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.
Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, fell on his face, and shoed respect. David said, “ Mephibosheth?” He ansered, “ Behold, your servant!”

David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I ill surely sho you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and ill restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You ill eat bread at my table continually.”
He boed don, and said, “ What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?”
Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said to him, “ All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master’s son.

Till the land for him— you, your sons, and your servants. Bring in the harvest, that your master’s son may have bread to eat; but Mephibosheth your master’s son ill alays eat bread at my table.” No Ziba had fifteen sons and tenty servants.
Then Ziba said to the king, “ According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant ill do.” So Mephibosheth ate at the king’s table like one of the king’s sons.
Mephibosheth had a young son, hose name as Mica. All ho lived in Ziba’s house ere servants to Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king’s table. He as lame in both his feet.
After this, the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

David said, “ I ill sho kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shoed kindness to me.” So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, “ Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn’t David sent his servants to you to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthro it?”
So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them aay.
When they told David this, he sent to meet them, for the men ere greatly ashamed. The king said, “ Wait at Jericho until your beards have gron, and then return.”

When the children of Ammon sa that they had become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth Rehob and the Syrians of Zobah, tenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah ith one thousand men, and the men of Tob telve thousand men.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.
The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate. The Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah ere by themselves in the field.
No hen Joab sa that the battle as set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel and put them in array against the Syrians.
The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.
He said, “ If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I ill come and help you.
Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and may the LORD do hat seems good to him.”
So Joab and the people ho ere ith him came near to the battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him.
When the children of Ammon sa that the Syrians had fled, they likeise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians sa that they ere defeated by Israel, they gathered themselves together.
Hadadezer sent and brought out the Syrians ho ere beyond the River; and they came to Helam, ith Shobach the captain of the army of Hadadezer at their head.
David as told that; and he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Syrians set themselves in array against David and fought ith him.
The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed seven hundred charioteers of the Syrians and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their army, so that he died there.
When all the kings ho ere servants to Hadadezer sa that they ere defeated before Israel, they made peace ith Israel and served them. So the Syrians ere afraid to help the children of Ammon any more.

At the return of the year, at the time hen kings go out, David sent Joab and his servants ith him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.
At evening, David arose from his bed and alked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof, he sa a oman bathing, and the oman as very beautiful to look at.
David sent and inquired after the oman. One said, “Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, Uriah the Hittite’s ife?”
David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay ith her ( for she as purified from her uncleanness); and she returned to her house.
The oman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, “ I am ith child.”
David sent to Joab, “ Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.
When Uriah had come to him, David asked him ho Joab did, and ho the people fared, and ho the ar prospered.
David said to Uriah, “ Go don to your house and ash your feet.” Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and a gift from the king as sent after him.
But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house ith all the servants of his lord, and didn’t go don to his house.
When they had told David, saying, “Uriah didn’t go don to his house,” David said to Uriah, “Haven’t you come from a journey? Why didn’t you go don to your house?”

Uriah said to David, “ The ark, Israel, and Judah, are staying in tents; and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open field. Shall I then go into my house to eat and to drink, and to lie ith my ife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I ill not do this thing!”
David said to Uriah, “ Stay here today also, and tomorro I ill let you depart.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next day.
When David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk. At evening, he ent out to lie on his bed ith the servants of his lord, but didn’t go don to his house.
In the morning, David rote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
He rote in the letter, saying, “Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck and die.”
When Joab kept atch on the city, he assigned Uriah to the place here he kne that valiant men ere.
The men of the city ent out and fought ith Joab. Some of the people fell, even of David’s servants; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the ar;
and he commanded the messenger, saying, “ When you have finished telling all the things concerning the ar to the king,
it shall be that, if the king’s rath arise, and he asks you, ’ Why did you go so near to the city to fight? Didn’t you kno that they ould shoot from the all?

Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Didn’t a oman cast an upper millstone on him from the all, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the all?’ then you shall say, ’ Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.’”
So the messenger ent, and came and shoed David all that Joab had sent him for.
The messenger said to David, “ The men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field; and e ere on them even to the entrance of the gate.
The shooters shot at your servants from off the all; and some of the king’s servants are dead, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.”

Then David said to the messenger, “Tell Joab, ’Don’t let this thing displease you, for the sord devours one as ell as another. Make your battle stronger against the city, and overthro it.’ Encourage him.”
When Uriah’s ife heard that Uriah her husband as dead, she mourned for her husband.
When the mourning as past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his ife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
The LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “ There ere to men in one city: the one rich, and the other poor.
The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

but the poor man had nothing, except one little ee lamb, hich he had bought and raised. It gre up together ith him and ith his children. It ate of his on food, drank of his on cup, and lay in his bosom, and as like a daughter to him.

A traveler came to the rich man, and he didn’t ant to take of his on flock and of his on herd to prepare for the ayfaring man ho had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man ho had come to him.”
David’s anger burned hot against the man, and he said to Nathan, “ As the LORD lives, the man ho has done this deserves to die!
He must restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity!”
Nathan said to David, “ You are the man! This is hat the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ’ I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

I gave you your master’s house and your master’s ives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that ould have been too little, I ould have added to you many more such things.

Why have you despised the LORD’s ord, to do that hich is evil in his sight? You have struck Uriah the Hittite ith the sord, have taken his ife to be your ife, and have slain him ith the sord of the children of Ammon.
No therefore the sord ill never depart from your house, because you have despised me and have taken Uriah the Hittite’s ife to be your ife.’

“ This is hat the LORD says: ’ Behold, I ill raise up evil against you out of your on house; and I ill take your ives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he ill lie ith your ives in the sight of this sun.
For you did this secretly, but I ill do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.’”
David said to Nathan, “ I have sinned against the LORD.” Nathan said to David, “ The LORD also has put aay your sin. You ill not die.
Hoever, because by this deed you have given great occasion to the LORD’s enemies to blaspheme, the child also ho is born to you ill surely die.”
Then Nathan departed to his house. The LORD struck the child that Uriah’s ife bore to David, and he as very sick.
David therefore begged God for the child; and David fasted, and ent in and lay all night on the ground.
The elders of his house arose beside him, to raise him up from the earth; but he ould not, and he didn’t eat bread ith them.

On the seventh day, the child died. David’s servants ere afraid to tell him that the child as dead, for they said, “ Behold, hile the child as yet alive, e spoke to him and he didn’t listen to our voice. Ho ill he then harm himself if e tell him that the child is dead?”
But hen David sa that his servants ere hispering together, David perceived that the child as dead; and David said to his servants, “ Is the child dead?” They said, “ He is dead.”

Then David arose from the earth, and ashed and anointed himself, and changed his clothing; and he came into the LORD’s house, and orshiped. Then he came to his on house; and hen he requested, they set bread before him and he ate.
Then his servants said to him, “ What is this that you have done? You fasted and ept for the child hile he as alive, but hen the child as dead, you rose up and ate bread.”
He said, “ While the child as yet alive, I fasted and ept; for I said, ’ Who knos hether the LORD ill not be gracious to me, that the child may live?’
But no he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I ill go to him, but he ill not return to me.”
David comforted Bathsheba his ife, and ent in to her, and lay ith her. She bore a son, and he called his name Solomon. The LORD loved him;
and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he named him Jedidiah, for the LORD’s sake.
No Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
Joab sent messengers to David, and said, “ I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of aters.
No therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called by my name.”
David gathered all the people together and ent to Rabbah, and fought against it and took it.

He took the cron of their king from off his head; and its eight as a talent of gold, and in it ere precious stones; and it as set on David’s head. He brought a great quantity of plunder out of the city.

He brought out the people ho ere in it, and put them to ork under sas, under iron picks, under axes of iron, and made them go to the brick kiln; and he did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
After this, Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, hose name as Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
Amnon as so troubled that he became sick because of his sister Tamar, for she as a virgin, and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her.
But Amnon had a friend hose name as Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother; and Jonadab as a very subtle man.
He said to him, “ Why, son of the king, are you so sad from day to day? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon said to him, “ I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”

Jonadab said to him, “ Lay don on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, tell him, ’ Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it and eat it from her hand.’”

So Amnon lay don and faked being sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, “ Please let my sister Tamar come and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.”
Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, “ Go no to your brother Amnon’s house, and prepare food for him.”
So Tamar ent to her brother Amnon’s house; and he as lying don. She took dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.
She took the pan and poured them out before him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, “ Have all men leave me.” Then every man ent out from him.
Amnon said to Tamar, “ Bring the food into the room, that I may eat from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes hich she had made, and brought them into the room to Amnon her brother.
When she had brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, “ Come, lie ith me, my sister!”
She ansered him, “ No, my brother, do not force me! For no such thing ought to be done in Israel. Don’t you do this folly!
As for me, here ould I carry my shame? And as for you, you ill be as one of the fools in Israel. No therefore, please speak to the king; for he ill not ithhold me from you.”
Hoever, he ould not listen to her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her and lay ith her.
Then Amnon hated her ith exceedingly great hatred; for the hatred ith hich he hated her as greater than the love ith hich he had loved her. Amnon said to her, “ Arise, be gone!”
She said to him, “ Not so, because this great rong in sending me aay is orse than the other that you did to me!” But he ould not listen to her.
Then he called his servant ho ministered to him, and said, “ No put this oman out from me, and bolt the door after her.”
She had a garment of various colors on her, for the king’s daughters ho ere virgins dressed in such robes. Then his servant brought her out and bolted the door after her.
Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her garment of various colors that as on her; and she laid her hand on her head and ent her ay, crying aloud as she ent.

Absalom her brother said to her, “ Has Amnon your brother been ith you? But no hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother. Don’t take this thing to heart.” So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
But hen King David heard of all these things, he as very angry.
Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
After to full years, Absalom had sheep shearers in Baal Hazor, hich is beside Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
Absalom came to the king and said, “ See no, your servant has sheep shearers. Please let the king and his servants go ith your servant.”
The king said to Absalom, “ No, my son, let’s not all go, lest e be burdensome to you.” He pressed him; hoever he ould not go, but blessed him.
Then Absalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go ith us.” The king said to him, “ Why should he go ith you?”
But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go ith him.

Absalom commanded his servants, saying, “ Mark no, hen Amnon’s heart is merry ith ine; and hen I tell you, ’ Strike Amnon,’ then kill him. Don’t be afraid. Haven’t I commanded you? Be courageous, and be valiant!”
The servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man got up on his mule and fled.
While they ere on the ay, the nes came to David, saying, “Absalom has slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left!”
Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by ith their clothes torn.

Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, ansered, “Don’t let my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men, the king’s sons, for Amnon only is dead; for by the appointment of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
No therefore don’t let my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead; for only Amnon is dead.”
But Absalom fled. The young man ho kept the atch lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people ere coming by ay of the hillside behind him.
Jonadab said to the king, “ Behold, the king’s sons are coming! It is as your servant said.”
As soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voices and ept. The king also and all his servants ept bitterly.
But Absalom fled and ent to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.
So Absalom fled and ent to Geshur, and as there three years.
King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he as comforted concerning Amnon, since he as dead.
No Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart as toard Absalom.

Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a ise oman from there, and said to her, “ Please act like a mourner, and put on mourning clothing, please, and don’t anoint yourself ith oil; but be as a oman ho has mourned a long time for the dead.
Go in to the king and speak like this to him.” So Joab put the ords in her mouth.
When the oman of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, shoed respect, and said, “ Help, O king!”
The king said to her, “ What ails you?” She ansered, “Truly I am a ido, and my husband is dead.
Your servant had to sons; and they both fought together in the field, and there as no one to part them, but the one struck the other and killed him.

Behold, the hole family has risen against your servant, and they say, ’ Deliver him ho struck his brother, that e may kill him for the life of his brother hom he killed, and so destroy the heir also.’ Thus they ould quench my coal hich is left, and ould leave to my husband neither name nor remainder on the surface of the earth.”
The king said to the oman, “ Go to your house, and I ill give a command concerning you.”
The oman of Tekoa said to the king, “ My lord, O king, may the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house; and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
The king said, “Whoever says anything to you, bring him to me, and he ill not bother you any more.”

Then she said, “ Please let the king remember the LORD your God, that the avenger of blood destroy not any more, lest they destroy my son.” He said, “ As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the earth.”
Then the oman said, “ Please let your servant speak a ord to my lord the king.” He said, “ Say on.”

The oman said, “ Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this ord the king is as one ho is guilty, in that the king does not bring home again his banished one.
For e must die, and are like ater spilled on the ground, hich can’t be gathered up again; neither does God take aay life, but devises means, that he ho is banished not be an outcast from him.

No therefore, seeing that I have come to speak this ord to my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid. Your servant said, ’ I ill no speak to the king; it may be that the king ill perform the request of his servant.’
For the king ill hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man ho ould destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
Then your servant said, ’ Please let the ord of my lord the king bring rest; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad. May the LORD, your God, be ith you.’”
Then the king ansered the oman, “ Please don’t hide anything from me that I ask you.” The oman said, “ Let my lord the king no speak.”

The king said, “ Is the hand of Joab ith you in all this?” The oman ansered, “ As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab urged me, and he put all these ords in the mouth of your servant.
Your servant Joab has done this thing to change the face of the matter. My lord is ise, according to the isdom of an angel of God, to kno all things that are on the earth.”
The king said to Joab, “ Behold no, I have granted this thing. Go therefore, and bring the young man Absalom back.”

Joab fell to the ground on his face, shoed respect, and blessed the king. Joab said, “ Today your servant knos that I have found favor in your sight, my lord, O king, in that the king has performed the request of his servant.”
So Joab arose and ent to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
The king said, “ Let him return to his on house, but let him not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his on house, and didn’t see the king’s face.
No in all Israel there as no one to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the cron of his head there as no defect in him.

When he cut the hair of his head ( no it as at every year’s end that he cut it; because it as heavy on him, therefore he cut it), he eighed the hair of his head at to hundred shekels, after the king’s eight.
Three sons ere born to Absalom, and one daughter, hose name as Tamar. She as a oman ith a beautiful face.
Absalom lived to full years in Jerusalem, and he didn’t see the king’s face.
Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he ould not come to him. Then he sent again a second time, but he ould not come.
Therefore he said to his servants, “ Behold, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
Then Joab arose and came to Absalom to his house, and said to him, “ Why have your servants set my field on fire?”

Absalom ansered Joab, “ Behold, I sent to you, saying, ’ Come here, that I may send you to the king, to say, “ Why have I come from Geshur? It ould be better for me to be there still. No therefore, let me see the king’s face; and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”’”
So Joab came to the king and told him; and hen he had called for Absalom, he came to the king and boed himself on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.
After this, Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.

Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the ay of the gate. When any man had a suit hich should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him, and said, “ What city are you from?” He said, “ Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.”
Absalom said to him, “ Behold, your matters are good and right; but there is no man deputized by the king to hear you.”
Absalom said moreover, “ Oh that I ere made judge in the land, that every man ho has any suit or cause might come to me, and I ould do him justice!”
It as so, that hen any man came near to bo don to him, he stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and kissed him.
Absalom did this sort of thing to all Israel ho came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
At the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, “ Please let me go and pay my vo, hich I have voed to the LORD, in Hebron.
For your servant voed a vo hile I stayed at Geshur in Syria, saying, ’ If the LORD shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I ill serve the LORD.’”
The king said to him, “ Go in peace.” So he arose and ent to Hebron.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “ As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ’Absalom is king in Hebron!’”
To hundred men ent ith Absalom out of Jerusalem, ho ere invited, and ent in their simplicity; and they didn’t kno anything.

Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city, even from Giloh, hile he as offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy as strong, for the people increased continually ith Absalom.
A messenger came to David, saying, “ The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.”

David said to all his servants ho ere ith him at Jerusalem, “ Arise! Let’s flee, or else none of us ill escape from Absalom. Hurry to depart, lest he overtake us quickly and bring don evil on us, and strike the city ith the edge of the sord.”
The king’s servants said to the king, “ Behold, your servants are ready to do hatever my lord the king chooses.”
The king ent out, and all his household after him. The king left ten omen, ho ere concubines, to keep the house.
The king ent out, and all the people after him; and they stayed in Beth Merhak.
All his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men ho came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “ Why do you also go ith us? Return, and stay ith the king; for you are a foreigner and also an exile. Return to your on place.
Whereas you came but yesterday, should I today make you go up and don ith us, since I go here I may? Return, and take back your brothers. Mercy and truth be ith you.”
Ittai ansered the king and said, “ As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in hat place my lord the king is, hether for death or for life, your servant ill be there also.”
David said to Ittai, “ Go and pass over.” Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones ho ere ith him.
All the country ept ith a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toard the ay of the ilderness.
Behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites ith him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and they set don God’s ark; and Abiathar ent up until all the people finished passing out of the city.
The king said to Zadok, “Carry God’s ark back into the city. If I find favor in the LORD’s eyes, he ill bring me again, and sho me both it and his habitation;
but if he says, ’ I have no delight in you,’ behold, here I am. Let him do to me as seems good to him.”
The king said also to Zadok the priest, “Aren’t you a seer? Return into the city in peace, and your to sons ith you, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
Behold, I ill stay at the fords of the ilderness until ord comes from you to inform me.”
Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried God’s ark to Jerusalem again; and they stayed there.

David ent up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and ept as he ent up; and he had his head covered and ent barefoot. All the people ho ere ith him each covered his head, and they ent up, eeping as they ent up.
Someone told David, saying, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators ith Absalom.” David said, “ LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.”
When David had come to the top, here God as orshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him ith his tunic torn and earth on his head.
David said to him, “ If you pass on ith me, then you ill be a burden to me;

but if you return to the city, and tell Absalom, ’ I ill be your servant, O king. As I have been your father’s servant in time past, so I ill no be your servant; then you ill defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.’
Don’t you have Zadok and Abiathar the priests there ith you? Therefore hatever you hear out of the king’s house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
Behold, they have there ith them their to sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son. Send to me everything that you shall hear by them.”
So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city; and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

When David as a little past the top, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him ith a couple of donkeys saddled, and on them to hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a container of ine.

The king said to Ziba, “ What do you mean by these?” Ziba said, “ The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the ine, that those ho are faint in the ilderness may drink.”
The king said, “ Where is your master’s son?” Ziba said to the king, “ Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem; for he said, ’ Today the house of Israel ill restore me the kingdom of my father.’”
Then the king said to Ziba, “ Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” Ziba said, “ I bo don. Let me find favor in your sight, my lord, O king.”
When King David came to Bahurim, behold, a man of the family of Saul’s house came out, hose name as Shimei, the son of Gera. He came out and cursed as he came.
He cast stones at David and at all the servants of King David, and all the people and all the mighty men ere on his right hand and on his left.
Shimei said hen he cursed, “ Be gone, be gone, you man of blood, and icked fello!

The LORD has returned on you all the blood of Saul’s house, in hose place you have reigned! The LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son! Behold, you are caught by your on mischief, because you are a man of blood!”
Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, “ Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head.”
The king said, “ What have I to do ith you, you sons of Zeruiah? Because he curses, and because the LORD has said to him, ’ Curse David,’ ho then shall say, ’ Why have you done so?’”

David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “ Behold, my son, ho came out of my boels, seeks my life. Ho much more this Benjamite, no? Leave him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD has invited him.
It may be that the LORD ill look on the rong done to me, and that the LORD ill repay me good for the cursing of me today.”
So David and his men ent by the ay; and Shimei ent along on the hillside opposite him and cursed as he ent, thre stones at him, and thre dust.
The king and all the people ho ere ith him arrived eary; and he refreshed himself there.
Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel ith him.
When Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, had come to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
Absalom said to Hushai, “ Is this your kindness to your friend? Why didn’t you go ith your friend?”
Hushai said to Absalom, “ No; but homever the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, I ill be his, and I ill stay ith him.
Again, hom should I serve? Shouldn’t I serve in the presence of his son? As I have served in your father’s presence, so I ill be in your presence.”
Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “ Give your counsel hat e shall do.”

Ahithophel said to Absalom, “ Go in to your father’s concubines that he has left to keep the house. Then all Israel ill hear that you are abhorred by your father. Then the hands of all ho are ith you ill be strong.”
So they spread a tent for Absalom on the top of the house, and Absalom ent in to his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
The counsel of Ahithophel, hich he gave in those days, as as if a man inquired at the inner sanctuary of God. All the counsel of Ahithophel as like this both ith David and ith Absalom.
Moreover Ahithophel said to Absalom, “ Let me no choose telve thousand men, and I ill arise and pursue after David tonight.
I ill come on him hile he is eary and exhausted, and ill make him afraid. All the people ho are ith him ill flee. I ill strike the king only,
and I ill bring back all the people to you. The man hom you seek is as if all returned. All the people shall be in peace.”
The saying pleased Absalom ell, and all the elders of Israel.
Then Absalom said, “ No call Hushai the Archite also, and let’s hear likeise hat he says.”
When Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, “Ahithophel has spoken like this. Shall e do hat he says? If not, speak up.”
Hushai said to Absalom, “ The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good.”

Hushai said moreover, “ You kno your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are fierce in their minds, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Your father is a man of ar, and ill not lodge ith the people.

Behold, he is no hidden in some pit, or in some other place. It ill happen, hen some of them have fallen at the first, that hoever hears it ill say, ’ There is a slaughter among the people ho follo Absalom!’
Even he ho is valiant, hose heart is as the heart of a lion, ill utterly melt; for all Israel knos that your father is a mighty man, and those ho are ith him are valiant men.
But I counsel that all Israel be gathered together to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that you go to battle in your on person.
So e ill come on him in some place here he ill be found, and e ill light on him as the de falls on the ground, then e ill not leave so much as one of him and of all the men ho are ith him.
Moreover, if he has gone into a city, then all Israel ill bring ropes to that city, and e ill dra it into the river, until there isn’t one small stone found there.”

Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “ The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil on Absalom.
Then Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, “Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel that ay; and I have counseled this ay.
No therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, ’Don’t lodge tonight at the fords of the ilderness, but by all means pass over, lest the king be salloed up, and all the people ho are ith him.’”
No Jonathan and Ahimaaz ere staying by En Rogel; and a female servant used to go and report to them, and they ent and told King David; for they couldn’t risk being seen coming into the city.
But a boy sa them, and told Absalom. Then they both ent aay quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, ho had a ell in his court; and they ent don there.
The oman took and spread the covering over the ell’s mouth, and spread out crushed grain on it; and nothing as knon.

Absalom’s servants came to the oman to the house; and they said, “ Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The oman said to them, “ They have gone over the brook of ater.” When they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
After they had departed, they came up out of the ell and ent and told King David; and they said to David, “ Arise and pass quickly over the ater; for thus has Ahithophel counseled against you.”
Then David arose, and all the people ho ere ith him, and they passed over the Jordan. By the morning light there lacked not one of them ho had not gone over the Jordan.

When Ahithophel sa that his counsel as not folloed, he saddled his donkey, arose, and ent home to his city, set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and as buried in the tomb of his father.
Then David came to Mahanaim. Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel ith him.
Absalom set Amasa over the army instead of Joab. No Amasa as the son of a man hose name as Ithra the Israelite, ho ent in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
When David had come to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
brought beds, basins, earthen vessels, heat, barley, meal, parched grain, beans, lentils, roasted grain,
honey, butter, sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David and for the people ho ere ith him to eat; for they said, “ The people are hungry, eary, and thirsty in the ilderness.”
David counted the people ho ere ith him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

David sent the people out, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, “ I ill also surely go out ith you myself.”

But the people said, “ You shall not go out, for if e flee aay, they ill not care for us, neither if half of us die, ill they care for us. But you are orth ten thousand of us. Therefore no it is better that you are ready to help us out of the city.”
The king said to them, “ I ill do hat seems best to you.” The king stood beside the gate, and all the people ent out by hundreds and by thousands.
The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently for my sake ith the young man Absalom.” All the people heard hen the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.
So the people ent out into the field against Israel; and the battle as in the forest of Ephraim.
The people of Israel ere struck there before David’s servants, and there as a great slaughter there that day of tenty thousand men.
For the battle as there spread over the surface of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sord devoured.

Absalom happened to meet David’s servants. Absalom as riding on his mule, and the mule ent under the thick boughs of a great oak; and his head caught hold of the oak, and he as hanging beteen the sky and earth; and the mule that as under him ent on.
A certain man sa it, and told Joab, and said, “ Behold, I sa Absalom hanging in an oak.”
Joab said to the man ho told him, “ Behold, you sa it, and hy didn’t you strike him there to the ground? I ould have given you ten pieces of silver and a sash.”

The man said to Joab, “ Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I still ouldn’t stretch out my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, ’ Beare that no one touch the young man Absalom.’
Otherise, if I had dealt falsely against his life ( and there is no matter hidden from the king), then you yourself ould have set yourself against me.”
Then Joab said, “ I’m not going to ait like this ith you.” He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart hile he as still alive in the middle of the oak.
Ten young men ho bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom, and killed him.
Joab ble the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held the people back.
They took Absalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. Then all Israel fled, each to his on tent.

No Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar hich is in the king’s valley, for he said, “ I have no son to keep my name in memory.” He called the pillar after his on name. It is called Absalom’s monument, to this day.
Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “ Let me no run and carry the king nes, ho the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
Joab said to him, “ You must not be the bearer of nes today, but you must carry nes another day. But today you must carry no nes, because the king’s son is dead.”
Then Joab said to the Cushite, “ Go, tell the king hat you have seen!” The Cushite boed himself to Joab, and ran.

Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, “ But come hat may, please let me also run after the Cushite.” Joab said, “ Why do you ant to run, my son, since you ill have no reard for the nes?”
“ But come hat may,” he said, “ I ill run.” He said to him, “ Run!” Then Ahimaaz ran by the ay of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.
No David as sitting beteen the to gates; and the atchman ent up to the roof of the gate to the all, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.
The atchman shouted and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is nes in his mouth.” He came closer and closer.
The atchman sa another man running; and the atchman called to the gatekeeper and said, “ Behold, a man running alone!” The king said, “ He also brings nes.”
The atchman said, “ I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” The king said, “ He is a good man, and comes ith good nes.”

Ahimaaz called, and said to the king, “ All is ell.” He boed himself before the king ith his face to the earth, and said, “ Blessed is the LORD your God, ho has delivered up the men ho lifted up their hand against my lord the king!”
The king said, “ Is it ell ith the young man Absalom?” Ahimaaz ansered, “ When Joab sent the king’s servant, even me your servant, I sa a great tumult, but I don’t kno hat it as.”
The king said, “ Come and stand here.” He came and stood still.
Behold, the Cushite came. The Cushite said, “ Good nes for my lord the king, for the LORD has avenged you today of all those ho rose up against you.”

The king said to the Cushite, “ Is it ell ith the young man Absalom?” The Cushite ansered, “ May the enemies of my lord the king, and all ho rise up against you to do you harm, be as that young man is.”
The king as much moved, and ent up to the room over the gate and ept. As he ent, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I ish I had died instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son!”
Joab as told, “Behold, the king eeps and mourns for Absalom.”
The victory that day as turned into mourning among all the people, for the people heard it said that day, “ The king grieves for his son.”
The people sneaked into the city that day, as people ho are ashamed steal aay hen they flee in battle.
The king covered his face, and the king cried ith a loud voice, “ My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!”

Joab came into the house to the king, and said, “Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants ho today have saved your life, and the lives of your sons and of your daughters, and the lives of your ives, and the lives of your concubines;

in that you love those ho hate you and hate those ho love you. For you have declared today that princes and servants are nothing to you. For today I perceive that if Absalom had lived and e had all died today, then it ould have pleased you ell.

No therefore arise, go out and speak to comfort your servants; for I sear by the LORD, if you don’t go out, not a man ill stay ith you this night. That ould be orse to you than all the evil that has happened to you from your youth until no.”
Then the king arose and sat in the gate. The people ere all told, “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” All the people came before the king. No Israel had fled every man to his tent.

All the people ere at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “ The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and no he has fled out of the land from Absalom.
Absalom, hom e anointed over us, is dead in battle. No therefore hy don’t you speak a ord of bringing the king back?”

King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, “ Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, ’ Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house, since the speech of all Israel has come to the king, to return him to his house?
You are my brothers. You are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the last to bring back the king?’
Say to Amasa, ’Aren’t you my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you aren’t captain of the army before me continually instead of Joab.’”
He boed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as one man, so that they sent to the king, saying, “ Return, you and all your servants.”
So the king returned, and came to the Jordan. Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.
Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, ho as of Bahurim, hurried and came don ith the men of Judah to meet King David.
There ere a thousand men of Benjamin ith him, and Ziba the servant of Saul’s house, and his fifteen sons and his tenty servants ith him; and they ent through the Jordan in the presence of the king.
A ferry boat ent to bring over the king’s household, and to do hat he thought good. Shimei the son of Gera fell don before the king hen he had come over the Jordan.

He said to the king, “Don’t let my lord impute iniquity to me, or remember that hich your servant did perversely the day that my lord the king ent out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
For your servant knos that I have sinned. Therefore behold, I have come today as the first of all the house of Joseph to go don to meet my lord the king.”
But Abishai the son of Zeruiah ansered, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”

David said, “ What have I to do ith you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should be adversaries to me today? Shall any man be put to death today in Israel? For don’t I kno that I am king over Israel today?”
The king said to Shimei, “ You ill not die.” The king sore to him.

Mephibosheth the son of Saul came don to meet the king; and he had neither groomed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor ashed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace.
When he had come to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, “ Why didn’t you go ith me, Mephibosheth?”
He ansered, “ My lord, O king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, ’ I ill saddle a donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go ith the king,’ because your servant is lame.
He has slandered your servant to my lord the king, but my lord the king is as an angel of God. Therefore do hat is good in your eyes.

For all my father’s house ere but dead men before my lord the king; yet you set your servant among those ho ate at your on table. What right therefore have I yet that I should appeal any more to the king?”
The king said to him, “ Why do you speak any more of your matters? I say, you and Ziba divide the land.”
Mephibosheth said to the king, “Yes, let him take all, because my lord the king has come in peace to his on house.”
Barzillai the Gileadite came don from Rogelim; and he ent over the Jordan ith the king to conduct him over the Jordan.
No Barzillai as a very aged man, even eighty years old. He had provided the king ith sustenance hile he stayed at Mahanaim, for he as a very great man.
The king said to Barzillai, “Come over ith me, and I ill sustain you ith me in Jerusalem.”
Barzillai said to the king, “Ho many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up ith the king to Jerusalem?

I am eighty years old, today. Can I discern beteen good and bad? Can your servant taste hat I eat or hat I drink? Can I hear the voice of singing men and singing omen any more? Why then should your servant be a burden to my lord the king?
Your servant ill just go over the Jordan ith the king. Why should the king repay me ith such a reard?

Please let your servant turn back again, that I may die in my on city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, your servant Chimham; let him go over ith my lord the king; and do to him hat shall seem good to you.”
The king ansered, “ Chimham shall go over ith me, and I ill do to him that hich shall seem good to you. Whatever you request of me, that I ill do for you.”
All the people ent over the Jordan, and the king ent over. Then the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him; and he returned to his on place.
So the king ent over to Gilgal, and Chimham ent over ith him. All the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.

Behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, “Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you aay, and brought the king and his household, over the Jordan, and all David’s men ith him?”

All the men of Judah ansered the men of Israel, “ Because the king is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have e eaten at all at the king’s cost? Or has he given us any gift?”

The men of Israel ansered the men of Judah, and said, “ We have ten parts in the king, and e have also more claim to David than you. Why then did you despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king?” The ords of the men of Judah ere fiercer than the ords of the men of Israel.

There happened to be there a icked fello, hose name as Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite; and he ble the trumpet, and said, “ We have no portion in David, neither have e inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, Israel!”
So all the men of Israel ent up from folloing David, and folloed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah joined ith their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten omen his concubines, hom he had left to keep the house, and put them in custody and provided them ith sustenance, but didn’t go in to them. So they ere shut up to the day of their death, living in idohood.
Then the king said to Amasa, “ Call me the men of Judah together ithin three days, and be here present.”
So Amasa ent to call the men of Judah together, but he stayed longer than the set time hich had been appointed to him.

David said to Abishai, “ No Sheba the son of Bichri ill do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord’s servants and pursue after him, lest he get himself fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.”
Joab’s men ent out after him ith the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they ent out of Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

When they ere at the great stone hich is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab as clothed in his apparel of ar that he had put on, and on it as a sash ith a sord fastened on his aist in its sheath; and as he ent along it fell out.
Joab said to Amasa, “ Is it ell ith you, my brother?” Joab took Amasa by the beard ith his right hand to kiss him.

But Amasa took no heed to the sord that as in Joab’s hand. So he struck him ith it in the body and shed out his boels to the ground, and didn’t strike him again; and he died. Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba the son of Bichri.
One of Joab’s young men stood by him, and said, “ He ho favors Joab, and he ho is for David, let him follo Joab!”

Amasa lay alloing in his blood in the middle of the highay. When the man sa that all the people stood still, he carried Amasa out of the highay into the field, and cast a garment over him hen he sa that everyone ho came by him stood still.
When he as removed out of the highay, all the people ent on after Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
He ent through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, to Beth Maacah, and all the Berites. They ere gathered together, and ent also after him.
They came and besieged him in Abel of Beth Maacah, and they cast up a mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart; and all the people ho ere ith Joab battered the all to thro it don.
Then a ise oman cried out of the city, “ Hear, hear! Please say to Joab, ’ Come near here, that I may speak ith you.’”
He came near to her; and the oman said, “ Are you Joab?” He ansered, “ I am.” Then she said to him, “ Hear the ords of your servant.” He ansered, “ I’m listening.”
Then she spoke, saying, “ They used to say in old times, ’ They shall surely ask counsel at Abel,’ and so they settled a matter.
I am among those ho are peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why ill you sallo up the LORD’s inheritance?”
Joab ansered, “ Far be it, far be it from me, that I should sallo up or destroy.

To Abiathar the priest the king said, “ Go to Anathoth, to your on fields, for you are orthy of death. But I ill not at this time put you to death, because you bore the Lord GOD’s ark before David my father, and because you ere afflicted in all in hich my father as afflicted.”

This nes came to Joab; for Joab had folloed Adonijah, although he didn’t follo Absalom. Joab fled to the LORD’s Tent, and held onto the horns of the altar.

Benaiah came to the LORD’s Tent, and said to him, “ The king says, ’ Come out!’” He said, “ No; but I ill die here.” Benaiah brought the king ord again, saying, “ This is hat Joab said, and this is ho he ansered me.”
The king said to him, “ Do as he has said, and fall on him, and bury him, that you may take aay the blood, hich Joab shed ithout cause, from me and from my father’s house.

The LORD ill return his blood on his on head, because he fell on to men more righteous and better than he, and killed them ith the sord, and my father David didn’t kno it: Abner the son of Ner, captain of the army of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the army of Judah.

Then Benaiah the son of Jehoiada ent up and fell on him, and killed him; and he as buried in his on house in the ilderness.

The king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, “ Build yourself a house in Jerusalem, and live there, and don’t go anyhere else.

Solomon said, “ You have shon to your servant David my father great loving kindness, because he alked before you in truth, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart ith you. You have kept for him this great loving kindness, that you have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is today.

This request pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

God said to him, “ Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked for yourself long life, nor have you asked for riches for yourself, nor have you asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to discern justice,
behold, I have done according to your ord. Behold, I have given you a ise and understanding heart, so that there has been no one like you before you, and after you none ill arise like you.
