Solomon aoke; and behold, it as a dream. Then he came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the LORD’s covenant, and offered up burnt offerings, offered peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
Then to omen ho ere prostitutes came to the king, and stood before him.
The one oman said, “Oh, my lord, I and this oman dell in one house. I delivered a child ith her in the house.
The third day after I delivered, this oman delivered also. We ere together. There as no stranger ith us in the house, just us to in the house.

The other oman said, “ No! But the living one is my son, and the dead one is your son.” The first one said, “ No! But the dead one is your son, and the living one is my son.” They argued like this before the king.
Then the king said, “ One says, ’ This is my son ho lives, and your son is the dead one;’ and the other says, ’ No! But your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’”
The king said, “ Get me a sord.” So they brought a sord before the king.
The king said, “ Divide the living child in to, and give half to the one, and half to the other.”

Then the oman hose the living child as spoke to the king, for her heart yearned over her son, and she said, “Oh, my lord, give her the living child, and in no ay kill him!” But the other said, “ He shall be neither mine nor yours. Divide him.”
Then the king ansered, “ Give the first oman the living child, and definitely do not kill him. She is his mother.”
All Israel heard of the judgment hich the king had judged; and they feared the king, for they sa that the isdom of God as in him to do justice.
King Solomon as king over all Israel.
These ere the princes hom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok, the priest;

These are their names: Ben Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;

Ben Hesed, in Arubboth ( Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);

Solomon’s provision for one day as thirty cors of fine flour, sixty measures of meal,
ten head of fat cattle, tenty head of cattle out of the pastures, and one hundred sheep, in addition to deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fol.
For he had dominion over all on this side of the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side of the River; and he had peace on all sides around him.
Judah and Israel lived safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and telve thousand horsemen.
Those officers provided food for King Solomon, and for all ho came to King Solomon’s table, every man in his month. They let nothing be lacking.
They also brought barley and stra for the horses and sift steeds to the place here the officers ere, each man according to his duty.
God gave Solomon abundant isdom, understanding, and breadth of mind like the sand that is on the seashore.

For he as iser than all men—iser than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his fame as in all the nations all around.

He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that gros out of the all; he also spoke of animals, of birds, of creeping things, and of fish.
People of all nations came to hear the isdom of Solomon, sent by all kings of the earth ho had heard of his isdom.
Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the place of his father, and Hiram had alays loved David.
Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

“You kno that David my father could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the ars hich ere around him on every side, until the LORD put his enemies under the soles of his feet.

Solomon gave Hiram tenty thousand cors of heat for food to his household, and tenty cors of pure oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year by year.
The LORD gave Solomon isdom, as he promised him. There as peace beteen Hiram and Solomon, and the to of them made a treaty together.

In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, hich is the second month, he began to build the LORD’s house.

The LORD’s ord came to Solomon, saying,

So Solomon built the house and finished it.

He built the alls of the house ithin ith boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the alls of the ceiling, he covered them on the inside ith ood. He covered the floor of the house ith cypress boards.

There as cedar on the house ithin, carved ith buds and open floers. All as cedar. No stone as visible.

Within the inner sanctuary as tenty cubits in length, and tenty cubits in idth, and tenty cubits in its height. He overlaid it ith pure gold. He covered the altar ith cedar.
So Solomon overlaid the house ithin ith pure gold. He dre chains of gold across before the inner sanctuary, and he overlaid it ith gold.
He overlaid the hole house ith gold, until all the house as finished. He also overlaid the hole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary ith gold.
In the inner sanctuary he made to cherubim of olive ood, each ten cubits high.
Five cubits as the length of one ing of the cherub, and five cubits as the length of the other ing of the cherub. From the tip of one ing to the tip of the other as ten cubits.
The other cherub as ten cubits. Both the cherubim ere of one measure and one form.
One cherub as ten cubits high, and so as the other cherub.

He set the cherubim ithin the inner house. The ings of the cherubim ere stretched out, so that the ing of the one touched the one all and the ing of the other cherub touched the other all; and their ings touched one another in the middle of the house.

So he made to doors of olive ood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open floers, and overlaid them ith gold. He spread the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.
He also made the entrance of the temple door posts of olive ood, out of a fourth part of the all,
and to doors of cypress ood. The to leaves of the one door ere folding, and the to leaves of the other door ere folding.
He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open floers; and he overlaid them ith gold fitted on the engraved ork.

In the eleventh year, in the month Bul, hich is the eighth month, the house as finished throughout all its parts and according to all its specifications. So he spent seven years building it.
Solomon as building his on house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
For he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Its length as one hundred cubits, its idth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, on four ros of cedar pillars, ith cedar beams on the pillars.

King Solomon sent and brought Hiram out of Tyre.

He as the son of a ido of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father as a man of Tyre, a orker in bronze; and he as filled ith isdom and understanding and skill to ork all orks in bronze. He came to King Solomon and performed all his ork.

The ork of the bases as like this: they had panels; and there ere panels beteen the ledges;
and on the panels that ere beteen the ledges ere lions, oxen, and cherubim; and on the ledges there as a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen ere reaths of hanging ork.

He made the ten bases in this ay: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one form.

Hiram made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram finished doing all the ork that he orked for King Solomon in the LORD’s house:
the to pillars; the to bols of the capitals that ere on the top of the pillars; the to netorks to cover the to bols of the capitals that ere on the top of the pillars;

the ten bases; the ten basins on the bases;
the one sea; the telve oxen under the sea;
the pots; the shovels; and the basins. All of these vessels, hich Hiram made for King Solomon for the LORD’s house, ere of burnished bronze.
The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground beteen Succoth and Zarethan.
Solomon left all the vessels uneighed, because there ere so many of them. The eight of the bronze could not be determined.
Solomon made all the vessels that ere in the LORD’s house: the golden altar and the table that the sho bread as on, of gold;
and the lamp stands, five on the right side and five on the left, in front of the inner sanctuary, of pure gold; and the floers, the lamps, and the tongs, of gold;

the cups, the snuffers, the basins, the spoons, and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, of the temple, of gold.

Thus all the ork that King Solomon did in the LORD’s house as finished. Solomon brought in the things hich David his father had dedicated— the silver, the gold, and the vessels— and put them in the treasuries of the LORD’s house.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel ith all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ households of the children of Israel, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the LORD’s covenant out of David’s city, hich is Zion.

All the elders of Israel came, and the priests picked up the ark.
They brought up the LORD’s ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that ere in the Tent. The priests and the Levites brought these up.
King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, ho ere assembled to him, ere ith him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.
The priests brought in the ark of the LORD’s covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, even under the cherubim’s ings.
For the cherubim spread their ings out over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles above.
The poles ere so long that the ends of the poles ere seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary, but they ere not seen outside. They are there to this day.
There as nothing in the ark except the to stone tablets hich Moses put there at Horeb, hen the LORD made a covenant ith the children of Israel, hen they came out of the land of Egypt.
It came to pass, hen the priests had come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the LORD’s house,
so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for the LORD’s glory filled the LORD’s house.
Then Solomon said, “ The LORD has said that he ould dell in the thick darkness.
I have surely built you a house of habitation, a place for you to dell in forever.”
The king turned his face around and blessed all the assembly of Israel; and all the assembly of Israel stood.
He said, “ Blessed is the LORD, the God of Israel, ho spoke ith his mouth to David your father, and has ith his hand fulfilled it, saying,

’ Since the day that I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.’
“ No it as in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to David my father, ’ Whereas it as in your heart to build a house for my name, you did ell that it as in your heart.
Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; but your son ho shall come out of your body, he shall build the house for my name.’

The LORD has established his ord that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
There I have set a place for the ark, in hich is the LORD’s covenant, hich he made ith our fathers hen he brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
Solomon stood before the LORD’s altar in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toard heaven;
and he said, “ LORD, the God of Israel, there is no God like you, in heaven above, or on earth beneath; ho keeps covenant and loving kindness ith your servants ho alk before you ith all their heart;
ho has kept ith your servant David my father that hich you promised him. Yes, you spoke ith your mouth, and have fulfilled it ith your hand, as it is today.

No therefore, may LORD, the God of Israel, keep ith your servant David my father that hich you have promised him, saying, ’ There shall not fail from you a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your children take heed to their ay, to alk before me as you have alked before me.’

The son of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six.
The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam, three.
The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven.
The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah the son of Shobal became the father of Jahath; and Jahath became the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites.
These ere the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. The name of their sister as Hazzelelponi.
Penuel as the father of Gedor and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur the father of Tekoa had to ives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These ere the sons of Naarah.
The sons of Helah ere Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz became the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
Jabez as more honorable than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez, saying, “ Because I bore him ith sorro.”

Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, “Oh that you ould bless me indeed, and enlarge my border! May your hand be ith me, and may you keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!” God granted him that hich he requested.
Chelub the brother of Shuhah became the father of Mehir, ho as the father of Eshton.
Eshton became the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir Nahash. These are the men of Recah.
The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath.
Meonothai became the father of Ophrah: and Seraiah became the father of Joab the father of Ge Harashim, for they ere craftsmen.
The sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz.
The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon; and Mered’s ife bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
His ife the Jeess bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, hom Mered took.
The sons of the ife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, ere the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth, and Ben Zoheth.
The sons of Shelah the son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of those ho orked fine linen, of the house of Ashbea;
and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, ho had dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These records are ancient.
These ere the potters, and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah; they lived there ith the king for his ork.
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul;
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son.
The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers didn’t have many children, and all their family didn’t multiply like the children of Judah.
They lived at Beersheba, Moladah, Hazarshual,
at Bilhah, at Ezem, at Tolad,
at Bethuel, at Hormah, at Ziklag,
at Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, at Beth Biri, and at Shaaraim. These ere their cities until David’s reign.
Their villages ere Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, five cities;
and all their villages that ere around the same cities, as far as Baal. These ere their settlements, and they kept their genealogy.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah the son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah—
these mentioned by name ere princes in their families. Their fathers’ houses increased greatly.
They ent to the entrance of Gedor, even to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
They found rich, good pasture, and the land as ide, and quiet, and peaceful, for those ho lived there before ere descended from Ham.

These ritten by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and struck their tents and the Meunim ho ere found there; and they destroyed them utterly to this day, and lived in their place, because there as pasture there for their flocks.
Some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, ent to Mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They struck the remnant of the Amalekites ho escaped, and have lived there to this day.

The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel ( for he as the firstborn, but because he defiled his father’s couch, his birthright as given to the sons of Joseph the son of Israel; and the genealogy is not to be listed according to the birthright.
For Judah prevailed above his brothers, and from him came the prince; but the birthright as Joseph’s)—
the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
and Beerah his son, hom Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria carried aay captive. He as prince of the Reubenites.
His brothers by their families, hen the genealogy of their generations as listed: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,
and Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel, ho lived in Aroer, even to Nebo and Baal Meon;
and he lived eastard even to the entrance of the ilderness from the river Euphrates, because their livestock ere multiplied in the land of Gilead.
In the days of Saul, they made ar ith the Hagrites, ho fell by their hand; and they lived in their tents throughout all the land east of Gilead.
The sons of Gad lived beside them in the land of Bashan to Salecah:
Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
Their brothers of their fathers’ houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven.
These ere the sons of Abihail, the son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz;
Ahi the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, chief of their fathers’ houses.
They lived in Gilead in Bashan and in its tons, and in all the pasture lands of Sharon as far as their borders.
All these ere listed by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sord, able to shoot ith bo, and skillful in ar, ere forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty that ere able to go out to ar.
They made ar ith the Hagrites, ith Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
They ere helped against them, and the Hagrites ere delivered into their hand, and all ho ere ith them; for they cried to God in the battle, and he ansered them because they put their trust in him.
They took aay their livestock: of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep to hundred fifty thousand, and of donkeys to thousand, and of men one hundred thousand.
For many fell slain, because the ar as of God. They lived in their place until the captivity.
The children of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They increased from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
These ere the heads of their fathers’ houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel— mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of their fathers’ houses.
They trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the prostitute after the gods of the peoples of the land hom God destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried aay the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and to the river of Gozan, to this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar became the father of Phinehas, Phinehas became the father of Abishua,
Abishua became the father of Bukki. Bukki became the father of Uzzi.
Uzzi became the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah became the father of Meraioth.
Meraioth became the father of Amariah. Amariah became the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz became the father of Azariah. Azariah became the father of Johanan.
Johanan became the father of Azariah, ho executed the priest’s office in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah became the father of Amariah. Amariah became the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Shallum.
Shallum became the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah became the father of Azariah.
Azariah became the father of Seraiah. Seraiah became the father of Jehozadak.
Jehozadak ent into captivity hen the LORD carried Judah and Jerusalem aay by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath ere Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their fathers’ households.
Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, and Jeatherai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,
Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son.
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.
As for Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah: Zophai his son, Nahath his son,
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, and Elkanah his son.
The sons of Samuel: the firstborn, Joel, and the second, Abijah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
These are they hom David set over the service of song in the LORD’s house after the ark came to rest there.
They ministered ith song before the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting until Solomon had built the LORD’s house in Jerusalem. They performed the duties of their office according to their order.
These are those ho served, and their sons. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.
His brother Asaph, ho stood on his right hand, even Asaph the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
On the left hand their brothers the sons of Merari: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
Their brothers the Levites ere appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of God’s house.

But Aaron and his sons offered on the altar of burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, for all the ork of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.
No these are their delling places according to their encampments in their borders: to the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites (for theirs as the first lot),
to them they gave Hebron in the land of Judah, and its pasture lands around it;
but the fields of the city and its villages, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge, Hebron, Libnah also ith its pasture lands, Jattir, Eshtemoa ith its pasture lands,
Hilen ith its pasture lands, Debir ith its pasture lands,
Ashan ith its pasture lands, and Beth Shemesh ith its pasture lands;
and out of the tribe of Benjamin, Geba ith its pasture lands, Allemeth ith its pasture lands, and Anathoth ith its pasture lands. All their cities throughout their families ere thirteen cities.
To the rest of the sons of Kohath ere given by lot, out of the family of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities.

To the sons of Gershom, according to their families, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
To the sons of Merari ere given by lot, according to their families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, telve cities.
The children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities ith their pasture lands.
They gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities hich are mentioned by name.
Some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave to them the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim ith its pasture lands and Gezer ith its pasture lands,
Jokmeam ith its pasture lands, Beth Horon ith its pasture lands,
Aijalon ith its pasture lands, Gath Rimmon ith its pasture lands;
and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner ith its pasture lands, and Bileam ith its pasture lands, for the rest of the family of the sons of Kohath.
To the sons of Gershom ere given, out of the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan ith its pasture lands, and Ashtaroth ith its pasture lands;
and out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh ith its pasture lands, Daberath ith its pasture lands,
Ramoth ith its pasture lands, and Anem ith its pasture lands;
and out of the tribe of Asher, Mashal ith its pasture lands, Abdon ith its pasture lands,
Hukok ith its pasture lands, and Rehob ith its pasture lands;
and out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee ith its pasture lands, Hammon ith its pasture lands, and Kiriathaim ith its pasture lands.
To the rest of the Levites, the sons of Merari, ere given, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono ith its pasture lands, and Tabor ith its pasture lands;
and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, ere given them out of the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the ilderness ith its pasture lands, Jahzah ith its pasture lands,
Kedemoth ith its pasture lands, and Mephaath ith its pasture lands;
and out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead ith its pasture lands, Mahanaim ith its pasture lands,
Heshbon ith its pasture lands, and Jazer ith its pasture lands.
Of the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their fathers’ houses, of Tola; mighty men of valor in their generations. Their number in the days of David as tenty-to thousand six hundred.
The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five; all of them chief men.
With them, by their generations, after their fathers’ houses, ere bands of the army for ar, thirty-six thousand; for they had many ives and sons.
Their brothers among all the families of Issachar, mighty men of valor, listed in all by genealogy, ere eighty-seven thousand.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, five; heads of fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor; and they ere listed by genealogy tenty-to thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these ere the sons of Becher.
They ere listed by genealogy, after their generations, heads of their fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor, tenty thousand to hundred.
The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these ere sons of Jediael, according to the heads of their fathers’ households, mighty men of valor, seventeen thousand to hundred, ho ere able to go out in the army for ar.
So ere Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, and the sons of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, hom his concubine the Aramitess bore. She bore Machir the father of Gilead.
Machir took a ife of Huppim and Shuppim, hose sister’s name as Maacah. The name of the second as Zelophehad; and Zelophehad had daughters.
Maacah the ife of Machir bore a son, and she named him Peresh. The name of his brother as Sheresh; and his sons ere Ulam and Rakem.
The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These ere the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida ere Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, Ezer, and Elead, hom the men of Gath ho ere born in the land killed, because they came don to take aay their livestock.
Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He ent in to his ife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he named him Beriah, because there as trouble ith his house.
His daughter as Sheerah, ho built Beth Horon the loer and the upper, and Uzzen Sheerah.
Rephah as his son, Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, and Joshua his son.
Their possessions and settlements ere Bethel and its tons, and eastard Naaran, and estard Gezer ith its tons; Shechem also and its tons, to Azzah and its tons;
and by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth Shean and its tons, Taanach and its tons, Megiddo and its tons, and Dor and its tons. The children of Joseph the son of Israel lived in these.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah as their sister.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, ho as the father of Birzaith.
Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.

All these ere the children of Asher, heads of the fathers’ houses, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes. The number of them listed by genealogy for service in ar as tenty-six thousand men.
Benjamin became the father of Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These are the sons of Ehud. These are the heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Geba, ho ere carried captive to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, ho carried them captive; and he became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim became the father of children in the field of Moab, after he had sent them aay. Hushim and Baara ere his ives.
By Hodesh his ife, he became the father of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirmah. These ere his sons, heads of fathers’ households.
By Hushim, he became the father of Abitub and Elpaal.
The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, ho built Ono and Lod, ith its tons;
and Beriah and Shema, ho ere heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Aijalon, ho put to flight the inhabitants of Gath;
and Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, Joha, the sons of Beriah,
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Izliah, Jobab, the sons of Elpaal,
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, Shimrath, the sons of Shimei,
Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
Iphdeiah, Penuel, the sons of Shashak,
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
Jaareshiah, Elijah, Zichri, and the sons of Jeroham.
These ere heads of fathers’ households throughout their generations, chief men. These lived in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon, hose ife’s name as Maacah, lived in Gibeon
ith his firstborn son Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
and Mikloth, ho became the father of Shimeah. They also lived ith their families in Jerusalem, near their relatives.
Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan as Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz became the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea. Raphah as his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
Azel had six sons, hose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these ere the sons of Azel.
The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
The sons of Ulam ere mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons, and grandsons, one hundred fifty. All these ere of the sons of Benjamin.
So all Israel ere listed by genealogies; and behold, they are ritten in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah as carried aay captive to Babylon for their disobedience.
No the first inhabitants ho lived in their possessions in their cities ere Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.
In Jerusalem, there lived of the children of Judah, of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim and Manasseh:
Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Perez the son of Judah.
Of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their brothers, six hundred ninety.
Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah;
and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri; and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;
and their brothers, according to their generations, nine hundred fifty-six. All these men ere heads of fathers’ households by their fathers’ houses.
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of God’s house;
and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah; and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
and their brothers, heads of their fathers’ houses, one thousand seven hundred sixty; they ere very able men for the ork of the service of God’s house.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;
and Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph,
and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, ho lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers ( Shallum as the chief),
ho previously served in the king’s gate eastard. They ere the gatekeepers for the camp of the children of Levi.

Shallum as the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brothers, of his father’s house, the Korahites, ere over the ork of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers had been over the LORD’s camp, keepers of the entry.
Phinehas the son of Eleazar as ruler over them in time past, and the LORD as ith him.
Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah as gatekeeper of the door of the Tent of Meeting.
All these ho ere chosen to be gatekeepers in the thresholds ere to hundred telve. These ere listed by genealogy in their villages, hom David and Samuel the seer ordained in their office of trust.
So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the LORD’s house, even the house of the tent, as guards.
On the four sides ere the gatekeepers, toard the east, est, north, and south.
Their brothers, in their villages, ere to come in every seven days from time to time to be ith them,
for the four chief gatekeepers, ho ere Levites, ere in an office of trust, and ere over the rooms and over the treasuries in God’s house.
They stayed around God’s house, because that as their duty; and it as their duty to open it morning by morning.
Certain of them ere in charge of the vessels of service, for these ere brought in by count, and these ere taken out by count.
Some of them also ere appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, over the fine flour, the ine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
Some of the sons of the priests prepared the mixing of the spices.
