a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for ar, and a time for peace.
What profit has he ho orks in that in hich he labors?
I have seen the burden hich God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted ith.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the ork that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
I kno that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.
Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
I kno that hatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
That hich is has been long ago, and that hich is to be has been long ago. God seeks again that hich is passed aay.
Moreover I sa under the sun, in the place of justice, that ickedness as there; and in the place of righteousness, that ickedness as there.
I said in my heart, “God ill judge the righteous and the icked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every ork.”
I said in my heart, “ As for the sons of men, God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like animals.

For that hich happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals, for all is vanity.
All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.
Who knos the spirit of man, hether it goes upard, and the spirit of the animal, hether it goes donard to the earth?”
Therefore I sa that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his orks, for that is his portion; for ho can bring him to see hat ill be after him?

Then I returned and sa all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold, the tears of those ho ere oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there as poer; but they had no comforter.
Therefore I praised the dead ho have been long dead more than the living ho are yet alive.
Yes, better than them both is him ho has not yet been, ho has not seen the evil ork that is done under the sun.
Then I sa all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after ind.
The fool folds his hands together and ruins himself.
Better is a handful, ith quietness, than to handfuls ith labor and chasing after ind.
Then I returned and sa vanity under the sun.

There is one ho is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied ith ealth. “ For hom then do I labor and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
To are better than one, because they have a good reard for their labor.
For if they fall, the one ill lift up his fello; but oe to him ho is alone hen he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
Again, if to lie together, then they have armth; but ho can one keep arm alone?
If a man prevails against one ho is alone, to shall ithstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Better is a poor and ise youth than an old and foolish king ho doesn’t kno ho to receive admonition any more.
For out of prison he came out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he as born poor.
I sa all the living ho alk under the sun, that they ere ith the youth, the other, ho succeeded him.
There as no end of all the people, even of all them over hom he as— yet those ho come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after ind.
Guard your steps hen you go to God’s house; for to dra near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t kno that they do evil.
Don’t be rash ith your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your ords be fe.
For as a dream comes ith a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech ith a multitude of ords.
When you vo a vo to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that hich you vo.
It is better that you should not vo, than that you should vo and not pay.
Don’t allo your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this as a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the ork of your hands?
For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as ell as in many ords; but you must fear God.

If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking aay of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter, for one official is eyed by a higher one, and there are officials over them.
Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
He ho loves silver shall not be satisfied ith silver, nor he ho loves abundance, ith increase. This also is vanity.
When goods increase, those ho eat them are increased; and hat advantage is there to its oner, except to feast on them ith his eyes?
The sleep of a laboring man is seet, hether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich ill not allo him to sleep.
There is a grievous evil hich I have seen under the sun: ealth kept by its oner to his harm.
Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
As he came out of his mother’s omb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, hich he may carry aay in his hand.
This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And hat profit does he have ho labors for the ind?
All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and rath.

Behold, that hich I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in hich he labors under the sun, all the days of his life hich God has given him; for this is his portion.
Every man also to hom God has given riches and ealth, and has given him poer to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor— this is the gift of God.
For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life, because God occupies him ith the joy of his heart.
There is an evil hich I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men:

a man to hom God gives riches, ealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no poer to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled ith good, and moreover he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he;
for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered ith darkness.
Moreover it has not seen the sun nor knon it. This has rest rather than the other.
Yes, though he live a thousand years tice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, don’t all go to one place?
All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
For hat advantage has the ise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knos ho to alk before the living?
Better is the sight of the eyes than the andering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after ind.
Whatever has been, its name as given long ago; and it is knon hat man is; neither can he contend ith him ho is mightier than he.
For there are many ords that create vanity. What does that profit man?
For ho knos hat is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life hich he spends like a shado? For ho can tell a man hat ill be after him under the sun?
A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorro is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
The heart of the ise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the ise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
Surely extortion makes the ise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
Don’t say, “ Why ere the former days better than these?” For you do not ask isely about this.
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those ho see the sun.
For isdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knoledge is that isdom preserves the life of him ho has it.
Consider the ork of God, for ho can make that straight hich he has made crooked?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side ith the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man ho perishes in his righteousness, and there is a icked man ho lives long in his evildoing.
Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly ise. Why should you destroy yourself?
Don’t be too icked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also don’t ithdra your hand from that; for he ho fears God ill come out of them all.
Wisdom is a strength to the ise man more than ten rulers ho are in a city.
Surely there is not a righteous man on earth ho does good and doesn’t sin.
Also don’t take heed to all ords that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you;
for often your on heart knos that you yourself have likeise cursed others.
All this I have proved in isdom. I said, “ I ill be ise;” but it as far from me.
That hich is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
I turned around, and my heart sought to kno and to search out, and to seek isdom and the scheme of things, and to kno that ickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
I find more bitter than death the oman hose heart is snares and traps, hose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner ill be ensnared by her.
“ Behold, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “ to one another, to find an explanation
hich my soul still seeks, but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a oman among all those.
Behold, I have only found this: that God made mankind upright; but they search for many inventions.”
Who is like the ise man? And ho knos the interpretation of a thing? A man’s isdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
I say, “ Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
Don’t be hasty to go out of his presence. Don’t persist in an evil thing, for he does hatever pleases him,
for the king’s ord is supreme. Who can say to him, “ What are you doing?”
Whoever keeps the commandment shall not come to harm, and his ise heart ill kno the time and procedure.
For there is a time and procedure for every purpose, although the misery of man is heavy on him.
For he doesn’t kno that hich ill be; for ho can tell him ho it ill be?
There is no man ho has poer over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have poer over the day of death. There is no discharge in ar; neither shall ickedness deliver those ho practice it.
All this I have seen, and applied my mind to every ork that is done under the sun. There is a time in hich one man has poer over another to his hurt.
So I sa the icked buried. Indeed they came also from holiness. They ent and ere forgotten in the city here they did this. This also is vanity.
Because sentence against an evil ork is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I kno that it ill be better ith those ho fear God, ho are reverent before him.
But it shall not be ell ith the icked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shado, because he doesn’t fear God.

There is a vanity hich is done on the earth, that there are righteous men to hom it happens according to the ork of the icked. Again, there are icked men to hom it happens according to the ork of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, to drink, and to be joyful: for that ill accompany him in his labor all the days of his life hich God has given him under the sun.
When I applied my heart to kno isdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth ( even though eyes see no sleep day or night),

then I sa all the ork of God, that man can’t find out the ork that is done under the sun, because hoever much a man labors to seek it out, yet he on’t find it. Yes even though a ise man thinks he can comprehend it, he on’t be able to find it.

For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the ise, and their orks, are in the hand of God; hether it is love or hatred, man doesn’t kno it; all is before them.

All things come alike to all. There is one event to the righteous and to the icked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to him ho sacrifices, and to him ho doesn’t sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; he ho takes an oath, as he ho fears an oath.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all. Yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart hile they live, and after that they go to the dead.
For to him ho is joined ith all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living kno that they ill die, but the dead don’t kno anything, neither do they have any more a reard; for their memory is forgotten.
Also their love, their hatred, and their envy has perished long ago; neither do they any longer have a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.
Go your ay— eat your bread ith joy, and drink your ine ith a merry heart; for God has already accepted your orks.
Let your garments be alays hite, and don’t let your head lack oil.

Live joyfully ith the ife hom you love all the days of your life of vanity, hich he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity, for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in hich you labor under the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it ith your might; for there is no ork, nor plan, nor knoledge, nor isdom, in Sheol, here you are going.

I returned and sa under the sun that the race is not to the sift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the ise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.

For man also doesn’t kno his time. As the fish that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, hen it falls suddenly on them.
I have also seen isdom under the sun in this ay, and it seemed great to me.
There as a little city, and fe men ithin it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great bularks against it.
No a poor ise man as found in it, and he by his isdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
Then I said, “ Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s isdom is despised, and his ords are not heard.
The ords of the ise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him ho rules among fools.
Wisdom is better than eapons of ar; but one sinner destroys much good.
Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outeigh isdom and honor.
A ise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
Yes also hen the fool alks by the ay, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
There is an evil hich I have seen under the sun, the sort of error hich proceeds from the ruler.
Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a lo place.
I have seen servants on horses, and princes alking like servants on the earth.
He ho digs a pit may fall into it; and hoever breaks through a all may be bitten by a snake.
Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits ood may be endangered by it.
If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
The ords of a ise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is salloed by his on lips.
The beginning of the ords of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
A fool also multiplies ords. Man doesn’t kno hat ill be; and that hich ill be after him, ho can tell him?
The labor of fools earies every one of them; for he doesn’t kno ho to go to the city.
Woe to you, land, hen your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
Happy are you, land, hen your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
A feast is made for laughter, and ine makes the life glad; and money is the anser for all things.
Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that hich has ings may tell the matter.
Cast your bread on the aters; for you shall find it after many days.
Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight; for you don’t kno hat evil ill be on the earth.
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toard the south, or toard the north, in the place here the tree falls, there shall it be.
He ho observes the ind on’t so; and he ho regards the clouds on’t reap.
As you don’t kno hat is the ay of the ind, nor ho the bones gro in the omb of her ho is ith child; even so you don’t kno the ork of God ho does all.
In the morning so your seed, and in the evening don’t ithhold your hand; for you don’t kno hich ill prosper, hether this or that, or hether they both ill be equally good.
Truly the light is seet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.
Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and alk in the ays of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes; but kno that for all these things God ill bring you into judgment.
Therefore remove sorro from your heart, and put aay evil from your flesh; for youth and the dan of life are vanity.
Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years dra near, hen you ill say, “ I have no pleasure in them;”
Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
in the day hen the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bo themselves, and the grinders cease because they are fe, and those ho look out of the indos are darkened,
and the doors shall be shut in the street; hen the sound of the grinding is lo, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought lo;

yes, they shall be afraid of heights, and terrors ill be on the ay; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets;
before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bol is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the heel broken at the cistern,
and the dust returns to the earth as it as, and the spirit returns to God ho gave it.
“ Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher. “ All is vanity!”
Further, because the Preacher as ise, he still taught the people knoledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
The Preacher sought to find out acceptable ords, and that hich as ritten blamelessly, ords of truth.
The ords of the ise are like goads; and like nails ell fastened are ords from the masters of assemblies, hich are given from one shepherd.
Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a eariness of the flesh.
This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the hole duty of man.
For God ill bring every ork into judgment, ith every hidden thing, hether it is good, or hether it is evil.
The Song of songs, hich is Solomon’s. \sp Beloved
Let him kiss me ith the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than ine.
Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.
Take me aay ith you. Let’s hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. \sp Friends We ill be glad and rejoice in you. We ill praise your love more than ine! \sp Beloved They are right to love you.
I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.
Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons ere angry ith me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my on vineyard.
Tell me, you hom my soul loves, here you graze your flock, here you rest them at noon; for hy should I be as one ho is veiled beside the flocks of your companions? \sp Lover
If you don’t kno, most beautiful among omen, follo the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents. \b
I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
Your cheeks are beautiful ith earrings, your neck ith strings of jeels. \sp Friends
We ill make you earrings of gold, ith studs of silver. \sp Beloved
While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies beteen my breasts.
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi. \sp Lover
Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves. \sp Beloved
Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant. \sp Lover
The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.
I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys. \sp Lover
As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters. \sp Beloved
As the apple tree among the trees of the ood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat don under his shado ith great delight, his fruit as seet to my taste.
He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
Strengthen me ith raisins, refresh me ith apples; for I am faint ith love.
His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor aaken love, until it so desires. \b
The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our all! He looks in at the indos. He glances through the lattice. \b
My beloved spoke, and said to me, “ Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come aay.
For behold, the inter is past. The rain is over and gone.
The floers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come aay.” \sp Lover
My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is seet and your face is lovely.
Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom. \sp Beloved
My beloved is mine, and I am his. He broses among the lilies.
Until the day is cool, and the shados flee aay, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
By night on my bed, I sought him hom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
I ill get up no, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I ill seek him hom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
The atchmen ho go about the city found me; “ Have you seen him hom my soul loves?”
I had scarcely passed from them, hen I found him hom my soul loves. I held him, and ould not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her ho conceived me. \b
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor aaken love, until it so desires. \b
Who is this ho comes up from the ilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed ith myrrh and frankincense, ith all spices of the merchant?
Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
They all handle the sord, and are expert in ar. Every man has his sord on his thigh, because of fear in the night. \b
King Solomon made himself a carriage of the ood of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved ith love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, ith the cron ith hich his mother has croned him, in the day of his eddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a nely shorn flock, hich have come up from the ashing, here every one of them has tins. None is bereaved among them.
Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
Your neck is like David’s toer built for an armory, on hich a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.
Your to breasts are like to fans that are tins of a roe, hich feed among the lilies. \b
Until the day is cool, and the shados flee aay, I ill go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense. \b
You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.
Come ith me from Lebanon, my bride, ith me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards. \b
You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart ith one of your eyes, ith one chain of your neck.
Ho beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! Ho much better is your love than ine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!
Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, ith precious fruits, henna ith spikenard plants,
spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, ith every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, ith all the best spices,
a fountain of gardens, a ell of living aters, floing streams from Lebanon. \sp Beloved
Aake, north ind, and come, you south! Blo on my garden, that its spices may flo out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.

I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh ith my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb ith my honey; I have drunk my ine ith my milk. \sp Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved. \sp Beloved

I as asleep, but my heart as aake. It is the voice of my beloved ho knocks: “ Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled ith de, and my hair ith the dampness of the night.”
I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have ashed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped ith myrrh, my fingers ith liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone aay. My heart ent out hen he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t anser.
The atchmen ho go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the alls took my cloak aay from me. \b
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint ith love. \sp Friends
Ho is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among omen? Ho is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us? \sp Beloved
My beloved is hite and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside the ater brooks, ashed ith milk, mounted like jeels.

But no the LORD ho created you, Jacob, and he ho formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.

ho brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the mighty man ( they lie don together, they shall not rise; they are extinct, they are quenched like a ick) says:

Yet listen no, Jacob my servant, and Israel, hom I have chosen.

Everyone ho makes a carved image is vain. The things that they delight in ill not profit. Their on itnesses don’t see, nor kno, that they may be disappointed.

The carpenter stretches out a line. He marks it out ith a pencil. He shapes it ith planes. He marks it out ith compasses, and shapes it like the figure of a man, ith the beauty of a man, to reside in a house.
He cuts don cedars for himself, and takes the cypress and the oak, and strengthens for himself one among the trees of the forest. He plants a cypress tree, and the rain nourishes it.
Then it ill be for a man to burn; and he takes some of it and arms himself. Yes, he burns it and bakes bread. Yes, he makes a god and orships it; he makes it a carved image, and falls don to it.
He burns part of it in the fire. With part of it, he eats meat. He roasts a roast and is satisfied. Yes, he arms himself and says, “ Aha! I am arm. I have seen the fire.”
The rest of it he makes into a god, even his engraved image. He bos don to it and orships, and prays to it, and says, “ Deliver me, for you are my god!” \b
They don’t kno, neither do they consider, for he has shut their eyes, that they can’t see, and their hearts, that they can’t understand.

No one thinks, neither is there knoledge nor understanding to say, “ I have burned part of it in the fire. Yes, I have also baked bread on its coals. I have roasted meat and eaten it. Shall I make the rest of it into an abomination? Shall I bo don to a tree trunk?”

Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I have formed you. You are my servant. Israel, you ill not be forgotten by me.

The LORD, your Redeemer, and he ho formed you from the omb says: “ I am the LORD, ho makes all things; ho alone stretches out the heavens; ho spreads out the earth by myself;
ho frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; ho turns ise men backard, and makes their knoledge foolish;

ho confirms the ord of his servant, and performs the counsel of his messengers; ho says of Jerusalem, ’ She ill be inhabited;’ and of the cities of Judah, ’ They ill be built,’ and ’ I ill raise up its aste places;’
ho says to the deep, ’Be dry,’ and ’I ill dry up your rivers,’
ho says of Cyrus, ’ He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure,’ even saying of Jerusalem, ’She ill be built;’ and of the temple, ’ Your foundation ill be laid.’”
The LORD says to his anointed, to Cyrus, hose right hand I have held to subdue nations before him and strip kings of their armor, to open the doors before him, and the gates shall not be shut:
“ I ill go before you and make the rough places smooth. I ill break the doors of bronze in pieces and cut apart the bars of iron.

that they may kno from the rising of the sun, and from the est, that there is no one besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no one else.

Rain, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour don righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may produce salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up ith it. I, the LORD, have created it. \b

Woe to him ho says to a father, ’ What have you become the father of?’ or to a mother, ’ What have you given birth to?’” \b
The LORD, the Holy One of Israel and his Maker says: “ You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the ork of my hands!

The Lord GOD says, “ Behold, I ill lift up my hand to the nations, and lift up my banner to the peoples. They shall bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders.

“ Listen to me, my people; and hear me, my nation, for a la ill go out from me, and I ill establish my justice for a light to the peoples.

“ I, even I, am he ho comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man ho shall die, and of the son of man ho ill be made as grass?

“ Sing, barren, you ho didn’t give birth! Break out into singing, and cry aloud, you ho didn’t travail ith child! For more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married ife,” says the LORD.

For you ill spread out on the right hand and on the left; and your offspring ill possess the nations and settle in desolate cities. \b
“Don’t be afraid, for you ill not be ashamed. Don’t be confounded, for you ill not be disappointed. For you ill forget the shame of your youth. You ill remember the reproach of your idohood no more.

“ For a small moment I have forsaken you, but I ill gather you ith great mercies.
In overfloing rath I hid my face from you for a moment, but ith everlasting loving kindness I ill have mercy on you,” says the LORD your Redeemer. \b
“ For this is like the aters of Noah to me; for as I have sorn that the aters of Noah ill no more go over the earth, so I have sorn that I ill not be angry ith you, nor rebuke you.
For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed, but my loving kindness ill not depart from you, and my covenant of peace ill not be removed,” says the LORD ho has mercy on you. \b
“ You afflicted, tossed ith storms, and not comforted, behold, I ill set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations ith sapphires.
I ill make your pinnacles of rubies, your gates of sparkling jeels, and all your alls of precious stones.
All your children ill be taught by the LORD, and your children’s peace ill be great.

Behold, they may gather together, but not by me. Whoever gathers together against you ill fall because of you. \b
“ Behold, I have created the blacksmith ho fans the coals into flame, and forges a eapon for his ork; and I have created the destroyer to destroy.

No eapon that is formed against you ill prevail; and you ill condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the LORD’s servants, and their righteousness is of me,” says the LORD.
“ Hey! Come, everyone ho thirsts, to the aters! Come, he ho has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy ine and milk ithout money and ithout price.
Why do you spend money for that hich is not bread, and your labor for that hich doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that hich is good, and let your soul delight itself in richness.

Behold, I have given him for a itness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.
Behold, you shall call a nation that you don’t kno; and a nation that didn’t kno you shall run to you, because of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has glorified you.” \b
Seek the LORD hile he may be found. Call on him hile he is near.
Let the icked forsake his ay, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to the LORD, and he ill have mercy on him, to our God, for he ill freely pardon. \b
“ For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ays are not my ays,” says the LORD.
“ For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ays higher than your ays, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain comes don and the sno from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but aters the earth, and makes it gro and bud, and gives seed to the soer and bread to the eater;
so is my ord that goes out of my mouth: it ill not return to me void, but it ill accomplish that hich I please, and it ill prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
For you shall go out ith joy, and be led out ith peace. The mountains and the hills ill break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields ill clap their hands.
Instead of the thorn the cypress tree ill come up; and instead of the brier the myrtle tree ill come up. It ill make a name for the LORD, for an everlasting sign that ill not be cut off.”
The LORD says: “ Maintain justice and do hat is right, for my salvation is near and my righteousness ill soon be revealed.
Blessed is the man ho does this, and the son of man ho holds it fast; ho keeps the Sabbath ithout profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” \b
Let no foreigner ho has joined himself to the LORD speak, saying, “ The LORD ill surely separate me from his people.” Do not let the eunuch say, “ Behold, I am a dry tree.” \b
For the LORD says, “ To the eunuchs ho keep my Sabbaths, choose the things that please me, and hold fast to my covenant,
I ill give them in my house and ithin my alls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters. I ill give them an everlasting name that ill not be cut off. \b
Also the foreigners ho join themselves to the LORD to serve him, and to love the LORD’s name, to be his servants, everyone ho keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and holds fast my covenant,

I ill bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices ill be accepted on my altar; for my house ill be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”
The Lord GOD, ho gathers the outcasts of Israel, says, “ I ill yet gather others to him, in addition to his on ho are gathered.” \b
All you animals of the field, come to devour, all you animals in the forest.
His atchmen are blind. They are all ithout knoledge. They are all mute dogs. They can’t bark— dreaming, lying don, loving to slumber.

“ Come,” they say, “ I ill get ine, and e ill fill ourselves ith strong drink; and tomorro ill be as today, great beyond measure.”

He enters into peace. They rest in their beds, each one ho alks in his uprightness. \b
“ But dra near here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes.
Whom do you mock? Against hom do you make a ide mouth and stick out your tongue? Aren’t you children of disobedience and offspring of falsehood,

Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion. They, they are your lot. You have even poured a drink offering to them. You have offered an offering. Shall I be appeased for these things?

You have set up your memorial behind the doors and the posts, for you have exposed yourself to someone besides me, and have gone up. You have enlarged your bed and made a covenant for yourself ith them. You loved hat you sa on their bed.

and give him no rest until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise on the earth. \b

The LORD has sorn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, “ Surely I ill no more give your grain to be food for your enemies, and foreigners ill not drink your ne ine, for hich you have labored,
but those ho have harvested it ill eat it, and praise the LORD. Those ho have gathered it ill drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.” \b
Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the ay of the people! Build up, build up the highay! Gather out the stones! Lift up a banner for the peoples.

Who is this ho comes from Edom, ith dyed garments from Bozrah? Who is this ho is glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? “ It is I ho speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”

I ill tell of the loving kindnesses of the LORD and the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has given to us, and the great goodness toard the house of Israel, hich he has given to them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he said, “ Surely, they are my people, children ho ill not deal falsely;” so he became their Savior.

But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. Therefore he turned and became their enemy, and he himself fought against them. \b
Then he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, “Where is he ho brought them up out of the sea ith the shepherds of his flock? Where is he ho put his Holy Spirit among them?”
Who caused his glorious arm to be at Moses’ right hand? Who divided the aters before them, to make himself an everlasting name?
Who led them through the depths, like a horse in the ilderness, so that they didn’t stumble?

Look don from heaven, and see from the habitation of your holiness and of your glory. Where are your zeal and your mighty acts? The yearning of your heart and your compassion is restrained toard me.
For you are our Father, though Abraham doesn’t kno us, and Israel does not acknoledge us. You, LORD, are our Father. Our Redeemer from everlasting is your name.
O LORD, hy do you make us ander from your ays, and harden our heart from your fear? Return for your servants’ sake, the tribes of your inheritance.

Oh that you ould tear the heavens, that you ould come don, that the mountains might quake at your presence—
as hen fire kindles the brushood, and the fire causes the ater to boil. Make your name knon to your adversaries, that the nations may tremble at your presence!

The LORD said this to me: “ Go and stand in the gate of the children of the people, through hich the kings of Judah come in and by hich they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem.
Tell them, ’ Hear the LORD’s ord, you kings of Judah, all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that enter in by these gates:
The LORD says, “ Be careful, and bear no burden on the Sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem.
Don’t carry a burden out of your houses on the Sabbath day. Don’t do any ork, but make the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.

It ill happen, if you diligently listen to me,” says the LORD, “ to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but to make the Sabbath day holy, to do no ork therein;

then there ill enter in by the gates of this city kings and princes sitting on David’s throne, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their princes, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city ill remain forever.

They ill come from the cities of Judah, and from the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the loland, from the hill country, and from the South, bringing burnt offerings, sacrifices, meal offerings, and frankincense, and bringing sacrifices of thanksgiving to the LORD’s house.

But if you ill not listen to me to make the Sabbath day holy, and not to bear a burden and enter in at the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I ill kindle a fire in its gates, and it ill devour the palaces of Jerusalem. It ill not be quenched.”’”
The ord hich came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
“ Arise, and go don to the potter’s house, and there I ill cause you to hear my ords.”
Then I ent don to the potter’s house, and behold, he as making something on the heels.

Then the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

if that nation, concerning hich I have spoken, turns from their evil, I ill repent of the evil that I thought to do to them.

“ No therefore, speak to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, ’ The LORD says: “ Behold, I frame evil against you, and devise a plan against you. Everyone return from his evil ay no, and amend your ays and your doings.”’
But they say, ’ It is in vain; for e ill alk after our on plans, and e ill each follo the stubbornness of his evil heart.’”

“ Then you shall break the container in the sight of the men ho go ith you,

ho has ithdran his hand from the poor, ho hasn’t received interest or increase, has executed my ordinances, has alked in my statutes;
As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, robbed his brother, and did that hich is not good among his people, behold, he ill die in his iniquity.
“ Yet you say, ’ Why doesn’t the son bear the iniquity of the father?’ When the son has done that hich is laful and right, and has kept all my statutes, and has done them, he ill surely live.

The soul ho sins, he shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be on him, and the ickedness of the icked shall be on him.
“ But if the icked turns from all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all my statutes, and does that hich is laful and right, he shall surely live. He shall not die.
None of his transgressions that he has committed ill be remembered against him. In his righteousness that he has done, he shall live.
Have I any pleasure in the death of the icked?” says the Lord GOD, “ and not rather that he should return from his ay, and live?

“ But hen the righteous turns aay from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the icked man does, should he live? None of his righteous deeds that he has done ill be remembered. In his trespass that he has trespassed, and in his sin that he has sinned, in them he shall die.
“ Yet you say, ’ The ay of the Lord is not equal.’ Hear no, house of Israel: Is my ay not equal? Aren’t your ays unequal?
When the righteous man turns aay from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and dies in it, then he dies in his iniquity that he has done.
Again, hen the icked man turns aay from his ickedness that he has committed, and does that hich is laful and right, he ill save his soul alive.
Because he considers, and turns aay from all his transgressions that he has committed, he shall surely live. He shall not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, ’ The ay of the Lord is not fair.’ House of Israel, aren’t my ays fair? Aren’t your ays unfair?
“ Therefore I ill judge you, house of Israel, everyone according to his ays,” says the Lord GOD. “ Return, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions, so iniquity ill not be your ruin.
Cast aay from you all your transgressions in hich you have transgressed; and make yourself a ne heart and a ne spirit. For hy ill you die, house of Israel?
For I have no pleasure in the death of him ho dies,” says the Lord GOD. “ Therefore turn yourselves, and live!
“Moreover, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,
and say, ’ What as your mother? A lioness. She couched among lions, in the middle of the young lions she nourished her cubs.
She brought up one of her cubs. He became a young lion. He learned to catch the prey. He devoured men.
The nations also heard of him. He as taken in their pit; and they brought him ith hooks to the land of Egypt. \b
“’ No hen she sa that she had aited, and her hope as lost, then she took another of her cubs, and made him a young lion.
He ent up and don among the lions. He became a young lion. He learned to catch the prey. He devoured men.
He kne their palaces, and laid aste their cities. The land as desolate ith its fullness, because of the noise of his roaring.
Then the nations attacked him on every side from the provinces. They spread their net over him. He as taken in their pit.
They put him in a cage ith hooks, and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into strongholds, so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel. \b
“’ Your mother as like a vine in your blood, planted by the aters. It as fruitful and full of branches by reason of many aters.
It had strong branches for the scepters of those ho ruled. Their stature as exalted among the thick boughs. They ere seen in their height ith the multitude of their branches.
But it as plucked up in fury. It as cast don to the ground, and the east ind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches ere broken off and ithered. The fire consumed them.
No it is planted in the ilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
Fire has gone out of its branches. It has devoured its fruit, so that there is in it no strong branch to be a scepter to rule.’
In the seventh year, in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and sat before me.
The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and tell them, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ Is it to inquire of me that you have come? As I live,” says the Lord GOD, “ I ill not be inquired of by you.”’
“ Will you judge them, son of man? Will you judge them? Cause them to kno the abominations of their fathers.

Tell them, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ In the day hen I chose Israel, and sore to the offspring of the house of Jacob, and made myself knon to them in the land of Egypt, hen I sore to them, saying, ’ I am the LORD your God;’
in that day I sore to them to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, floing ith milk and honey, hich is the glory of all lands.
I said to them, ’Each of you thro aay the abominations of his eyes. Don’t defile yourselves ith the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’

“’“ But they rebelled against me and ouldn’t listen to me. They didn’t all thro aay the abominations of their eyes. They also didn’t forsake the idols of Egypt. Then I said I ould pour out my rath on them, to accomplish my anger against them in the middle of the land of Egypt.
But I orked for my name’s sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations among hich they ere, in hose sight I made myself knon to them in bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
So I caused them to go out of the land of Egypt and brought them into the ilderness.
I gave them my statutes and shoed them my ordinances, hich if a man does, he ill live in them.
Moreover also I gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign beteen me and them, that they might kno that I am the LORD ho sanctifies them.

“’“ But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the ilderness. They didn’t alk in my statutes and they rejected my ordinances, hich if a man keeps, he shall live in them. They greatly profaned my Sabbaths. Then I said I ould pour out my rath on them in the ilderness, to consume them.
But I orked for my name’s sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, in hose sight I brought them out.
Moreover also I sore to them in the ilderness that I ould not bring them into the land hich I had given them, floing ith milk and honey, hich is the glory of all lands,
because they rejected my ordinances, and didn’t alk in my statutes, and profaned my Sabbaths; for their heart ent after their idols.
Nevertheless my eye spared them, and I didn’t destroy them. I didn’t make a full end of them in the ilderness.
I said to their children in the ilderness, ’Don’t alk in the statutes of your fathers. Don’t observe their ordinances or defile yourselves ith their idols.
I am the LORD your God. Walk in my statutes, keep my ordinances, and do them.
Make my Sabbaths holy. They shall be a sign beteen me and you, that you may kno that I am the LORD your God.’

“’“ But the children rebelled against me. They didn’t alk in my statutes, and didn’t keep my ordinances to do them, hich if a man does, he shall live in them. They profaned my Sabbaths. Then I said I ould pour out my rath on them, to accomplish my anger against them in the ilderness.
Nevertheless I ithdre my hand and orked for my name’s sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, in hose sight I brought them out.
Moreover I sore to them in the ilderness, that I ould scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries,
because they had not executed my ordinances, but had rejected my statutes, and had profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes ere after their fathers’ idols.
Moreover also I gave them statutes that ere not good, and ordinances in hich they couldn’t live.
I polluted them in their on gifts, in that they caused all that opens the omb to pass through the fire, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might kno that I am the LORD.”’
“ Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel, and tell them, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ Moreover, in this your fathers have blasphemed me, in that they have committed a trespass against me.

For hen I had brought them into the land hich I sore to give to them, then they sa every high hill and every thick tree, and they offered there their sacrifices, and there they presented the provocation of their offering. There they also made their pleasant aroma, and there they poured out their drink offerings.
Then I said to them, ’ What does the high place here you go mean?’ So its name is called Bamah to this day.”’
“ Therefore tell the house of Israel, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ Do you pollute yourselves in the ay of your fathers? Do you play the prostitute after their abominations?

When you offer your gifts, hen you make your sons pass through the fire, do you pollute yourselves ith all your idols to this day? Should I be inquired of by you, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord GOD, I ill not be inquired of by you!
“’“ That hich comes into your mind ill not be at all, in that you say, ’We ill be as the nations, as the families of the countries, to serve ood and stone.’
As I live,” says the Lord GOD, “ surely ith a mighty hand, ith an outstretched arm, and ith rath poured out, I ill be king over you.
I ill bring you out from the peoples, and ill gather you out of the countries in hich you are scattered ith a mighty hand, ith an outstretched arm, and ith rath poured out.
I ill bring you into the ilderness of the peoples, and there I ill enter into judgment ith you face to face.
Just as I entered into judgment ith your fathers in the ilderness of the land of Egypt, so I ill enter into judgment ith you,” says the Lord GOD.
“ I ill cause you to pass under the rod, and I ill bring you into the bond of the covenant.

I ill purge out from among you the rebels and those ho disobey me. I ill bring them out of the land here they live, but they shall not enter into the land of Israel. Then you ill kno that I am the LORD.”

“’ As for you, house of Israel, the Lord GOD says: “ Go, everyone serve his idols, and hereafter also, if you ill not listen to me; but you shall no more profane my holy name ith your gifts and ith your idols.

For in my holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel,” says the Lord GOD, “ there all the house of Israel, all of them, shall serve me in the land. There I ill accept them, and there I ill require your offerings and the first fruits of your offerings, ith all your holy things.
I ill accept you as a pleasant aroma hen I bring you out from the peoples and gather you out of the countries in hich you have been scattered. I ill be sanctified in you in the sight of the nations.
You ill kno that I am the LORD hen I bring you into the land of Israel, into the country hich I sore to give to your fathers.
There you ill remember your ays, and all your deeds in hich you have polluted yourselves. Then you ill loathe yourselves in your on sight for all your evils that you have committed.
You ill kno that I am the LORD, hen I have dealt ith you for my name’s sake, not according to your evil ays, nor according to your corrupt doings, you house of Israel,” says the Lord GOD.’”
The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face toard the south, and preach toard the south, and prophesy against the forest of the field in the south.

Tell the forest of the south, ’Hear the LORD’s ord: The Lord GOD says, “Behold, I ill kindle a fire in you, and it ill devour every green tree in you, and every dry tree. The burning flame ill not be quenched, and all faces from the south to the north ill be burned by it.
All flesh ill see that I, the LORD, have kindled it. It ill not be quenched.”’”
Then I said, “Ah Lord GOD! They say of me, ’Isn’t he a speaker of parables?’”
The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, set your face toard Jerusalem, and preach toard the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
Tell the land of Israel, ’ The LORD says: “ Behold, I am against you, and ill dra my sord out of its sheath, and ill cut off from you the righteous and the icked.
Seeing then that I ill cut off from you the righteous and the icked, therefore my sord ill go out of its sheath against all flesh from the south to the north.
All flesh ill kno that I, the LORD, have dran my sord out of its sheath. It ill not return any more.”’
“ Therefore sigh, you son of man. You shall sigh before their eyes ith a broken heart and ith bitterness.

It shall be, hen they ask you, ’Why do you sigh?’ that you shall say, ’ Because of the nes, for it comes! Every heart ill melt, all hands ill be feeble, every spirit ill faint, and all knees ill be eak as ater. Behold, it comes, and it shall be done, says the Lord GOD.’”
The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“Son of man, prophesy, and say, ’ The LORD says: “ A sord! A sord! It is sharpened, and also polished.
It is sharpened that it may make a slaughter. It is polished that it may be as lightning. Should e then make mirth? The rod of my son condemns every tree.
It is given to be polished, that it may be handled. The sord is sharpened. Yes, it is polished to give it into the hand of the killer.”’
Cry and ail, son of man; for it is on my people. It is on all the princes of Israel. They are delivered over to the sord ith my people. Therefore beat your thigh. \b
“ For there is a trial. What if even the rod that condemns ill be no more?” says the Lord GOD.

“ You therefore, son of man, prophesy, and strike your hands together. Let the sord be doubled the third time, the sord of the fatally ounded. It is the sord of the great one ho is fatally ounded, hich enters into their rooms.
I have set the threatening sord against all their gates, that their heart may melt, and their stumblings be multiplied. Ah! It is made as lightning. It is pointed for slaughter.
Gather yourselves together. Go to the right. Set yourselves in array. Go to the left, herever your face is set.
I ill also strike my hands together, and I ill cause my rath to rest. I, the LORD, have spoken it.”
The LORD’s ord came to me again, saying,
“ Also, you son of man, appoint to ays, that the sord of the king of Babylon may come. They both ill come out of one land, and mark out a place. Mark it out at the head of the ay to the city.
You shall appoint a ay for the sord to come to Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and to Judah in Jerusalem the fortified.
For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the ay, at the head of the to ays, to use divination. He shook the arros back and forth. He consulted the teraphim. He looked in the liver.

In his right hand as the lot for Jerusalem, to set battering rams, to open the mouth in the slaughter, to lift up the voice ith shouting, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast up mounds, and to build forts.
It ill be to them as a false divination in their sight, ho have sorn oaths to them; but he brings iniquity to memory, that they may be taken.

“Therefore the Lord GOD says: ’ Because you have caused your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that in all your doings your sins appear; because you have come to memory, you ill be taken ith the hand.
“’ You, deadly ounded icked one, the prince of Israel, hose day has come, in the time of the iniquity of the end,
the Lord GOD says: “Remove the turban, and take off the cron. This ill not be as it as. Exalt that hich is lo, and humble that hich is high.
I ill overturn, overturn, overturn it. This also ill be no more, until he comes hose right it is; and I ill give it.”’

“ You, son of man, prophesy and say, ’ The Lord GOD says this concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach: “ A sord! A sord is dran! It is polished for the slaughter, to cause it to devour, that it may be as lightning;
hile they see for you false visions, hile they divine lies to you, to lay you on the necks of the icked ho are deadly ounded, hose day has come in the time of the iniquity of the end.
Cause it to return into its sheath. In the place here you ere created, in the land of your birth, I ill judge you.
I ill pour out my indignation on you. I ill blo on you ith the fire of my rath. I ill deliver you into the hand of brutish men, skillful to destroy.
You ill be for fuel to the fire. Your blood ill be in the middle of the land. You ill be remembered no more; for I, the LORD, have spoken it.”’”
Moreover the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ You, son of man, ill you judge? Will you judge the bloody city? Then cause her to kno all her abominations.
You shall say, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ A city that sheds blood ithin herself, that her time may come, and that makes idols against herself to defile her!

You have become guilty in your blood that you have shed, and are defiled in your idols hich you have made! You have caused your days to dra near, and have come to the end of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations, and a mocking to all the countries.
Those ho are near and those ho are far from you ill mock you, you infamous one, full of tumult.
“’“ Behold, the princes of Israel, everyone according to his poer, have been in you to shed blood.
In you have they treated father and mother ith contempt. Among you they have oppressed the foreigner. In you they have ronged the fatherless and the ido.
You have despised my holy things, and have profaned my Sabbaths.
Slanderous men have been in you to shed blood. In you they have eaten on the mountains. They have committed ledness among you.
In you have they uncovered their fathers’ nakedness. In you have they humbled her ho as unclean in her impurity.
One has committed abomination ith his neighbor’s ife, and another has ledly defiled his daughter-in-la. Another in you has humbled his sister, his father’s daughter.
In you have they taken bribes to shed blood. You have taken interest and increase, and you have greedily gained of your neighbors by oppression, and have forgotten me,” says the Lord GOD.
“’“ Behold, therefore I have struck my hand at your dishonest gain hich you have made, and at the blood hich has been shed ithin you.
Can your heart endure, or can your hands be strong, in the days that I ill deal ith you? I, the LORD, have spoken it, and ill do it.
I ill scatter you among the nations, and disperse you through the countries. I ill purge your filthiness out of you.
You ill be profaned in yourself in the sight of the nations. Then you ill kno that I am the LORD.”’”
The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All of them are bronze, tin, iron, and lead in the middle of the furnace. They are the dross of silver.
Therefore the Lord GOD says: ’ Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I ill gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.

As they gather silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into the middle of the furnace, to blo the fire on it, to melt it, so I ill gather you in my anger and in my rath, and I ill lay you there and melt you.
Yes, I ill gather you, and blo on you ith the fire of my rath, and you ill be melted in the middle of it.
As silver is melted in the middle of the furnace, so you ill be melted in the middle of it; and you ill kno that I, the LORD, have poured out my rath on you.’”
The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, tell her, ’ You are a land that is not cleansed nor rained on in the day of indignation.’
There is a conspiracy of her prophets ithin it, like a roaring lion ravening the prey. They have devoured souls. They take treasure and precious things. They have made many idos ithin it.

Her priests have done violence to my la and have profaned my holy things. They have made no distinction beteen the holy and the common, neither have they caused men to discern beteen the unclean and the clean, and have hidden their eyes from my Sabbaths. So I am profaned among them.
Her princes ithin it are like olves ravening the prey, to shed blood and to destroy souls, that they may get dishonest gain.
Her prophets have plastered for them ith hiteash, seeing false visions, and divining lies to them, saying, ’ The Lord GOD says,’ hen the LORD has not spoken.
The people of the land have used oppression and exercised robbery. Yes, they have troubled the poor and needy, and have oppressed the foreigner rongfully.
“ I sought for a man among them ho ould build up the all and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I ould not destroy it; but I found no one.
Therefore I have poured out my indignation on them. I have consumed them ith the fire of my rath. I have brought their on ay on their heads,” says the Lord GOD.
The LORD’s ord came again to me, saying,
“ Son of man, there ere to omen, the daughters of one mother.
They played the prostitute in Egypt. They played the prostitute in their youth. Their breasts ere fondled there, and their youthful nipples ere caressed there.
Their names ere Oholah the elder, and Oholibah her sister. They became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem Oholibah.
“Oholah played the prostitute hen she as mine. She doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbors,
ho ere clothed ith blue— governors and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.
She gave herself as a prostitute to them, all of them the choicest men of Assyria. She defiled herself ith the idols of homever she lusted after.
She hasn’t left her prostitution since leaving Egypt; for in her youth they lay ith her. They caressed her youthful nipples and they poured out their prostitution on her.
“ Therefore I delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians on hom she doted.
These uncovered her nakedness. They took her sons and her daughters, and they killed her ith the sord. She became a byord among omen; for they executed judgments on her.
“ Her sister Oholibah sa this, yet she as more corrupt in her lusting than she, and in her prostitution hich as more depraved than the prostitution of her sister.
She lusted after the Assyrians, governors and rulers— her neighbors, clothed most gorgeously, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.
I sa that she as defiled. They both ent the same ay.
“ She increased her prostitution; for she sa men portrayed on the all, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed ith red,
dressed ith belts on their aists, ith floing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like princes, after the likeness of the Babylonians in Chaldea, the land of their birth.
As soon as she sa them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them into Chaldea.
The Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her ith their prostitution. She as polluted ith them, and her soul as alienated from them.
So she uncovered her prostitution and uncovered her nakedness. Then my soul as alienated from her, just like my soul as alienated from her sister.
Yet she multiplied her prostitution, remembering the days of her youth, in hich she had played the prostitute in the land of Egypt.
She lusted after their lovers, hose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys, and hose issue is like the issue of horses.
Thus you called to memory the ledness of your youth, in the caressing of your nipples by the Egyptians because of your youthful breasts.
“ Therefore, Oholibah, the Lord GOD says: ’ Behold, I ill raise up your lovers against you, from hom your soul is alienated, and I ill bring them against you on every side:
the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, Koa, and all the Assyrians ith them; all of them desirable young men, governors and rulers, princes and men of renon, all of them riding on horses.

They ill come against you ith eapons, chariots, and agons, and ith a company of peoples. They ill set themselves against you ith buckler, shield, and helmet all around. I ill commit the judgment to them, and they ill judge you according to their judgments.

I ill set my jealousy against you, and they ill deal ith you in fury. They ill take aay your nose and your ears. Your remnant ill fall by the sord. They ill take your sons and your daughters; and the rest of you ill be devoured by the fire.
They ill also strip you of your clothes and take aay your beautiful jeels.
Thus I ill make your ledness to cease from you, and remove your prostitution from the land of Egypt, so that you ill not lift up your eyes to them, nor remember Egypt any more.’
“ For the Lord GOD says: ’ Behold, I ill deliver you into the hand of them hom you hate, into the hand of them from hom your soul is alienated.
They ill deal ith you in hatred, and ill take aay all your labor, and ill leave you naked and bare. The nakedness of your prostitution ill be uncovered, both your ledness and your prostitution.
These things ill be done to you because you have played the prostitute after the nations, and because you are polluted ith their idols.
You have alked in the ay of your sister; therefore I ill give her cup into your hand.’
“ The Lord GOD says: ’ You ill drink of your sister’s cup, hich is deep and large. You ill be ridiculed and held in derision. It contains much.
You ill be filled ith drunkenness and sorro, ith the cup of astonishment and desolation, ith the cup of your sister Samaria.
You ill even drink it and drain it out. You ill gna the broken pieces of it, and ill tear your breasts;
“ Therefore the Lord GOD says: ’ Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, therefore you also bear your ledness and your prostitution.’”
The LORD said moreover to me: “ Son of man, ill you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations.

For they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands. They have committed adultery ith their idols. They have also caused their sons, hom they bore to me, to pass through the fire to them to be devoured.
Moreover this they have done to me: they have defiled my sanctuary in the same day, and have profaned my Sabbaths.
For hen they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same day into my sanctuary to profane it; and behold, they have done this in the middle of my house.
“ Furthermore you sisters have sent for men ho come from far aay, to hom a messenger as sent, and behold, they came; for hom you ashed yourself, painted your eyes, decorated yourself ith ornaments,
and sat on a stately bed, ith a table prepared before it, hereupon you set my incense and my oil.
“ The voice of a multitude being at ease as ith her. With men of the common sort ere brought drunkards from the ilderness; and they put bracelets on their hands, and beautiful crons on their heads.
Then I said of her ho as old in adulteries, ’ No they ill play the prostitute ith her, and she ith them.’
They ent in to her, as they go in to a prostitute. So they ent in to Oholah and to Oholibah, the led omen.
Righteous men ill judge them ith the judgment of adulteresses and ith the judgment of omen ho shed blood, because they are adulteresses, and blood is in their hands.
“ For the Lord GOD says: ’ I ill bring up a mob against them, and ill give them to be tossed back and forth and robbed.
The company ill stone them ith stones and dispatch them ith their sords. They ill kill their sons and their daughters, and burn up their houses ith fire.
“’ Thus I ill cause ledness to cease out of the land, that all omen may be taught not to be led like you.
They ill recompense your ledness on you, and you ill bear the sins of your idols. Then you ill kno that I am the Lord GOD.’”
Again, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, rite the name of the day, this same day. The king of Babylon dre close to Jerusalem this same day.
Utter a parable to the rebellious house, and tell them, ’ The Lord GOD says, “ Put the cauldron on the fire. Put it on, and also pour ater into it.
Gather its pieces into it, even every good piece: the thigh and the shoulder. Fill it ith the choice bones.
Take the choice of the flock, and also a pile of ood for the bones under the cauldron. Make it boil ell. Yes, let its bones be boiled ithin it.”
“’ Therefore the Lord GOD says: “Woe to the bloody city, to the cauldron hose rust is in it, and hose rust hasn’t gone out of it! Take out of it piece after piece ithout casting lots for it. \b
“’“ For the blood she shed is in the middle of her. She set it on the bare rock. She didn’t pour it on the ground, to cover it ith dust.
That it may cause rath to come up to take vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, that it should not be covered.”
“’ Therefore the Lord GOD says: “Woe to the bloody city! I also ill make the pile great.
Heap on the ood. Make the fire hot. Boil the meat ell. Make the broth thick, and let the bones be burned.
Then set it empty on its coals, that it may be hot, and its bronze may burn, and that its filthiness may be molten in it, that its rust may be consumed.
She is eary ith toil; yet her great rust, rust by fire, doesn’t leave her.
“’“ In your filthiness is ledness. Because I have cleansed you and you eren’t cleansed, you on’t be cleansed from your filthiness any more, until I have caused my rath toard you to rest.

“’“ I, the LORD, have spoken it. It ill happen, and I ill do it. I on’t go back. I on’t spare. I on’t repent. According to your ays and according to your doings, they ill judge you,” says the Lord GOD.’”
Also the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, behold, I ill take aay from you the desire of your eyes ith one stroke; yet you shall neither mourn nor eep, neither shall your tears run don.
Sigh, but not aloud. Make no mourning for the dead. Bind your headdress on you, and put your sandals on your feet. Don’t cover your lips, and don’t eat mourner’s bread.”
So I spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening my ife died. So I did in the morning as I as commanded.
The people asked me, “Won’t you tell us hat these things mean to us, that you act like this?”
Then I said to them, “ The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

’Speak to the house of Israel, “ The Lord GOD says: ’ Behold, I ill profane my sanctuary, the pride of your poer, the desire of your eyes, and that hich your soul pities; and your sons and your daughters hom you have left behind ill fall by the sord.

“ You, son of man, shouldn’t it be in the day hen I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and that hereupon they set their heart— their sons and their daughters—
that in that day he ho escapes ill come to you, to cause you to hear it ith your ears?

The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, set your face toard the children of Ammon, and prophesy against them.

“’ The Lord GOD says: “ Because Moab and Seir say, ’ Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations,’
therefore, behold, I ill open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities hich are on its frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim,

“’ The Lord GOD says: “ Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,”

In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

“ For the Lord GOD says: ’ Behold, I ill bring on Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north, ith horses, ith chariots, ith horsemen, and an army ith many people.

By reason of the abundance of his horses, their dust ill cover you. Your alls ill shake at the noise of the horsemen, of the agons, and of the chariots, hen he enters into your gates, as men enter into a city hich is broken open.
He ill tread don all your streets ith the hoofs of his horses. He ill kill your people ith the sord. The pillars of your strength ill go don to the ground.

They ill make a plunder of your riches and make a prey of your merchandise. They ill break don your alls and destroy your pleasant houses. They ill lay your stones, your timber, and your dust in the middle of the aters.

“ The Lord GOD says to Tyre: ’Won’t the islands shake at the sound of your fall, hen the ounded groan, hen the slaughter is made ithin you?

Then all the princes of the sea ill come don from their thrones, and lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They ill clothe themselves ith trembling. They ill sit on the ground, and ill tremble every moment, and be astonished at you.

“ For the Lord GOD says: ’ When I make you a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited, hen I bring up the deep on you, and the great aters cover you,

then I ill bring you don ith those ho descend into the pit, to the people of old time, and ill make you dell in the loer parts of the earth, in the places that are desolate of old, ith those ho go don to the pit, that you be not inhabited; and I ill set glory in the land of the living.
I ill make you a terror, and you ill no more have any being. Though you are sought for, yet you ill never be found again,’ says the Lord GOD.”
The LORD’s ord came again to me, saying,
“ You, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre;
and tell Tyre, ’ You ho dell at the entry of the sea, ho are the merchant of the peoples to many islands, the Lord GOD says: “ You, Tyre, have said, ’ I am perfect in beauty.’
Your borders are in the heart of the seas. Your builders have perfected your beauty.
They have made all your planks of cypress trees from Senir. They have taken a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.

Your sail as of fine linen ith embroidered ork from Egypt, that it might be to you for a banner. Blue and purple from the islands of Elishah as your aning.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad ere your roers. Your ise men, Tyre, ere in you. They ere your pilots.
The old men of Gebal and its ise men ere your repairers of ship seams in you. All the ships of the sea ith their mariners ere in you to deal in your merchandise. \b
“’“ Persia, Lud, and Put ere in your army, your men of ar. They hung the shield and helmet in you. They shoed your beauty.
The men of Arvad ith your army ere on your alls all around, and valiant men ere in your toers. They hung their shields on your alls all around. They have perfected your beauty.
“’“ Tarshish as your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches. They traded for your ares ith silver, iron, tin, and lead.
“’“ Javan, Tubal, and Meshech ere your traders. They traded the persons of men and vessels of bronze for your merchandise.
“’“ They of the house of Togarmah traded for your ares ith horses, ar horses, and mules.
“’“ The men of Dedan traded ith you. Many islands ere the market of your hand. They brought you horns of ivory and ebony in exchange.
“’“Syria as your merchant by reason of the multitude of your handiorks. They traded for your ares ith emeralds, purple, embroidered ork, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
