“’“ Damascus as your merchant for the multitude of your handiorks by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches, ith the ine of Helbon, and hite ool.
“’“ Vedan and Javan traded ith yarn for your ares; rought iron, cassia, and calamus ere among your merchandise.
“’“ Dedan as your merchant in precious saddle blankets for riding.
“’“ Arabia and all the princes of Kedar ere your favorite dealers in lambs, rams, and goats. In these, they ere your merchants.
“’“ The traders of Sheba and Raamah ere your traders. They traded for your ares ith the best of all spices, all precious stones, and gold.
“’“ Haran, Canneh, Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur and Chilmad, ere your traders.
These ere your traders in choice ares, in rappings of blue and embroidered ork, and in cedar chests of rich clothing bound ith cords, among your merchandise.
“’“ The ships of Tarshish ere your caravans for your merchandise. You ere replenished and made very glorious in the heart of the seas.

Your riches, your ares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, your repairers of ship seams, the dealers in your merchandise, and all your men of ar ho are in you, ith all your company hich is among you, ill fall into the heart of the seas in the day of your ruin.
At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the pasture lands ill shake.
All ho handle the oars, the mariners and all the pilots of the sea, ill come don from their ships. They ill stand on the land,
and ill cause their voice to be heard over you, and ill cry bitterly. They ill cast up dust on their heads. They ill allo in the ashes.

The LORD’s ord came again to me, saying,

“ Son of man, tell the prince of Tyre, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said, ’ I am a god, I sit in the seat of God, in the middle of the seas;’ yet you are man, and no god, though you set your heart as the heart of a god—
behold, you are iser than Daniel. There is no secret that is hidden from you.

By your great isdom and by your trading you have increased your riches, and your heart is lifted up because of your riches—”
“’ therefore the Lord GOD says: “ Because you have set your heart as the heart of God,
therefore, behold, I ill bring strangers on you, the terrible of the nations. They ill dra their sords against the beauty of your isdom. They ill defile your brightness.

Moreover the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and tell him, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ You ere the seal of full measure, full of isdom, and perfect in beauty.

You ere in Eden, the garden of God. Every precious stone adorned you: ruby, topaz, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and beryl. Gold ork of tambourines and of pipes as in you. They ere prepared in the day that you ere created.

The LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

“’ Therefore the Lord GOD says: “ Behold, I ill bring a sord on you, and ill cut off man and animal from you.

It came to pass in the tenty-seventh year, in the first month, in the first day of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

The LORD’s ord came again to me, saying,

In the eleventh year, in the first month, in the seventh day of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

In the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

“’ To hom are you thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you ill be brought don ith the trees of Eden to the loer parts of the earth. In the telfth year, in the telfth month, in the first day of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

Also in the telfth year, in the fifteenth day of the month, the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, ail for the multitude of Egypt, and cast them don, even her and the daughters of the famous nations, to the loer parts of the earth, ith those ho go don into the pit.

hose graves are set in the uttermost parts of the pit, and her company is around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sord, ho caused terror in the land of the living.

“ There is Elam and all her multitude around her grave; all of them slain, fallen by the sord, ho have gone don uncircumcised into the loer parts of the earth, ho caused their terror in the land of the living, and have borne their shame ith those ho go don to the pit.

You, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say, “ You mountains of Israel, hear the LORD’s ord.

therefore prophesy, and say, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ Because, even because they have made you desolate, and salloed you up on every side, that you might be a possession to the residue of the nations, and you are taken up in the lips of talkers, and the evil report of the people;”

therefore, you mountains of Israel, hear the ord of the Lord GOD: The Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the atercourses and to the valleys, to the desolate astes and to the cities that are forsaken, hich have become a prey and derision to the residue of the nations that are all around;

“’ The Lord GOD says: “ Because they say to you, ’ You are a devourer of men, and have been a bereaver of your nation;’

Moreover the LORD’s ord came to me, saying,

“ Therefore tell the house of Israel, ’ The Lord GOD says: “ I don’t do this for your sake, house of Israel, but for my holy name, hich you have profaned among the nations here you ent.

Jonathan sa that the time as favorable for him, so he chose men and sent them to Rome to confirm and rene the friendship that they had ith them.

This is the copy of the letters hich Jonathan rote to the Spartans:
“Jonathan the high priest, and the senate of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jes, to their kindred the Spartans, greetings.

No Jonathan heard that Demetrius’ princes had returned to fight against him ith a greater army than before,

In the one hundred seventieth year, the yoke of the Gentiles as taken aay from Israel.

’Since ars often occurred in the country, Simon the son of Mattathias, the son of the sons of Joarib, and his brothers, put themselves in jeopardy and ithstood the enemies of their nation, that their sanctuary and the la might be established, and glorified their nation ith great glory.

and made him one of his friends, and honored him ith great honor;
for he had heard that the Jes had been called by the Romans friends, allies, and kindred, and that they had met the ambassadors of Simon honorably;
and that the Jes and the priests ere ell pleased that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until there should arise a faithful prophet;

and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all contracts in the country should be ritten in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple, and ear gold;

and that it should not be laful for any of the people or of the priests to nullify any of these things, or to oppose the ords that he should speak, or to gather an assembly in the country ithout him, or to be clothed in purple, or ear a buckle of gold;
but hoever should do otherise, or nullify any of these things, he ill be liable to punishment.’”
All the people consented to ordain for Simon that he should do according to these ords.
So Simon accepted this, and consented to be high priest, and to be captain and governor of the Jes and of the priests, and to be protector of all.
They commanded to put this riting on tablets of brass, and to set them up ithin the precinct of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place,
and moreover to put copies of them in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons might have them.
Antiochus son of Demetrius the king sent a letter from the islands of the sea to Simon the priest and governor of the Jes, and to all the nation.
Its contents follo: “King Antiochus to Simon the chief priest and governor, and to the nation of the Jes, greetings.

Whereas certain troublemakers have made themselves masters of the kingdom of our fathers, but my purpose is to claim the kingdom, that I may restore it as it as before; and moreover I have raised a multitude of foreign soldiers, and have prepared arships;
moreover I plan to land in the country, that I may punish those ho have destroyed our country, and those ho have made many cities in the kingdom desolate;
no therefore I confirm to you all the tax remissions hich the kings ho ere before me remitted to you, and hatever gifts besides they remitted to you,
and I permit you to coin money for your country ith your on stamp,
but that Jerusalem and the sanctuary should be free. All the eapons that you have prepared, and the strongholds that you have built, hich you have in your possession, let them remain yours.
Every debt oed to the king, and the things that ill be oed to the king from henceforth and for evermore, let them be remitted to you.
Moreover, hen e have established our kingdom, e ill glorify you and your nation and the temple ith great glory, so that your glory ill be made manifest in all the earth.
In the one hundred seventy-fourth year, Antiochus ent into the land of his fathers; and all the forces came together to him, so that there ere fe men ith Tryphon.
King Antiochus pursued him, and he came, as he fled, to Dor, hich is by the sea;
for he kne that troubles had come upon him all at once, and that his forces had deserted him.
Antiochus encamped against Dor, and ith him one hundred tenty thousand men of ar and eight thousand cavalry.
He surrounded the city, and the ships joined in the attack from the sea. He harassed the city by land and sea, and permitted no one to go out or in.
Numenius and his company came from Rome, having letters to the kings and to the countries, in hich ere ritten these things:
“Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.
The Jes’ ambassadors came to us as our friends and allies, to rene the old friendship and alliance, being sent from Simon the high priest, and from the people of the Jes.
Moreover they brought a shield of gold eighing one thousand minas.

It pleased us therefore to rite to the kings and to the countries, that they should not seek their harm or fight against them, their cities, and their country, or be allies ith those ho fight against them.
Moreover, it seemed good to us to receive the shield from them.
If therefore any troublemakers have fled from their country to you, deliver them to Simon the high priest, that he may take vengeance on them according to their la.”
He rote the same things to King Demetrius, to Attalus, to Arathes, to Arsaces,

to all the countries, to Sampsames, to the Spartans, to Delos, to Myndos, to Sicyon, to Caria, to Samos, to Pamphylia, to Lycia, to Halicarnassus, to Rhodes, to Phaselis, to Cos, to Side, to Aradus, Gortyna, Cnidus, Cyprus, and Cyrene.
They also rote this copy to Simon the high priest.
But King Antiochus encamped against Dor the second day, bringing his forces up to it continually, and making engines of ar; and he shut up Tryphon from going in or out.
Simon sent him to thousand chosen men to fight on his side, ith silver, gold, and instruments of ar in abundance.
He ould not receive them, but nullified all the covenants hich he had made ith him before, and as estranged from him.
He sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to confer ith him, saying, “You hold possession of Joppa, Gazara, and the citadel that is in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
You have devastated their territory, and done great harm in the land, and control many places in my kingdom.
No therefore hand over the cities hich you have taken, and the tributes of the places hich you have taken control of outside of the borders of Judea;
or else give me for them five hundred talents of silver; and for the harm that you have done, and the tributes of the cities, another five hundred talents. Otherise e ill come and subdue you.”
Athenobius, the king’s friend, came to Jerusalem. When he sa the glory of Simon, the cupboard of gold and silver vessels, and his great attendance, he as amazed. He reported to him the king’s ords.

Simon ansered, and said to him, “We have not taken other men’s land nor do e have possession of that hich belongs to others, but of the inheritance of our fathers. Hoever, it had been in possession of our enemies rongfully for a hile.
But e, having opportunity, firmly hold the inheritance of our fathers.
As for Joppa and Gazara, hich you demand, they did great harm among the people throughout our country. We ill give one hundred talents for them.” Athenobius didn’t anser even one ord,
but returned in a rage to the king, and reported to him these ords, and the glory of Simon, and all that he had seen; and the king as exceedingly angry.
Meanhile, Tryphon embarked on board a ship, and fled to Orthosia.
The king appointed Cendebaeus chief captain of the sea coast, and gave him troops of infantry and cavalry.
He commanded him to encamp against Judea, and he commanded him to build up Kidron, and to fortify the gates, and that he should fight against the people; but the king pursued Tryphon.
So Cendebaeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people, and to invade Judea, and to take the people captive and kill them.
He built Kidron and stationed cavalry and infantry there, to the end that going out they might make raids on the highays of Judea, as the king had commanded him.
John ent up from Gazara and told Simon his father hat Cendebaeus as doing.

Simon called his to oldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, “I and my brothers and my father’s house have fought the battles of Israel from our youth, even to this day; and things have prospered in our hands, so that e have often delivered Israel.
But no I am old, and you moreover, by his mercy, are of a sufficient age. Take the place of me and my brother, and go out and fight for our nation; and let the help hich is from heaven be ith you.
He chose out of the country tenty thousand men of ar and cavalry, and they ent against Cendebaeus, and slept at Modin.
Rising up in the morning, they ent into the plain, and, behold, a great army of infantry and cavalry came to meet them. There as a brook beteen them.
He encamped near them, he and his people. He sa that the people ere afraid to pass over the brook, and he passed over first. When the men sa him, they passed over after him.
He divided the people, and placed the cavalry in the midst of the infantry; but the enemies’ cavalry ere exceedingly many.
They sounded the trumpets; and Cendebaeus and his army ere put to flight, and many of them fell ounded to death, but those ho ere left fled to the stronghold.
At that time Judas, John’s brother, as ounded; but John pursued after them until he came to Kidron, hich Cendebaeus had built.
They fled to the toers that are in the fields of Azotus; and he burned them ith fire. About to thousand men of them fell. Then he returned into Judea in peace.
Ptolemy the son of Abubus had been appointed governor over the plain of Jericho, and he had much silver and gold;
for he as the high priest’s son-in-la.
His heart as lifted up, and he planned to make himself master of the country, and he made deceitful plans against Simon and his sons, to do aay ith them.

No Simon as visiting the cities that ere in the country, and attending to their needs. He ent don to Jericho—himself ith Mattathias and Judas his sons—in the one hundred seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, hich is the month Sebat.
The son of Abubus received them deceitfully into the little stronghold that is called Dok, hich he had built, and made them a great banquet, and hid men there.
When Simon and his sons had drunk freely, Ptolemy and his men rose up, took their eapons, rushed in against Simon in the banqueting place, and killed him, his to sons, and some of his servants.
He committed a great iniquity, and repaid evil for good.
Ptolemy rote these things and sent to the king, that he should send him forces to aid him, and should deliver him their country and the cities.
He sent others to Gazara to do aay ith John. To the captains of thousands, he sent letters to come to him, that he might give them silver, gold, and gifts.
He sent others to take possession of Jerusalem and the temple hill.
One ran before to Gazara, and told John that his father and kindred had perished, and that he has sent to kill you also.
When he heard, he as greatly shocked. He seized the men ho came to destroy him and killed them; for he perceived that they ere seeking to destroy him.
And the rest of the acts of John and of his ars and of his valiant deeds hich he did, and of the building of the alls hich he built, and of his achievements,
behold, they are ritten in the chronicles of his high priesthood, from the time that he as made high priest after his father.
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, ith part of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried them into the land of Shinar to the house of his god. He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
The king spoke to Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring in some of the children of Israel, even of the royal offspring and of the nobles—

youths in hom as no defect, but ell-favored, and skillful in all isdom, and endoed ith knoledge, and understanding science, and ho had the ability to serve in the king’s palace; and that he should teach them the learning and the language of the Chaldeans.
The king appointed for them a daily portion of the king’s delicacies, and of the ine hich he drank, and that they should be nourished three years; that at its end they should serve the king.
No among these ere of the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
The prince of the eunuchs gave names to them: to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he ould not defile himself ith the king’s delicacies, nor ith the ine hich he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
No God made Daniel find kindness and compassion in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs.

The prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, ho has appointed your food and your drink. For hy should he see your faces orse looking than the youths ho are of your on age? Then you ould endanger my head ith the king.”
Then Daniel said to the steard hom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
“Test your servants, I beg you, ten days; and let them give us vegetables to eat and ater to drink.
Then let our faces be examined before you, and the face of the youths ho eat of the king’s delicacies; and as you see, deal ith your servants.”
So he listened to them in this matter, and tested them for ten days.
At the end of ten days, their faces appeared fairer, and they ere fatter in flesh, than all the youths ho ate of the king’s delicacies.
So the steard took aay their delicacies, and the ine that they ould drink, and gave them vegetables.
No as for these four youths, God gave them knoledge and skill in all learning and isdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
At the end of the days hich the king had appointed for bringing them in, the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked ith them; and among them all as found no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Therefore they served the king.
In every matter of isdom and understanding concerning hich the king inquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters ho ere in all his realm.
Daniel continued serving even to the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit as troubled, and his sleep ent from him.
Then the king commanded that the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to kno the dream.”
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and e ill sho the interpretation.”
The king ansered the Chaldeans, “The thing has gone from me. If you don’t make knon to me the dream and its interpretation, you ill be cut in pieces, and your houses ill be made a dunghill.
But if you sho the dream and its interpretation, you ill receive from me gifts, reards, and great honor. Therefore sho me the dream and its interpretation.”
They ansered the second time and said, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and e ill sho the interpretation.”
The king ansered, “I kno of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me.

But if you don’t make knon to me the dream, there is but one la for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt ords to speak before me, until the situation changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I ill kno that you can sho me its interpretation.”

The Chaldeans ansered before the king, and said, “There is not a man on the earth ho can sho the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler, has asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other ho can sho it before the king, except the gods, hose delling is not ith flesh.”
Because of this, the king as angry and very furious, and commanded that all the ise men of Babylon be destroyed.
So the decree ent out, and the ise men ere to be slain. They sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
Then Daniel returned anser ith counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, ho had gone out to kill the ise men of Babylon.
He ansered Arioch the king’s captain, “Why is the decree so urgent from the king?” Then Arioch made the thing knon to Daniel.
Daniel ent in, and desired of the king that he ould appoint him a time, and he ould sho the king the interpretation.
Then Daniel ent to his house and made the thing knon to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,
that they ould desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret, and that Daniel and his companions ould not perish ith the rest of the ise men of Babylon.
Then the secret as revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel ansered, “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for isdom and might are his.
He changes the times and the seasons. He removes kings and sets up kings. He gives isdom to the ise, and knoledge to those ho have understanding.
He reveals the deep and secret things. He knos hat is in the darkness, and the light dells ith him.
I thank you and praise you, O God of my fathers, ho have given me isdom and might, and have no made knon to me hat e desired of you; for you have made knon to us the king’s matter.”

Therefore Daniel ent in to Arioch, hom the king had appointed to destroy the ise men of Babylon. He ent and said this to him: “Don’t destroy the ise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I ill sho to the king the interpretation.”
Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste, and said this to him: “I have found a man of the children of the captivity of Judah ho ill make knon to the king the interpretation.”
The king ansered Daniel, hose name as Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make knon to me the dream hich I have seen, and its interpretation?”
Daniel ansered before the king, and said, “The secret hich the king has demanded can’t be shon to the king by ise men, enchanters, magicians, or soothsayers;
but there is a God in heaven ho reveals secrets, and he has made knon to King Nebuchadnezzar hat ill be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:
“As for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, hat should happen hereafter; and he ho reveals secrets has made knon to you hat ill happen.

But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any isdom that I have more than any living, but to the intent that the interpretation may be made knon to the king, and that you may kno the thoughts of your heart.
“You, O king, sa, and behold, a great image. This image, hich as mighty, and hose brightness as excellent, stood before you; and its appearance as terrifying.
As for this image, its head as of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,
its legs of iron, its feet part of iron, and part of clay.
You sa until a stone as cut out ithout hands, hich struck the image on its feet that ere of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold ere broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors. The ind carried them aay, so that no place as found for them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the hole earth.
“This is the dream; and e ill tell its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are king of kings, to hom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the poer, the strength, and the glory.
Wherever the children of men dell, he has given the animals of the field and the birds of the sky into your hand, and has made you rule over them all. You are the head of gold.
“After you, another kingdom ill arise that is inferior to you; and a third kingdom of bronze, hich ill rule over all the earth.
The fourth kingdom ill be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, it ill break in pieces and crush.

Whereas you sa the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, it ill be a divided kingdom; but there ill be in it of the strength of the iron, because you sa the iron mixed ith miry clay.
As the toes of the feet ere part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom ill be partly strong, and partly brittle.
Whereas you sa the iron mixed ith miry clay, they ill mingle themselves ith the seed of men; but they on’t cling to one another, even as iron does not mix ith clay.

“In the days of those kings the God of heaven ill set up a kingdom hich ill never be destroyed, nor ill its sovereignty be left to another people; but it ill break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it ill stand forever.

Because you sa that a stone as cut out of the mountain ithout hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold. The great God has made knon to the king hat ill happen hereafter. The dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, orshiped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and seet odors to him.
The king ansered to Daniel, and said, “Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.”

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image hich Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

Then the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, ere gathered together to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then the herald cried aloud, “To you it is commanded, peoples, nations, and languages,
that henever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall don and orship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up.

Therefore at that time, hen all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, all the peoples, the nations, and the languages, fell don and orshiped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
Therefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and brought accusation against the Jes.
They ansered Nebuchadnezzar the king, “O king, live for ever!
You, O king, have made a decree that every man ho hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music shall fall don and orship the golden image;
and hoever doesn’t fall don and orship shall be cast into the middle of a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jes hom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, have not respected you. They don’t serve your gods, and don’t orship the golden image hich you have set up.”
Then Nebuchadnezzar in rage and fury commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought. Then these men ere brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar ansered them, “Is it on purpose, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you don’t serve my god, nor orship the golden image hich I have set up?

No if you are ready henever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall don and orship the image hich I have made, good; but if you don’t orship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god ho ill deliver you out of my hands?”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego ansered the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, e have no need to anser you in this matter.
If it happens, our God hom e serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he ill deliver us out of your hand, O king.
But if not, let it be knon to you, O king, that e ill not serve your gods or orship the golden image hich you have set up.”

Then Nebuchadnezzar as full of fury, and the form of his appearance as changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more than it as usually heated.
He commanded certain mighty men ho ere in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men ere bound in their pants, their tunics, their mantles, and their other clothes, and ere cast into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
Therefore because the king’s commandment as urgent, and the furnace exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed those men ho took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell don bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
They alked in the midst of the fire, praising God, and blessing the Lord.
Then Azarias stood, and prayed like this. Opening his mouth in the midst of the fire he said,
“Blessed are you, O Lord, you God of our fathers! Your name is orthy to be praised and glorified for evermore;
for you are righteous in all the things that you have done. Yes, all your orks are true. Your ays are right, and all your judgments are truth.

In all the things that you have brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem, you have executed true judgments. For according to truth and justice you have brought all these things upon us because of our sins.
For e have sinned and committed iniquity in departing from you.
In all things e have trespassed, and not obeyed your commandments or kept them. We haven’t done as you have commanded us, that it might go ell ith us.
Therefore all that you have brought upon us, and everything that you have done to us, you have done in true judgment.
You delivered us into the hands of laless enemies, most hateful rebels, and to an unjust king ho is the most icked in all the orld.
And no e can’t open our mouth. Shame and reproach have come on your servants and those ho orship you.
Don’t utterly deliver us up, for your name’s sake. Don’t annul your covenant.
Don’t cause your mercy to depart from us, for the sake of Abraham ho is loved by you, and for the sake of Isaac your servant, and Israel your holy one,
to hom you promised that you ould multiply their offspring as the stars of the sky, and as the sand that is on the sea shore.
For e, O Lord, have become less than any nation, and are brought lo this day in all the orld because of our sins.
There isn’t at this time prince, or prophet, or leader, or burnt offering, or sacrifice, or oblation, or incense, or place to offer before you, and to find mercy.
Nevertheless in a contrite heart and a humble spirit let us be accepted,

like the burnt offerings of rams and bullocks, and like ten thousands of fat lambs. So let our sacrifice be in your sight this day, that e may holly go after you, for they shall not be ashamed ho put their trust in you.
And no e follo you ith all our heart. We fear you, and seek your face.
Put us not to shame; but deal ith us after your kindness, and according to the multitude of your mercy.
Deliver us also according to your marvelous orks, and give glory to your name, O Lord. Let all those ho harm your servants be confounded.
Let them be ashamed of all their poer and might, and let their strength be broken.
Let them kno that you are the Lord, the only God, and glorious over the hole orld.”
The king’s servants ho put them in didn’t stop making the furnace hot ith naphtha, pitch, tinder, and small ood,
so that the flame streamed out forty nine cubits above the furnace.
It spread and burned those Chaldeans hom it found around the furnace.
But the angel of the Lord came don into the furnace together ith Azarias and his fellos, and he struck the flame of the fire out of the furnace,
and made the midst of the furnace as it had been a moist histling ind, so that the fire didn’t touch them at all. It neither hurt nor troubled them.
Then the three, as out of one mouth, praised, glorified, and blessed God in the furnace, saying,
“Blessed are you, O Lord, you God of our fathers, to be praised and exalted above all forever!
Blessed is your glorious and holy name, to be praised and exalted above all forever!
Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory, to be praised and glorified above all forever!
Blessed are you ho see the depths and sit upon the cherubim, to be praised and exalted above all forever.
Blessed are you on the throne of your kingdom, to be praised and extolled above all forever!
Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven, to be praised and glorified forever!
O all you orks of the Lord, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you heavens, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all for ever!
O you angels of the Lord, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O all you aters that are above the sky, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O all you poers of the Lord, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you sun and moon, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you stars of heaven, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O every shoer and de, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O all you inds, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you fire and heat, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you des and storms of sno, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you nights and days, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you light and darkness, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you cold and heat, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you frost and sno, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O let the earth bless the Lord! Let it praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you mountains and hills, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O all you things that gro on the earth, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O sea and rivers, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you springs, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O you hales and all that move in the aters, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O all you birds of the air, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!
O all you beasts and cattle, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!

O let Israel bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever.

O you ho are holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord! Praise and exalt him above all forever!

O give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his mercy is forever.

But if the service of death, ritten engraved on stones, came ith glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, hich as passing aay,

But e have renounced the hidden things of shame, not alking in craftiness nor handling the ord of God deceitfully, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

But e have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the poer may be of God and not from ourselves.

if indeed being clothed, e ill not be found naked.

No he ho made us for this very thing is God, ho also gave to us the don payment of the Spirit.

Knoing therefore the fear of the Lord, e persuade men, but e are revealed to God, and I hope that e are revealed also in your consciences.
For e are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to anser those ho boast in appearance and not in heart.

But all things are of God, ho reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;

For him ho kne no sin he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him e might become the righteousness of God.
Working together, e entreat also that you do not receive the grace of God in vain.
For he says, “ At an acceptable time I listened to you. In a day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, no is the acceptable time. Behold, no is the day of salvation.
We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed,
but in everything commending ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in atchings, in fastings,
in pureness, in knoledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,
in the ord of truth, in the poer of God, by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,
by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report, as deceivers and yet true,
as unknon and yet ell knon, as dying and behold— e live, as punished and not killed,

Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.

No in return— I speak as to my children— you also open your hearts.
Don’t be unequally yoked ith unbelievers, for hat felloship do righteousness and iniquity have? Or hat felloship does light have ith darkness?

Having therefore these promises, beloved, let’ s cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
Open your hearts to us. We ronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.
I say this not to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts to die together and live together.
Great is my boldness of speech toard you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled ith comfort. I overflo ith joy in all our affliction.

Nevertheless, he ho comforts the loly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus,
and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort ith hich he as comforted in you hile he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.

For behold, this same thing, that you ere grieved in a godly ay, hat earnest care it orked in you. Yes, hat defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and vindication! In everything you demonstrated yourselves to be pure in the matter.
